```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Helper: render interactive DT table (sortable, searchable)
render_dt <- function(df, caption = NULL, pageLength = 15, ...) {
  datatable(df, caption = caption, rownames = FALSE,
            options = list(pageLength = pageLength, scrollX = TRUE),
            ...)
}

# Helper: format a p-value for inline rendering. Avoids knitr's auto-LaTeX
# scientific notation (which produces "3.88^{-22}" artifacts in HTML).
format_p <- function(p, digits = 2) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 1e-3) {
    formatC(p, format = "e", digits = digits)
  } else {
    formatC(signif(p, digits + 1), format = "g")
  }
}

# Helper functions (adapted from 03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ct_to_label <- function(ct) tolower(gsub("_", "", ct))

comp_label <- function(comp) {
  switch(toupper(comp), C2 = "NMD", C4 = "Control", toupper(comp))
}

evt_types <- c("Alt_TSS", "Alt_TES", "A5SS", "A3SS", "SE",
               "Missing_Internal", "IR", "IR_diff",
               "Partial_IR_5", "Partial_IR_3")

compute_event_freq <- function(profiles) {
  n_pairs <- nrow(profiles)
  n_pir5 <- sum(sapply(profiles$detailed_events, function(de)
    any(de$event_type == "Partial_IR_5")))
  n_pir3 <- sum(sapply(profiles$detailed_events, function(de)
    any(de$event_type == "Partial_IR_3")))
  counts <- c(sum(profiles$tss_changed), sum(profiles$tes_changed),
              sum(profiles$n_a5ss > 0), sum(profiles$n_a3ss > 0),
              sum(profiles$n_se > 0), sum(profiles$n_missing_internal > 0),
              sum(profiles$n_ir > 0), sum(profiles$n_ir_diff > 0),
              n_pir5, n_pir3)
  data.frame(event_type = evt_types,
             n_pairs_with_event = counts,
             pct_of_pairs = round(100 * counts / n_pairs, 1))
}

compute_ptc_rates_row <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  coding_ids <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]
  p_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$profiles
  cod_c2 <- p_c2[p_c2$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                   p_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
  p_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$profiles
  cod_c4 <- p_c4[p_c4$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                   p_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
  if (nrow(cod_c2) == 0 || nrow(cod_c4) == 0) return(NULL)
  # Gene-match: restrict OR computation to genes appearing in both C2 and C4
  # coding pair sets so the 2x2 contingency is a within-gene comparison.
  shared_genes <- intersect(cod_c2$gene_id, cod_c4$gene_id)
  cod_c2 <- cod_c2[cod_c2$gene_id %in% shared_genes, ]
  cod_c4 <- cod_c4[cod_c4$gene_id %in% shared_genes, ]
  ptc_c2 <- sum(cod_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE])
  ptc_c4 <- sum(cod_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE])
  n_c2 <- nrow(cod_c2); n_c4 <- nrow(cod_c4)
  ft <- tryCatch({
    mat <- matrix(c(ptc_c2, n_c2 - ptc_c2, ptc_c4, n_c4 - ptc_c4), nrow = 2)
    fisher.test(mat)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    n_coding_pairs_NMD = n_c2,
    n_coding_pairs_Ctrl = n_c4,
    NMD_comp_ptc_n = ptc_c2,
    NMD_comp_ptc_pct = round(100 * ptc_c2 / n_c2, 1),
    Ctrl_comp_ptc_n = ptc_c4,
    Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct = round(100 * ptc_c4 / n_c4, 1),
    fisher_OR = if (!is.null(ft)) round(ft$estimate, 2) else NA_real_,
    p_value = if (!is.null(ft)) ft$p.value else NA_real_
  )
}

compute_frame_category_rows <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  fc_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$frame_comp
  fc_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$frame_comp
  if (is.null(fc_c2) || is.null(fc_c4)) return(NULL)
  ps_c2 <- fc_c2$pair_summary
  ps_c4 <- fc_c4$pair_summary
  cats <- c("same_start_in_frame", "same_start_frameshift",
            "diff_start_same_frame", "diff_start_diff_frame",
            "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift",
            "non_coding", "no_shared_cds")
  # Denominator: coding pairs only (exclude non_coding and no_shared_cds)
  n_coding_c2 <- sum(!ps_c2$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
  n_coding_c4 <- sum(!ps_c4$frame_category %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds"))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(cats, function(cat) {
    is_coding_cat <- !cat %in% c("non_coding", "no_shared_cds")
    data.frame(
      cell_type = ct,
      frame_category = cat,
      NMD_n = sum(ps_c2$frame_category == cat),
      NMD_pct = if (is_coding_cat) round(100 * sum(ps_c2$frame_category == cat) / n_coding_c2, 1) else NA_real_,
      Ctrl_n = sum(ps_c4$frame_category == cat),
      Ctrl_pct = if (is_coding_cat) round(100 * sum(ps_c4$frame_category == cat) / n_coding_c4, 1) else NA_real_
    )
  }))
}

compute_divergence_row <- function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(set_results) || !c4_key %in% names(set_results)) return(NULL)
  div_c2 <- set_results[[c2_key]]$divergence
  div_c4 <- set_results[[c4_key]]$divergence
  if (is.null(div_c2) || nrow(div_c2) == 0 || is.null(div_c4) || nrow(div_c4) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    NMD_n = nrow(div_c2),
    NMD_median_pct_shared = round(median(div_c2$pct_shared, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Ctrl_n = nrow(div_c4),
    Ctrl_median_pct_shared = round(median(div_c4$pct_shared, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
}
```

# 0. Data Loading and Gene-Matching

## Data Provenance Overview

The core NMD analyses in this report use **gene-matched isoform pair sets**. The
data pipeline is:

1. **01_prepare_data_mashr.R**: Loads the isocall count matrix
   (`nmd_isocall.count_matrix.txt`, 645,273 isoforms x 38 samples), excludes
   2 outlier samples (DO donor 029T: `Sample25_DO_029T_DMSO` and
   `Sample26_DO_029T_Smg1i`, identified as PCA outlier), applies TMM
   normalization and condition-stratified 5% isoform filtering, then classifies
   isoforms as NMD-sensitive (`nmd_responsive == TRUE` in mashr DIE results) or
   non-NMD (`adj.P.Val > 0.30`; threshold raised from 0.50 to restore the
   historical proportion of non-NMD isoforms after the 4-CT mashr refit
   tightened p-value distributions). The count matrix carries 36 samples across
   six cell types, but downstream classification, pair construction, and all
   results are restricted to the **4 non-ALI paper-scope cell types: AT, DD,
   FB, MV**. DD_ALI, DO_ALI, and DO are not used. Outputs:
   `expression_data.rds`, `nmd_classification.rds`,
   `sample_metadata.rds`, `gene_map.rds`.

2. **02_build_profiles_mashr.R**: Generates isoform pairs —
   **C4 (Control)**: top-two non-NMD isoforms by DMSO CPM per gene
   (`generatePairsExpression(..., method = "top_two")`);
   **C2 (NMD)**: same C4 reference paired with top NMD isoform by Smg1i CPM
   (via `identifyDominantIsoforms()` + `inner_join` on `gene_id`).
   Builds splicing choice profiles with `Isopair::buildProfiles()`.
   Outputs: `profiles_c{2,4}_*.rds`, `pairs_c{2,4}_*.rds`.

3. **03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd**: Applies **gene-matching** (restricts C2 and C4
   to genes with shared `(gene_id, reference_isoform_id)` in both sets), then
   runs Isopair analysis functions on the matched profiles. Caches results to
   `analysis_cache/`.

4. **This report (05)**: Loads profiles from step 2, re-applies gene-matching
   (step 3), loads cached analysis results, and verifies consistency. All
   most downstream analyses use gene-matched profiles exclusively.


```{r load-data}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 1: Load raw data objects
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Publication Report Methods > NMD Classification (mashr)"
# ==============================================================================

# ── 01_prepare_data_mashr.R outputs ──
# Source: isocall count matrix → TMM normalization → 5% filter → mashr NMD classification
data_dir  <- "data_mashr"
cache_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "analysis_cache")

expr_mat    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "expression_data.rds"))
sample_meta <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "sample_metadata.rds"))
gene_map    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "gene_map.rds"))
nmd_class   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "nmd_classification.rds"))

# ── Infrastructure objects (isoform-intrinsic, DE-independent) ──
# Originally from Isopair pipeline scripts 02-05, copied to data_mashr/ by
# 02_build_profiles_mashr.R for self-containment.
# structures.rds: extractIsoformStructures() — exon coordinates per isoform
# cds.rds: extractCds() — CDS boundaries per isoform
# ptc.rds: testPtcAssociation() infrastructure — PTC status per isoform
# union_exons.rds: buildUnionExons() — merged exon models per gene
# isoform_union_mapping.rds: mapIsoformsToUnion() — isoform-to-union-exon mapping
# annotated_ue.rds: annotateUnionExons() — union exons with CDS/UTR labels
# cds_exons.rds: CDS mapped to individual exons
structures   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "structures.rds"))
cds          <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "cds.rds"))
ptc          <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "ptc.rds"))
union_exons  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "union_exons.rds"))
ue_mapping   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "isoform_union_mapping.rds"))
annotated_ue <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "annotated_ue.rds"))
cds_exons    <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "cds_exons.rds"))

# ── Prediction model objects (used in Sections 4 and 6) ──
unified <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "unified_model.rds"))
feat_labels <- unified$feature_labels
mc <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "model_comparison.rds"))

# ── CDS lookup vectors (used throughout the report) ──
# Build once from cds.rds via build_cds_lookups() (analysis_functions.R)
cds_lookups <- build_cds_lookups(cds)
coding_ids       <- cds_lookups$coding_ids
cds_start_lookup <- cds_lookups$cds_start_lookup
cds_stop_lookup  <- cds_lookups$cds_stop_lookup
strand_lookup    <- cds_lookups$strand_lookup

# ── Gene symbol lookup from mashr DE files ──
de_dir_mashr <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/isocall_dge/mashr"
gene_symbol_lookup <- character(0)
for (de_f in list.files(de_dir_mashr, pattern = "^nmd_mashr_die_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)) {
  de_tmp <- read.csv(de_f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c("gene_id", "hgnc_symbol")]
  de_tmp <- de_tmp[!duplicated(de_tmp$gene_id) & !is.na(de_tmp$hgnc_symbol) &
                    de_tmp$hgnc_symbol != "", ]
  new_entries <- setdiff(de_tmp$gene_id, names(gene_symbol_lookup))
  gene_symbol_lookup[de_tmp$gene_id[de_tmp$gene_id %in% new_entries]] <-
    de_tmp$hgnc_symbol[de_tmp$gene_id %in% new_entries]
}

get_gene_sym <- function(gid) {
  sym <- gene_symbol_lookup[gid]
  if (is.na(sym) || sym == "") gid else sym
}

# Cell types — paper scope (2026-04-29): 4 non-ALI cell types
cell_types  <- c("all_samples", "AT", "DD", "FB", "MV")
comparisons <- c("c2", "c4")
main_cts    <- c("AT", "DD", "FB", "MV")
```

```{r load-profiles}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 2: Load profiles and apply gene-matching
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Publication Report Methods > Pair Construction and Gene-Matching"
# ==============================================================================
#
# profiles_c{2,4}_*.rds are the output of 02_build_profiles_mashr.R. C2 pairs
# share their reference isoform with C4 (by construction in script 02), but C4
# may contain genes that have no NMD isoform (i.e., genes with >=2 non-NMD
# isoforms but no mashr-classified NMD isoform). Gene-matching restricts both
# sets to the intersection of (gene_id, reference_isoform_id), ensuring fair
# NMD vs Control comparison on identical gene sets.

profiles_list <- list()
for (ct in cell_types) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  for (comp in comparisons) {
    key <- paste(comp, ct_label, sep = "_")
    prof_file <- file.path(data_dir, sprintf("profiles_%s.rds", key))
    if (file.exists(prof_file)) profiles_list[[key]] <- readRDS(prof_file)
  }
}

# ── Gene-matching ──
# Replicates the logic from 03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd (gene-matching step).
# For each cell type, restrict C2 and C4 profiles to genes where both have
# a pair with the same (gene_id, reference_isoform_id).
gene_match_summary <- list()
for (ct in cell_types) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  if (!c2_key %in% names(profiles_list) || !c4_key %in% names(profiles_list)) next

  n_c2_before <- nrow(profiles_list[[c2_key]])
  n_c4_before <- nrow(profiles_list[[c4_key]])

  c2_gene_refs <- unique(profiles_list[[c2_key]][, c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id")])
  c4_gene_refs <- unique(profiles_list[[c4_key]][, c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id")])
  shared_refs  <- dplyr::inner_join(c2_gene_refs, c4_gene_refs,
                                     by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))

  profiles_list[[c2_key]] <- dplyr::semi_join(profiles_list[[c2_key]], shared_refs,
                                               by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))
  profiles_list[[c4_key]] <- dplyr::semi_join(profiles_list[[c4_key]], shared_refs,
                                               by = c("gene_id", "reference_isoform_id"))

  gene_match_summary[[ct]] <- data.frame(
    cell_type      = ct,
    c2_before      = n_c2_before,
    c4_before      = n_c4_before,
    matched_genes  = nrow(shared_refs),
    c2_after       = nrow(profiles_list[[c2_key]]),
    c4_after       = nrow(profiles_list[[c4_key]])
  )
}
gene_match_df <- do.call(rbind, gene_match_summary)
```

```{r build-set-results}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 3: Build set_results from gene-matched profiles + cached analyses
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Reading Frame and PTC Analysis"
# ==============================================================================
#
# set_results[[key]] is the primary data structure for all downstream analyses.
# $profiles: gene-matched splicing choice profiles (from STAGE 2 above)
# $divergence: quantifyPairDivergence() output (cached by script 03)
# $frame_comp: compareIsoformFrames() output (cached by script 03)
# $frame_walk: analyzeFrameWalk() output (cached by script 03)
# $ptc_assoc: testPtcAssociation() output (cached by script 03)
# $evt_freq: computed here from gene-matched profiles

set_results <- list()
for (key in names(profiles_list)) {
  profiles <- profiles_list[[key]]
  set_results[[key]] <- list(
    profiles   = profiles,
    divergence = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("div_", key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    frame_comp = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("fc_",  key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    frame_walk = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("fw_",  key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    ptc_assoc  = tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("ptc_", key, ".rds"))), error = function(e) NULL),
    evt_freq   = compute_event_freq(profiles)
  )
}

# Load divergence for all_samples (used by multiple sections)
div_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
div_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence
```

```{r verify-cache-consistency, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# STAGE 4: Verify cached analysis objects match gene-matched profiles
# ==============================================================================
#
# The cached div/fc/fw/ptc objects were computed by script 03 from gene-matched
# profiles. We verify that the row counts in the cached objects match our
# gene-matched profiles_list. A mismatch would indicate the cache is stale or
# was computed from a different pair set.

verification_rows <- list()
for (key in names(set_results)) {
  sr <- set_results[[key]]
  n_profiles <- nrow(sr$profiles)

  # divergence: 1 row per pair (should exactly match profiles)
  n_div <- if (!is.null(sr$divergence)) nrow(sr$divergence) else NA
  # frame_comp$pair_summary: 1 row per pair (should exactly match)
  n_fc <- if (!is.null(sr$frame_comp)) nrow(sr$frame_comp$pair_summary) else NA
  # frame_walk$profile_summary: 1 row per pair (should exactly match)
  n_fw <- if (!is.null(sr$frame_walk)) nrow(sr$frame_walk$profile_summary) else NA
  # ptc_assoc$pair_summary: 1 row per pair where PTC analysis was possible
  #   (both isoforms coding with EJC data). Expected to be <= n_profiles.
  n_ptc <- if (!is.null(sr$ptc_assoc)) nrow(sr$ptc_assoc$pair_summary) else NA

  # Exact match expected for div, fc, fw
  div_ok <- is.na(n_div) || n_div == n_profiles
  fc_ok  <- is.na(n_fc)  || n_fc  == n_profiles
  fw_ok  <- is.na(n_fw)  || n_fw  == n_profiles
  # ptc: subset is OK (non-coding pairs excluded), but should not exceed profiles
  ptc_ok <- is.na(n_ptc) || n_ptc <= n_profiles

  verification_rows[[key]] <- data.frame(
    key = key, n_profiles = n_profiles,
    n_div = n_div, n_fc = n_fc, n_fw = n_fw, n_ptc = n_ptc,
    exact_match = div_ok & fc_ok & fw_ok,
    ptc_subset_ok = ptc_ok
  )
}
verification_df <- do.call(rbind, verification_rows)

if (!all(verification_df$exact_match)) {
  warning("CACHE MISMATCH DETECTED — div/fc/fw row counts do not match ",
          "gene-matched profiles. Affected keys: ",
          paste(verification_df$key[!verification_df$exact_match], collapse = ", "))
}
if (!all(verification_df$ptc_subset_ok)) {
  warning("PTC CACHE ANOMALY — ptc_assoc has MORE rows than profiles for: ",
          paste(verification_df$key[!verification_df$ptc_subset_ok], collapse = ", "))
}
```

and C4 (Control) profile sets prior to gene-matching; **n_after_c2 /

pair count loaded for this key (from STAGE 2); **n_div / n_fc / n_fw /
n_ptc** = row counts in the cached `div_*`, `fc_*$pair_summary`,

**exact_match** = TRUE when div / fc / fw row counts equal n_profiles
(invariant: these are 1-row-per-pair); **ptc_subset_ok** = TRUE when
n_ptc ≤ n_profiles (PTC analysis subsets to coding pairs only, so this
should always be smaller).

# Event Type Glossary {.tabset}

Isopair identifies structural differences between pairs of isoforms from the
same gene by comparing their exon structures against a shared union exon
coordinate system. Each detected splice event is validated through reference
isoform reconstruction: the comparator's exon structure plus the detected
events must exactly reconstruct the reference isoform's exon structure,
ensuring that the event set is complete and self-consistent. The sections
below define all 12 splice event types recognized by Isopair, organized into
4 categories.

In all diagrams, the **Reference** (top) is the dominant non-NMD isoform and
the **Comparator** (bottom) is the isoform being compared. Events are always
described from the comparator's perspective: a **GAIN** means the comparator
has additional sequence relative to the reference, and a **LOSS** means the
comparator is missing sequence present in the reference.

```{r glossary-helper, include=FALSE}
glossary_plot <- function(ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, title, subtitle,
                          ref_cds = NULL, comp_cds = NULL, events = NULL) {
  plot_ucsc_pair(ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, strand = "+",
                 ref_cds = ref_cds, comp_cds = comp_cds,
                 ref_label = "Reference", comp_label = "Comparator",
                 events = events, title = title, subtitle = subtitle)
}
```

## Alt_TSS

**Alternative Transcription Start Site.** The two isoforms begin at different
genomic positions. Detected when the 5'-most exon of one isoform does not
overlap the 5'-most exon of the other. Direction: GAIN if the comparator's
TSS is further upstream (extending the transcript); LOSS if it is further
downstream (truncating it).

```{r glossary-alt-tss, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(250, 400, 700), comp_e = c(350, 550, 850),
  title = "Alt_TSS: Alternative Transcription Start Site",
  subtitle = "Comparator starts at a different position (here, downstream = LOSS)")
```

## Alt_TES

**Alternative Transcription End Site.** The two isoforms end at different
genomic positions. Detected when the 3'-most exon of one isoform does not
overlap the 3'-most exon of the other. Direction: GAIN if the comparator
extends further; LOSS if it ends earlier.

```{r glossary-alt-tes, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 900),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 550, 800),
  title = "Alt_TES: Alternative Transcription End Site",
  subtitle = "Comparator ends earlier (LOSS)")
```

## A5SS

**Alternative 5' Splice Site.** An internal exon has a different **donor**
(exon_end on + strand) boundary while sharing the same **acceptor**
(exon_start) boundary. The exon is extended or truncated at its
downstream/3' end. Direction: GAIN if the comparator's exon is longer;
LOSS if shorter.

```{r glossary-a5ss, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 600, 850),
  title = "A5SS: Alternative 5' Splice Site",
  subtitle = "Same acceptor (start), different donor (end). Comparator exon extends further (GAIN)")
```

## A3SS

**Alternative 3' Splice Site.** An internal exon has a different **acceptor**
(exon_start on + strand) boundary while sharing the same **donor** (exon_end)
boundary. The exon is extended or truncated at its upstream/5' end.
Direction: GAIN if the comparator's exon is longer; LOSS if shorter.

```{r glossary-a3ss, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 350, 700), comp_e = c(200, 550, 850),
  title = "A3SS: Alternative 3' Splice Site",
  subtitle = "Same donor (end), different acceptor (start). Comparator exon extends further (GAIN)")
```

## Partial_IR_5

**Partial Intron Retention (5' end).** An intron is partially retained: one
isoform's exon extends into the intron from its 5' side, covering what is
intronic sequence in the other isoform. The 3' boundary of the retaining
exon falls within the intron. Direction: GAIN if the comparator retains;
LOSS if the reference retains.

```{r glossary-pir5, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 700), comp_e = c(200, 620, 850),
  title = "Partial_IR_5: Partial Intron Retention (5' side)",
  subtitle = "Comparator exon extends into the intron from the 5' end (GAIN)")
```

## Partial_IR_3

**Partial Intron Retention (3' end).** An intron is partially retained: one
isoform's exon extends into the intron from its 3' side, covering what is
intronic sequence in the other isoform. The 5' boundary of the retaining
exon falls within the intron. Direction: GAIN if the comparator retains;
LOSS if the reference retains.

```{r glossary-pir3, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 640), comp_e = c(200, 550, 850),
  title = "Partial_IR_3: Partial Intron Retention (3' side)",
  subtitle = "Comparator exon extends into the intron from the 3' end (GAIN)")
```

## SE (Skipped Exon)

**Skipped Exon.** An exon present in one isoform is completely absent from the
other. The flanking exons splice directly to each other, skipping over the
exon. Direction: GAIN if the comparator includes the exon (reference skips
it); LOSS if the comparator skips it (reference includes it).

```{r glossary-se, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 600, 800), ref_e  = c(200, 500, 700, 900),
  comp_s = c(100, 400, 800),       comp_e = c(200, 500, 900),
  title = "SE: Skipped Exon",
  subtitle = "Comparator skips an internal exon present in the reference (LOSS)")
```

## Missing_Internal

**Missing Internal Exon.** Similar to SE but arising from a multi-exon skip:
one isoform is missing one or more internal exons that are present in the
other. Often co-occurs with other Missing_Internal events from the same
splice decision. Direction: GAIN if the comparator has the exon; LOSS if
the comparator lacks it.

```{r glossary-mi, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 350, 550, 750, 950), ref_e  = c(200, 450, 650, 850, 1050),
  comp_s = c(100, 950),                 comp_e = c(200, 1050),
  title = "Missing_Internal: Missing Internal Exon(s)",
  subtitle = "Comparator skips multiple internal exons (LOSS x 3)")
```

## IR

**Full Intron Retention.** One isoform has a single exon that spans the region
covered by two or more exons (plus the intervening intron) in the other
isoform. The retaining exon boundaries match exactly. Direction: GAIN if the
comparator retains the intron; LOSS if the reference retains it.

```{r glossary-ir, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400),       comp_e = c(200, 850),
  title = "IR: Full Intron Retention",
  subtitle = "Comparator retains intron -- single exon spans two exons + intron in ref (GAIN)")
```

## IR_diff_5

**Intron Retention with 5' Boundary Difference.** Like IR, but the retaining
exon's 5' boundary differs from the first overlapping exon in the other
isoform. The intron is retained, but the retaining exon starts after the
first reference overlap exon (falls short at the 5' end).

```{r glossary-ird5, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 430),       comp_e = c(200, 850),
  title = "IR_diff_5: Intron Retention with 5' Boundary Difference",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon starts AFTER ref overlap exon (falls short at 5' end)")
```

## IR_diff_3

**Intron Retention with 3' Boundary Difference.** Like IR, but the retaining
exon's 3' boundary differs from the last overlapping exon in the other
isoform. The intron is retained, but the retaining exon ends before the
last reference overlap exon (falls short at the 3' end).

```{r glossary-ird3, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 400),       comp_e = c(200, 820),
  title = "IR_diff_3: Intron Retention with 3' Boundary Difference",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon ends BEFORE ref overlap exon (falls short at 3' end)")
```

## IR_diff_5_3

**Intron Retention with Both Boundary Differences.** Like IR, but both the 5'
and 3' boundaries of the retaining exon differ from the flanking exons in the
other isoform. The intron is retained but the retaining exon falls short at
both ends.

```{r glossary-ird53, fig.width=8, fig.height=3, echo=FALSE}
glossary_plot(
  ref_s  = c(100, 400, 700), ref_e  = c(200, 550, 850),
  comp_s = c(100, 430),       comp_e = c(200, 820),
  title = "IR_diff_5_3: Intron Retention with Both Boundary Differences",
  subtitle = "Retaining exon falls short at both 5' and 3' ends")
```

In the IR section of this report, **IR_diff** refers to the aggregate of IR_diff_5,
IR_diff_3, and IR_diff_5_3 events.


# 1. Comparison of Long-read to Short-read RNA-seq Gene Level Quantification {#sec1-srlr}

Before pivoting to long-read isoform-level analyses, we verify that the
short-read and long-read platforms agree on the differential expression
effect of Smg1i treatment at the gene level. (A full multipanel figure
including expression-magnitude correlation is in the manuscript
supplement; this section reports only the per-cell-type logFC
concordance.)

```{r sec1-srlr-data}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source:
#   - SR gene mashr DE files: shortread_dge/mashr/nmd_mashr_dge_{at,dd,fb,mv}_2026.3.10.csv
#   - LR isoform mashr DIE files: isocall_dge/mashr/nmd_mashr_die_{at,dd,fb,mv}_2026.3.10.csv
# Population: genes shared between platforms (matched on unversioned ENSG ID).
# LR gene-level summary: median posterior logFC across all isoforms of each gene.

sr_dir <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/shortread_dge/mashr"
lr_dir <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/isocall_dge/mashr"

# Strip Ensembl versions for matching
strip_ver <- function(x) sub("\\..*$", "", x)

srlr_concordance <- lapply(c("AT", "DD", "FB", "MV"), function(ct) {
  sr <- read.csv(file.path(sr_dir, sprintf("nmd_mashr_dge_%s_2026.3.10.csv",
                                            tolower(ct))),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  lr <- read.csv(file.path(lr_dir, sprintf("nmd_mashr_die_%s_2026.3.10.csv",
                                            tolower(ct))),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  sr$gene_unv <- strip_ver(sr$ensembl_gene_id_version)
  lr$gene_unv <- strip_ver(lr$gene_id)
  # Aggregate LR isoform → gene by median logFC
  lr_gene <- aggregate(logFC ~ gene_unv, data = lr, FUN = median, na.rm = TRUE)
  m <- merge(sr[, c("gene_unv", "logFC")], lr_gene,
             by = "gene_unv", suffixes = c("_sr", "_lr"))
  m <- m[!is.na(m$logFC_sr) & !is.na(m$logFC_lr), ]
  data.frame(
    `Cell Type` = ct,
    `N genes` = format(nrow(m), big.mark = ","),
    `Pearson r (logFC)` = round(cor(m$logFC_sr, m$logFC_lr), 3),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
})
srlr_table <- do.call(rbind, srlr_concordance)
render_dt(srlr_table, caption = "SR↔LR logFC concordance, gene level")
```

Column definitions: **Cell Type** = primary lung cell type; **N genes** =
count of genes shared between SR gene-level mashr and LR isoform-level
mashr (matched on unversioned Ensembl gene ID); **Pearson r (logFC)** =
correlation between SR posterior logFC and LR median-isoform posterior
logFC across the shared gene set.

The Smg1i logFC effect correlates moderately between platforms across
all four cell types (Pearson r `r round(min(srlr_table$"Pearson r (logFC)"), 2)`–`r round(max(srlr_table$"Pearson r (logFC)"), 2)`).
This is lower than typical gene-level expression concordance (which is
generally r > 0.8) but expected — logFC is a derived quantity, and the
gene-level LR signal is approximated by the median across isoforms of
each gene since a native LR gene-level mashr fit is not yet available
in this run. See Methods for the aggregation choice. The full multipanel
concordance figure is in the manuscript supplement:
`paper_figures/FigX-SRLRConcordance_generated.pdf`.

# 2. Isoform Expression Landscape {#sec2-landscape}

Before asking what triggers NMD, we briefly establish the transcriptional
landscape. NMD-sensitive isoforms are excluded so that the baseline reflects
normal transcriptional diversity.

**Data source:** Non-NMD expressed isoforms for genes in the gene-matched
pair set (structures.rds, expression_data.rds, nmd_classification.rds).

```{r sec1-diversity-data}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: structures.rds (extractIsoformStructures), cds.rds (extractCds),
#   expression_data.rds (TMM-normalized count matrix from 01_prepare_data_mashr.R),
#   nmd_classification.rds (mashr NMD/non-NMD classification)
# Population: Expressed NON-NMD isoforms for genes in gene-matched pair set.
#   NMD-sensitive isoforms (mashr all_samples) are excluded so that Section 2
#   describes the baseline transcriptional landscape that NMD acts upon.
#   Gene set defined by profiles_list (loaded in STAGE 2, gene-matched).

# Genes in the gene-matched pair set
pair_genes <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$gene_id)

# NMD isoform IDs to exclude
nmd_isoforms <- nmd_class$all_samples$nmd

# All expressed non-NMD isoforms for these genes (coding + non-coding)
sec1_structures <- structures %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% pair_genes,
         isoform_id %in% rownames(expr_mat),
         !isoform_id %in% nmd_isoforms)

# Coding subset (for CDS-dependent analyses later)
coding_structures <- sec1_structures %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"])

coding_cds <- cds %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% coding_structures$isoform_id)

cat("Gene-matched pair genes:", length(pair_genes), "\n")
cat("NMD isoforms excluded:", sum(structures$isoform_id %in% nmd_isoforms &
      structures$gene_id %in% pair_genes &
      structures$isoform_id %in% rownames(expr_mat)), "\n")
cat("Non-NMD expressed isoforms (these genes):", nrow(sec1_structures), "\n")
cat("  of which coding:", nrow(coding_structures), "\n")

# ── Isoform count per gene (all isoforms) ──
iso_per_gene <- sec1_structures %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  summarise(n_isoforms = n(), .groups = "drop")

cat("\nIsoforms per gene (all expressed):\n")
print(summary(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms))
cat("Genes with ≥2 isoforms:", sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 2), "\n")
cat("Genes with ≥5 isoforms:", sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 5), "\n")
```

## Isoform Count Distribution

```{r sec1-isoform-count-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
fig_iso_count <- ggplot(iso_per_gene, aes(x = n_isoforms)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#4292c6", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 30, 5)) +
  labs(title = "Expressed Isoform Count per Gene",
       subtitle = sprintf("Gene-matched pair set | Median: %d isoforms | %s genes with ≥2",
                          median(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms),
                          fmt(sum(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms >= 2))),
       x = "Number of expressed isoforms", y = "Number of genes")
save_fig(fig_iso_count, "fig0a_isoform_count_distribution")
```

<summary>Click to view tabular data for isoform count distribution</summary>

```{r sec1-isocount-table, echo=FALSE}
iso_summary <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Genes", "Median isoforms/gene", "Mean isoforms/gene",
                "Q25", "Q75", "Max",
                "Genes with \u2265 2 isoforms", "Genes with \u2265 5 isoforms"),
  Value = c(fmt(nrow(iso_per_gene)),
            median(iso_per_gene$n_isoforms),

```

Columns: **Statistic** = summary measure; **Value** = computed value across
gene-matched pair genes (non-NMD expressed isoforms only).

</details>

An "expressed isoform" is one that passed the condition-stratified 5%
isoform proportion filter applied during data preparation
(`01_prepare_data_mashr.R`): for each gene, an isoform is retained if it
contributes at least 5% of the gene's total expression in either the DMSO
or SMG1i condition. Expression is quantified from a PacBio long-read IsoSeq
count matrix (`r fmt(n_raw_isoforms)` isoforms across `r n_samples` samples
after exclusion of 2 outlier samples), TMM-normalized via edgeR. The gene set
shown here is restricted to the `r fmt(length(pair_genes))` genes in the
gene-matched pair set (genes with at least one NMD-sensitive and one
non-NMD isoform in both C2 and C4 comparisons). NMD-sensitive isoforms
(mashr posterior logFC > 0 and lfsr < 0.05 in the all-samples analysis)
are excluded from this count so that the distribution reflects baseline
transcriptional diversity, not NMD-driven variation. Both coding and
non-coding isoforms are included.

## Expression Level of Reference and Comparator Isoforms

```{r sec1-expression-concentration}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: expression_data.rds (DMSO + SMG1i samples), sec1_structures
#   (all expressed non-NMD isoforms, coding + non-coding),
#   profiles_list (gene-matched pairs for reference/comparator CPM)
# Population: multi-isoform genes in the gene-matched pair set (all biotypes)
# --- Dominant isoform expression share ---
dmso_samples <- sample_meta$sample_id[sample_meta$treatment == "DMSO"]
dmso_mat <- expr_mat[, colnames(expr_mat) %in% dmso_samples]
lib_sizes <- colSums(dmso_mat)
cpm_mat <- sweep(dmso_mat, 2, lib_sizes, "/") * 1e6

gene_ids <- sec1_structures$gene_id[match(rownames(cpm_mat), sec1_structures$isoform_id)]
valid <- !is.na(gene_ids) & rownames(cpm_mat) %in% sec1_structures$isoform_id
mean_cpm <- rowMeans(cpm_mat[valid, ])
iso_df <- data.frame(isoform_id = rownames(cpm_mat)[valid],
                      gene_id = gene_ids[valid], mean_cpm = mean_cpm,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dominant_fraction <- iso_df %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2, sum(mean_cpm) > 0) %>%
  summarise(n_iso = n(), total_cpm = sum(mean_cpm), max_cpm = max(mean_cpm),
            dominant_pct = 100 * max_cpm / total_cpm, .groups = "drop")

med_dom_pct <- round(median(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct), 1)
pct_gt50 <- round(100 * mean(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 50), 1)
pct_gt80 <- round(100 * mean(dominant_fraction$dominant_pct > 80), 1)

fig_conc <- ggplot(dominant_fraction, aes(x = dominant_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "#4393c3", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_dom_pct, linetype = "dashed", color = "#d6604d", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = med_dom_pct + 2, y = Inf, vjust = 2, hjust = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("Median: %.1f%%", med_dom_pct)) +
  labs(title = "Expression Concentration: Dominant Isoform Share",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s multi-isoform coding genes | >50%%: %s%% of genes | >80%%: %s%%",
                          fmt(nrow(dominant_fraction)), pct_gt50, pct_gt80),
       x = "Dominant isoform expression share (%)", y = "Number of genes") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20))
save_fig(fig_conc, "fig_sec1_expression_concentration", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec1-expression-cpm}
# --- CPM comparison: reference, NMD comparator, Control comparator ---
# Compute mean DMSO CPM for reference, NMD comp, and Control comp isoforms
ref_ids_c2 <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$reference_isoform_id)
comp_ids_c2 <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$comparator_isoform_id)
comp_ids_c4 <- unique(profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]]$comparator_isoform_id)

# Compute mean CPM separately for DMSO and SMG1i conditions
smg1i_samples <- sample_meta$sample_id[sample_meta$treatment == "Smg1i"]
smg1i_mat <- expr_mat[, colnames(expr_mat) %in% smg1i_samples]
smg1i_lib <- colSums(smg1i_mat)
smg1i_cpm_mat <- sweep(smg1i_mat, 2, smg1i_lib, "/") * 1e6

get_mean_cpm <- function(ids, mat) {
  idx <- match(ids, rownames(mat))
  idx <- idx[!is.na(idx)]
  rowMeans(mat[idx, , drop = FALSE])
}

# DMSO expression
cpm_ref_dmso <- get_mean_cpm(ref_ids_c2, cpm_mat)
cpm_nmd_dmso <- get_mean_cpm(comp_ids_c2, cpm_mat)
cpm_ctrl_dmso <- get_mean_cpm(comp_ids_c4, cpm_mat)

# SMG1i expression
cpm_ref_smg1i <- get_mean_cpm(ref_ids_c2, smg1i_cpm_mat)
cpm_nmd_smg1i <- get_mean_cpm(comp_ids_c2, smg1i_cpm_mat)
cpm_ctrl_smg1i <- get_mean_cpm(comp_ids_c4, smg1i_cpm_mat)

cpm_compare <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "Reference", cpm = cpm_ref_dmso, condition = "DMSO"),
  data.frame(group = "NMD comparator", cpm = cpm_nmd_dmso, condition = "DMSO"),
  data.frame(group = "Control comparator", cpm = cpm_ctrl_dmso, condition = "DMSO"),
  data.frame(group = "Reference", cpm = cpm_ref_smg1i, condition = "SMG1i"),
  data.frame(group = "NMD comparator", cpm = cpm_nmd_smg1i, condition = "SMG1i"),
  data.frame(group = "Control comparator", cpm = cpm_ctrl_smg1i, condition = "SMG1i"))
cpm_compare$group <- factor(cpm_compare$group,
  levels = c("Reference", "Control comparator", "NMD comparator"))
cpm_compare$condition <- factor(cpm_compare$condition, levels = c("DMSO", "SMG1i"))

fig_cpm <- ggplot(cpm_compare, aes(x = group, y = log10(cpm + 1), fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("DMSO" = "#4393c3", "SMG1i" = "#ef8a62")) +
  labs(title = "Expression Level: Reference, NMD Comparator, and Control Comparator",
       subtitle = sprintf("Reference: %s | NMD comp: %s | Control comp: %s isoforms",
                          fmt(length(cpm_ref_dmso)), fmt(length(cpm_nmd_dmso)),
                          fmt(length(cpm_ctrl_dmso))),
       x = NULL, y = "log10(mean CPM + 1)", fill = "Treatment") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_cpm, "fig_sec1_cpm_by_role", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec1-expression-length}
# --- Transcript length comparison ---
tx_lengths_all <- setNames(

len_compare$group <- factor(len_compare$group,
  levels = c("Reference (non-NMD)", "Control comparator", "NMD comparator"))

fig_len <- ggplot(len_compare, aes(x = group, y = length, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +

                                "Control comparator" = "#67a9cf",
                                "NMD comparator" = "#ef8a62")) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Transcript Length: Reference, NMD Comparator, and Control Comparator",
       subtitle = sprintf("Reference: %s | NMD comp: %s | Control comp: %s isoforms",

       x = NULL, y = "Transcript length (bp, log scale)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
save_fig(fig_len, "fig_sec1_length_by_role", width = 10, height = 5)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon tests and summary statistics
len_by_group <- split(len_compare$length, len_compare$group)
len_summary <- data.frame(
  Group = names(len_by_group),
  n = sapply(len_by_group, length),
  Median = sapply(len_by_group, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q25 = sapply(len_by_group, quantile, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
  Q75 = sapply(len_by_group, quantile, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Pairwise tests
pw_tests <- list(
  c("NMD comparator", "Reference (non-NMD)"),
  c("NMD comparator", "Control comparator"),
  c("Control comparator", "Reference (non-NMD)"))
pw_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pw_tests, function(pair) {
  wt <- wilcox.test(len_by_group[[pair[1]]], len_by_group[[pair[2]]])
  data.frame(Comparison = paste(pair[1], "vs", pair[2]),
             p_value = signif(wt$p.value, 3), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

invisible(NULL)  # tables rendered in collapsible block below
```

two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

</details>

For each multi-isoform gene, the dominant isoform share is computed as
`100 * max(mean_DMSO_CPM) / sum(mean_DMSO_CPM)` across all expressed
non-NMD isoforms for that gene. Some genes show very high concentration
(>90%) because the 5% isoform proportion filter is condition-stratified:
an isoform passes if it reaches 5% in either DMSO or SMG1i. Minor
isoforms that pass only in SMG1i (e.g., NMD targets rescued by SMG1
inhibition) may have very low DMSO expression, contributing little to
the denominator. Despite maintaining many expressed isoforms, most genes
concentrate the majority of their output on a single dominant isoform
(median `r med_dom_pct`% of gene expression). `r pct_gt50`% of genes have
a dominant isoform accounting for more than half their output, and
`r pct_gt80`% exceed 80%. This concentration motivates the paired
comparison framework: the dominant non-NMD isoform serves as the reference
against which NMD-sensitive comparators are compared.

NMD comparators are expressed at lower levels than references in DMSO (as
expected for isoforms targeted by degradation) but increase under SMG1i
treatment, which inhibits the NMD pathway. This rescue effect --- higher
expression when NMD is blocked --- is the empirical basis for classifying
these isoforms as NMD-sensitive. Reference and Control comparator expression
is largely unchanged between conditions, confirming that the SMG1i effect is
specific to NMD targets.

## Isoform Annotation Status

```{r sec1-annotation-status}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: profiles_list (gene-matched C2 and C4 pairs)
# Population: unique isoform IDs by role (reference, NMD comparator, Control comparator)
# Novel isoforms identified by ".novelN" suffix in the isoform ID

is_novel_iso <- function(ids) grepl("[.]novel[0-9]+$", ids)

ref_ids_ann <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$reference_isoform_id)
nmd_ids_ann <- unique(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]$comparator_isoform_id)
ctrl_ids_ann <- unique(profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]]$comparator_isoform_id)

ann_table <- data.frame(
  Role = c("Reference (non-NMD)", "NMD comparator", "Control comparator"),
  n = c(length(ref_ids_ann), length(nmd_ids_ann), length(ctrl_ids_ann)),
  ENST = c(sum(!is_novel_iso(ref_ids_ann)), sum(!is_novel_iso(nmd_ids_ann)),
            sum(!is_novel_iso(ctrl_ids_ann))),
  Novel = c(sum(is_novel_iso(ref_ids_ann)), sum(is_novel_iso(nmd_ids_ann)),
             sum(is_novel_iso(ctrl_ids_ann))),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ann_table$pct_ENST <- round(100 * ann_table$ENST / ann_table$n, 1)
ann_table$pct_Novel <- round(100 * ann_table$Novel / ann_table$n, 1)

render_dt(ann_table, caption = "Isoform Annotation Status by Role")
```

Columns: **Role** = isoform role in the paired analysis; **n** = unique
isoform count; **ENST** = GENCODE-annotated isoforms (ENST prefix);
**Novel** = novel isoforms identified by long-read sequencing (gene_id.novelN
suffix); **pct_ENST / pct_Novel** = percentages.

NMD comparators are predominantly novel isoforms
(`r ann_table$pct_Novel[ann_table$Role == "NMD comparator"]`%), consistent
with NMD-sensitive transcripts being underrepresented in reference annotations
due to their rapid degradation in vivo. Reference isoforms are mostly
GENCODE-annotated (`r ann_table$pct_ENST[ann_table$Role == "Reference (non-NMD)"]`%),
as expected for dominant, stably expressed transcripts. This distinction is
important for CDS interpretation: GENCODE isoforms have curated CDS
annotations, while novel isoforms rely entirely on computational CDS
prediction (TransDecoder2).

# 3. Isopair Pair Analysis: Splicing Events Distinguishing NMD from Control {#sec3-isopair}

This section begins the NMD-specific analysis. We compare structural profiles
between NMD (C2) and Control (C4) gene-matched isoform pairs to identify which
splicing event types are enriched in NMD-sensitive isoforms.

**Methods:** Structural profiles from `Isopair::buildProfiles()` quantify
splicing event types for each pair. Sequence divergence
(`quantifyPairDivergence()`) measures exonic sequence shared between isoforms.
NMD vs Control enrichment is tested by Fisher's exact test per event type.

## Sequence Shared — NMD vs Control

```{r goal1-fig1-pct-shared, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}

# div_c4: same for Control

pct_shared_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(comparison = "NMD",     pct_shared = div_c2$pct_shared),
  data.frame(comparison = "Control", pct_shared = div_c4$pct_shared))
pct_shared_data <- pct_shared_data[!is.na(pct_shared_data$pct_shared), ]

  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +

       subtitle = "NMD pairs shifted right = more similar (targeted splicing changes)",
       x = "Sequence Shared (%)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig1_shared, "fig1_pct_shared_density")

# Summary stats
shared_summary <- pct_shared_data |>
  group_by(comparison) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median = round(median(pct_shared), 1),
            mean = round(mean(pct_shared), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

## Splicing Event Enrichment — NMD vs Control

For each event type, the denominator is all gene-matched pairs (not restricted
to coding) — a pair is counted if it has ≥1 event of that type. Fisher's exact
test compares the proportion of pairs with each event type between NMD (C2) and
Control (C4), both on the same gene-matched set.

```{r goal1-table1b-event-enrichment}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (set_results[[key]]$profiles)
# compute_event_freq(profiles) counts pairs with each event type using:
#   - Boolean columns (tss_changed, tes_changed, n_a5ss > 0, etc.) from profiles
#   - Partial_IR_5/3 from detailed_events list-column
#   These are computed by buildProfiles → compareSplicingChoices
# Fisher's exact test: event prevalence in NMD vs Control on gene-matched sets

ef_c2 <- compute_event_freq(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
ef_c4 <- compute_event_freq(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_c2 <- nrow(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_c4 <- nrow(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)

enrichment <- merge(ef_c2, ef_c4, by = "event_type", suffixes = c("_NMD", "_Ctrl"))

# Fisher's exact test per event type
enrichment$fisher_OR <- NA_real_
enrichment$fisher_p <- NA_real_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(enrichment))) {
  a <- enrichment$n_pairs_with_event_NMD[i]
  b <- n_c2 - a
  c <- enrichment$n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl[i]
  d <- n_c4 - c
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, c, d), nrow = 2)), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    enrichment$fisher_OR[i] <- round(ft$estimate, 2)
    enrichment$fisher_p[i] <- ft$p.value
  }
}

enrichment$direction <- ifelse(enrichment$fisher_p > 0.05, "Non-significant",
  ifelse(enrichment$fisher_OR > 1, "Enriched in NMD", "Enriched in Control"))
enrichment <- enrichment[order(enrichment$fisher_p), ]

enrich_display <- enrichment[, c("event_type", "n_pairs_with_event_NMD", "pct_of_pairs_NMD",
                                 "n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl", "pct_of_pairs_Ctrl",
                                 "fisher_OR", "fisher_p", "direction")]
enrich_display$fisher_p <- signif(enrich_display$fisher_p, 3)
write.csv(enrichment, file.path(table_dir, "table1b_event_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r sec1-enrichment-table, echo=FALSE}
          caption = "Table 1b: Splicing Event Type Enrichment — NMD vs Control")
```

Columns: **event_type** = splicing event type (see Event Type Glossary);
**n_pairs_with_event_NMD** = number of gene-matched NMD (C2) pairs with ≥1
event of this type; **pct_of_pairs_NMD** = percentage of all
`r fmt(n_c2)` NMD pairs; **n_pairs_with_event_Ctrl/pct_of_pairs_Ctrl** =
same for Control (C4, `r fmt(n_c4)` pairs); **fisher_OR** = Fisher's exact
test odds ratio (>1 = NMD-enriched); **fisher_p** = p-value; **direction** =
Enriched in NMD, Enriched in Control, or Non-significant (p > 0.05).

</details>

```{r goal1-fig1b-event-barplot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
bar_df <- rbind(
```

## Gain/Loss Direction by Event Type

For each event type, the comparator can GAIN sequence (comparator has additional
sequence relative to reference) or LOSE sequence (comparator is missing sequence
present in reference). The table below shows event counts and the percentage of
events in each direction, separately for NMD and Control pairs.

```{r goal1-table1c-gain-loss}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (set_results[[key]]$profiles)
# $detailed_events: list-column, one data.frame per pair from buildProfiles
#   Each event row has event_type and direction (GAIN or LOSS)
#   Direction is from comparator's perspective (see Event Type Glossary)
# For each comparison (NMD, Control): count events by type × direction,
#   compute % GAIN and % LOSS within each event type

get_gain_loss_pct <- function(profiles, label) {
  all_events <- do.call(rbind, profiles$detailed_events)
  if (is.null(all_events) || nrow(all_events) == 0) return(NULL)
  gl <- all_events |>
    group_by(event_type, direction) |>
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  totals <- gl |> group_by(event_type) |> summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  gl <- merge(gl, totals, by = "event_type")
  gl$pct <- round(100 * gl$n / gl$total, 1)
  gl$comparison <- label
  gl
}

gl_c2 <- get_gain_loss_pct(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles, "NMD")
gl_c4 <- get_gain_loss_pct(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles, "Control")
gl_all <- rbind(gl_c2, gl_c4)

gl_wide <- gl_all |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = event_type,
    names_from = c(comparison, direction),
    values_from = c(n, pct),
    values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(event_type)

col_order <- c("event_type",
  "n_NMD_GAIN", "n_NMD_LOSS", "pct_NMD_GAIN",
  "n_Control_GAIN", "n_Control_LOSS", "pct_Control_GAIN")
existing_cols <- intersect(col_order, names(gl_wide))
gl_display <- gl_wide[, existing_cols, drop = FALSE]

gl_display$fisher_p <- NA_real_
gl_display$direction_diff <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gl_display))) {
  ng <- gl_display$n_NMD_GAIN[i]
  nl <- gl_display$n_NMD_LOSS[i]
  cg <- gl_display$n_Control_GAIN[i]
  cl <- gl_display$n_Control_LOSS[i]
  if (ng + nl > 0 && cg + cl > 0) {
    ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(ng, nl, cg, cl), nrow = 2)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(ft)) {
      gl_display$fisher_p[i] <- signif(ft$p.value, 3)
      pct_nmd <- 100 * ng / (ng + nl)
      pct_ctrl <- 100 * cg / (cg + cl)
      gl_display$direction_diff[i] <- if (ft$p.value > 0.05) "Non-significant"
        else if (pct_nmd > pct_ctrl) "More GAIN in NMD"
        else "More LOSS in NMD"
    }
  }
}

write.csv(gl_display, file.path(table_dir, "table1c_gain_loss_events.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Stop Codon Analysis

The prediction model (Section 3e) identifies downstream EJC count as the strongest
single predictor of NMD status. Here we examine stop codon position in detail
using gene-matched C2 (NMD) vs C4 (Control) isoform pairs, quantify PTC
enrichment with a dose-response relationship, and trace how PTCs arise through
three distinct splicing mechanisms.

# 4. PTC Mechanism: How Splicing Triggers NMD {#sec4-ptc-mechanism}

## PTC Rates

*This subsection's first chunk is a silent setup step that subsets gene-matched
profiles to coding pairs (both reference and comparator isoforms classified as
coding by SQANTI3). The PTC rate table and Fisher OR are computed and rendered
in the chunks that follow.*

```{r goal1-ptc-rates-subsetting}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Reading Frame and PTC Analysis > PTC Detection"
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles (profiles_list → set_results$profiles)
#   Pipeline: 01 (mashr NMD classification) → 02 (pair generation + buildProfiles)
#   → gene-matching (this report, STAGE 2) → set_results (STAGE 3)
#
# Subsetting for PTC rate calculation:
#   1. Start with gene-matched C2 (NMD) and C4 (Control) profiles
#   2. Restrict to "coding pairs": both reference AND comparator isoform must have
#      coding_status == "coding" in cds.rds (from Isopair extractCds() on SQANTI CDS)
#   3. Numerator: comparator isoforms with has_ptc == TRUE in ptc.rds
#      PTC definition: stop codon >50 nt upstream of the last exon-junction complex (EJC)
#   4. Denominator: total coding pairs (from step 2)
#   5. Fisher's exact test: 2×2 table of (PTC+/PTC−) × (NMD/Control)

# Using centralized coding_ids from load-data
n_gm_c2 <- nrow(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles)
n_gm_c4 <- nrow(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles)

p_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles
cod_c2 <- p_c2[p_c2$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                p_c2$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
p_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles
cod_c4 <- p_c4[p_c4$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                p_c4$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
```

From `r fmt(n_gm_c2)` gene-matched NMD pairs and `r fmt(n_gm_c4)` Control
pairs, we restrict to **coding pairs** (both reference and comparator classified
as protein-coding by SQANTI). This yields `r fmt(nrow(cod_c2))` coding NMD
pairs and `r fmt(nrow(cod_c4))` coding Control pairs. The PTC rate is the
fraction of coding comparators whose stop codon falls >50 nt upstream of the
last EJC.

```{r goal1-ptc-rates}
write.csv(ptc_rates, file.path(table_dir, "table2_ptc_rates_allsamples.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Three Mechanisms of PTC Creation {#sec2b-ptc-mechanisms}

PTCs in NMD-responsive isoforms arise through three distinct splicing mechanisms:

- **Frameshift → PTC**: A splice event (e.g., skipped exon, retained intron)
  shifts the reading frame, and the new frame encounters a stop codon upstream
  of the last EJC. Identified by `analyzeFrameWalk()`.
- **In-frame stop → PTC**: A splice event changes the exon path such that the
  comparator's stop codon is in a different position from the reference, falling
  upstream of the last EJC. The PTC-causing event is identified by finding the
  event whose genomic coordinates contain the comparator's stop codon.
- **3'UTR splicing → PTC**: The comparator and reference share the **same stop
  codon**, but the comparator has additional exon-exon junctions downstream of
  the stop — from 3'UTR splicing events — that reposition the last EJC, making
  the shared stop codon "premature" under the >50 nt rule. We refer to these as
  **same-stop PTC+** pairs.

## How PTCs Arise: Frameshift vs In-Frame Stop

*This subsection's first chunk is a silent compute step that runs the
three-mechanism PTC attribution (Frameshift / In-frame stop / 3'UTR splice)
across all PTC-positive NMD comparators using the shared
`attribute_ptc_events()` function in `analysis_functions.R` — the same routine
used downstream for reclassified PTC-negative pairs (Section 4, "Ruling Out
Alternative NMD Mechanisms"). Counts and percentages are summarized in the
prose and Sankey figure that follow.*

```{r goal2-ptc-mechanisms}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: attribute_ptc_events() from analysis_functions.R (shared with 05r)
# Methods: METHODS.md § "PTC-Causing Event Attribution"
#
# For each PTC+ NMD comparator, identify the PTC-CAUSING splice event using
# the shared three-mechanism attribution function. This is the SAME code used
# for reclassified PTC-negative pairs in Section 4 (Ruling Out Alternative NMD Mechanisms).
#
# Strand-aware PTC position:
#   + strand: PTC = cds_stop (larger genomic coordinate = 3' end of CDS)
#   - strand: PTC = cds_start (smaller genomic coordinate = 3' end on minus strand)

fc_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$frame_comp
fw_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$frame_walk
prof_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles

ptc_pos_ids <- ptc$isoform_id[ptc$has_ptc == TRUE]

fc_c2_ps <- fc_c2$pair_summary
fc_c2_ps$has_ptc <- fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_pos_ids

frameshift_cats <- c("same_start_frameshift",
                     "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")
fc_c2_ps$is_frameshift_cat <- fc_c2_ps$frame_category %in% frameshift_cats

# PTC+ pairs by mechanism — restrict to coding pairs (both ref and comp coding)
# to match the coding_pairs_c2 base used in Goals 3-4 and the cumulative flowchart
ptc_plus <- fc_c2_ps[fc_c2_ps$has_ptc == TRUE &
  fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
  fc_c2_ps$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
n_ptc_via_fs    <- sum(ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat)
n_ptc_via_nonfs <- sum(!ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat)
n_ptc_total     <- nrow(ptc_plus)

# Also count all coding NMD pairs for context (same coding filter as ptc_plus)
fc_c2_coding <- fc_c2_ps[fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
  fc_c2_ps$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]
n_coding_nmd <- nrow(fc_c2_coding)

# ── Strand-aware PTC position (using centralized lookups from load-data) ──
# Build PTC genomic position vector (strand-aware)
ptc_genomic_pos <- ifelse(strand_lookup[ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id] == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id])
names(ptc_genomic_pos) <- ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id

# Build is_frameshift lookup
is_fs_lookup <- setNames(ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat, ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id)

# Use shared attribution function (same as Section 4 reclassified pairs)
ptc_events_df <- attribute_ptc_events(
  pairs = ptc_plus[, c("comparator_isoform_id", "reference_isoform_id")],
  fw_events = fw_c2$events,
  profiles = prof_c2,
  ptc_genomic_pos = ptc_genomic_pos,
  atg_genomic_pos = NULL,  # no region filtering for PTC+ (SQANTI CDS)
  strand_vec = strand_lookup,
  is_frameshift_vec = is_fs_lookup
)

n_attributed <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "direct")
n_unresolved <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "unresolved")
```

Of `r fmt(n_coding_nmd)` coding NMD pairs, `r fmt(n_ptc_total)` have a PTC in
the comparator: `r fmt(n_ptc_via_fs)` via frameshift
(`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_fs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%) and `r fmt(n_ptc_via_nonfs)`
via in-frame stop (`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_nonfs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%). Of
`r fmt(nrow(ptc_events_df))` PTC+ pairs, `r fmt(n_attributed)` were directly
attributed to a specific splice event`r if (n_unresolved > 0) paste0(", with ", fmt(n_unresolved), " unresolved")`.

The Sankey diagram below adds a third category — same-stop PTC+ pairs arising
from 3'UTR splicing — to give a complete picture of PTC-causing mechanisms.

## PTC-Causing Splice Events (Sankey)

```{r goal2-fig5-sankey}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Combines three sources of PTC attribution:
#   1. Diff-stop frameshift: ptc_events_df (from attribute_ptc_events)
#   2. Diff-stop in-frame: ptc_events_df (from attribute_ptc_events)
#   3. Same-stop (3'UTR splice): attributed here using nearest-to-stop 3'UTR event
# Same-stop attribution: for each same-stop pair, find splice events downstream
# of the stop codon and attribute to the nearest one (the junction most likely
# to place the critical EJC within the >50 nt window).

# Build profile lookup (needed for 3'UTR event attribution below)
comp_to_idx <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(prof_c2)), prof_c2$comparator_isoform_id)

# ── Identify same-stop PTC+ pairs (strand-aware) ──
# This duplicates the strand-aware stop comparison from goal3-fig6-pop,
# which has not yet run. Uses the same logic: + strand → cds_stop, - strand → cds_start.
ptc_plus_sankey <- ptc_plus  # from goal2-ptc-mechanisms
ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s <- strand_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id]
ptc_plus_sankey$comp_stop_s <- ifelse(ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id])
ptc_plus_sankey$ref_stop_s <- ifelse(ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$reference_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$reference_isoform_id])
ptc_plus_sankey$same_stop_s <- ptc_plus_sankey$comp_stop_s == ptc_plus_sankey$ref_stop_s

same_stop_sankey <- ptc_plus_sankey[which(ptc_plus_sankey$same_stop_s == TRUE), ]

# ── Attribute same-stop pairs to nearest 3'UTR event ──
# Uses shared attribute_3utr_splice() (same function as 05r_ref_atg_analysis.R)
ss_stop_vec <- setNames(same_stop_sankey$comp_stop_s, same_stop_sankey$comparator_isoform_id)
ss_strand_vec <- setNames(same_stop_sankey$strand_s, same_stop_sankey$comparator_isoform_id)

same_stop_events <- attribute_3utr_splice(
  pairs = same_stop_sankey[, c("comparator_isoform_id", "reference_isoform_id")],
  profiles = prof_c2,
  stop_genomic_pos = ss_stop_vec,
  strand_vec = ss_strand_vec
)
same_stop_events <- same_stop_events[same_stop_events$attribution == "direct", ]
n_same_stop_attributed <- nrow(same_stop_events)

# ── Combine all attributed pairs ──
# Diff-stop attributed (from goal2-ptc-mechanisms), excluding same-stop pairs.
# Same-stop pairs may have been "directly" attributed in goal2 if the stop
# position fell inside an event by coincidence — these belong in 3'UTR splice.
# Pairs with unknown ref stop (coding_status="unknown") are kept in diff-stop.
same_stop_comp_ids <- same_stop_sankey$comparator_isoform_id
diffstop_attr <- ptc_events_df[ptc_events_df$attribution == "direct" &
  !ptc_events_df$comparator_isoform_id %in% same_stop_comp_ids, ]
# Same-stop attributed (from above)
all_attr <- rbind(diffstop_attr, same_stop_events)

# Shorten event type labels and collapse rare types (shared function)
all_attr$event_short <- shorten_event_labels(all_attr$ptc_causing_event, collapse_rare = 3)

# Also make ptc_attr available for Table 5a/5b (diff-stop attributed only)
ptc_attr <- all_attr[all_attr$mechanism != "3'UTR splice", ]

# Aggregate: event_type → mechanism
sankey_agg <- all_attr |>
  group_by(event_short, mechanism) |>
  summarise(freq = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Interactive Sankey (HTML only)
mech_colors <- c("Frameshift" = "#d6604d",
                 "In-frame stop" = "#4393c3",
                 "3'UTR splice" = "#66c2a5")

nodes_vec <- unique(c(sankey_agg$event_short, sankey_agg$mechanism))
nodes_sankey <- data.frame(name = nodes_vec, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
links_sankey <- data.frame(
  source = match(sankey_agg$event_short, nodes_vec) - 1L,
  target = match(sankey_agg$mechanism, nodes_vec) - 1L,
  value  = sankey_agg$freq)
node_colors <- ifelse(nodes_sankey$name %in% names(mech_colors),
                      mech_colors[nodes_sankey$name], "#bdbdbd")
color_scale <- paste0(
  'd3.scaleOrdinal().domain([',
  paste0('"', nodes_sankey$name, '"', collapse = ','), ']).range([',
  paste0('"', node_colors, '"', collapse = ','), '])')
networkD3::sankeyNetwork(
  Links = links_sankey, Nodes = nodes_sankey,
  Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value",
  NodeID = "name", fontSize = 14, nodeWidth = 30, nodePadding = 15,
  colourScale = color_scale, sinksRight = TRUE)

# Static stacked bar chart (saves as PNG/PDF for paper)

# Order event types by total frequency
evt_totals <- sankey_agg %>%
  group_by(event_short) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(total)
sankey_agg$event_short <- factor(sankey_agg$event_short, levels = evt_totals$event_short)
sankey_agg$mechanism <- factor(sankey_agg$mechanism,
  levels = c("Frameshift", "In-frame stop", "3'UTR splice"))

fig_sankey_ptcpos <- ggplot(sankey_agg,
    aes(x = freq, y = event_short, fill = mechanism)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(freq >= 10, fmt(freq), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.8, color = "white",
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mech_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "PTC-Causing Splice Events (PTC+ Pairs)",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s attributed pairs | Stacked by mechanism",
                          fmt(sum(sankey_agg$freq))),
       x = "Number of pairs", y = NULL, fill = "Mechanism") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 14))
save_fig(fig_sankey_ptcpos, "fig_sankey_ptcpos", width = 10, height = 7)
```

**Frameshift** (red; `r fmt(sum(all_attr$mechanism == "Frameshift"))` pairs),
**In-frame stop** (blue; `r fmt(sum(all_attr$mechanism == "In-frame stop"))`),
and **3'UTR splice** (green; `r fmt(n_same_stop_attributed)` same-stop PTC+
pairs where a downstream splice event repositions an EJC, making the shared
stop codon premature).
`r { n_same_stop_unresolved_in_goal2 <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "unresolved" & ptc_events_df$comparator_isoform_id %in% same_stop_comp_ids); n_diffstop_unresolved <- n_unresolved - n_same_stop_unresolved_in_goal2; n_same_no_event <- nrow(same_stop_sankey) - n_same_stop_attributed; paste0(fmt(nrow(all_attr)), " of ", fmt(nrow(ptc_plus)), " PTC+ pairs shown (", fmt(n_diffstop_unresolved), " unresolved diff-stop and ", fmt(n_same_no_event), " same-stop pairs without identifiable events excluded).") }`

Column definitions: **mechanism** = the way the splicing event creates a PTC

**ptc_causing_event** = Isopair splice event type (SE, A3SS, A5SS, IR, etc.);

## PTC-Causing Event Proportions vs Control Baseline

```{r goal2-table4b-baseline}
# ── Data provenance ──
# NMD: PTC-causing events attributed above (both frameshift and in-frame stop)
# Control baseline: all splicing events across all C4 pairs
# Comparison: proportion of each event type among PTC-causing NMD events vs
#   all Control events (the baseline frequency in normal alternative splicing)

# NMD PTC-causing event frequencies (attributed pairs: direct + largest_event)
n_ptc_attr <- nrow(ptc_attr)
ptc_evt_freq <- sort(table(ptc_attr$ptc_causing_event), decreasing = TRUE)
ptc_evt_df <- data.frame(
  event_type = names(ptc_evt_freq),
  n_ptc_events = as.integer(ptc_evt_freq),
  pct_of_ptc = round(100 * as.integer(ptc_evt_freq) / n_ptc_attr, 1),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Control baseline: all events across all C4 pairs
ctrl_all_events <- do.call(rbind, set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles$detailed_events)
ctrl_event_freq <- table(ctrl_all_events$event_type)
ctrl_total <- sum(ctrl_event_freq)

# Merge
ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events <- as.integer(ctrl_event_freq[ptc_evt_df$event_type])
ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events[is.na(ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events)] <- 0L
ptc_evt_df$pct_ctrl <- round(100 * ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events / ctrl_total, 1)
ptc_evt_df$enrichment <- round(ptc_evt_df$pct_of_ptc / pmax(ptc_evt_df$pct_ctrl, 0.1), 1)

# Fisher's exact test per event type: is this event over-represented among
# PTC-causing events vs all Control events?
ptc_evt_df$fisher_p <- NA_real_
ptc_evt_df$direction <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ptc_evt_df))) {
  a <- ptc_evt_df$n_ptc_events[i]      # this event in PTC-causing
  b <- n_ptc_attr - a                    # other events in PTC-causing
  c_val <- ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events[i]  # this event in Control
  d_val <- ctrl_total - c_val            # other events in Control
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, c_val, d_val), nrow = 2)),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    ptc_evt_df$fisher_p[i] <- signif(ft$p.value, 3)
    ptc_evt_df$direction[i] <- if (ft$p.value > 0.05) "Non-significant"
      else if (ptc_evt_df$enrichment[i] > 1) "Enriched in PTC-causing"
      else "Depleted in PTC-causing"
  }
}

write.csv(ptc_evt_df, file.path(table_dir, "table5b_ptc_event_enrichment.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r goal2-fig5b-ptc-event-barplot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ptc_evt_df (computed above in goal2-table4b-baseline chunk)
# Paired bar chart: PTC-causing event proportions vs Control baseline

bar_df <- ptc_evt_df %>%
  select(event_type, `PTC-causing (NMD)` = pct_of_ptc,
         `All events (Control)` = pct_ctrl) %>%
  pivot_longer(-event_type, names_to = "source", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(event_type = factor(event_type,
    levels = ptc_evt_df$event_type[order(ptc_evt_df$pct_of_ptc, decreasing = TRUE)]))

# Significance annotations
sig_df <- ptc_evt_df %>%
  mutate(
    sig_label = case_when(
      fisher_p < 0.001 ~ "***",
      fisher_p < 0.01 ~ "**",
      fisher_p < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    ),
    y_pos = pmax(pct_of_ptc, pct_ctrl) + 1.5
  )

fig_ptc_events <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = event_type, y = pct, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(data = sig_df, aes(x = event_type, y = y_pos, label = sig_label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PTC-causing (NMD)" = "#ef8a62",
                                "All events (Control)" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "PTC-Causing Event Proportions vs Control Baseline",
       subtitle = sprintf("NMD: %s attributed PTC-causing events | Control: %s total events",
                          fmt(n_ptc_attr), fmt(ctrl_total)),
       x = NULL, y = "% of events", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_ptc_events, "fig5b_ptc_event_proportions", width = 10, height = 6)
```

Columns: **event_type** = splice event type; **n_ptc_events** = count of
