## Illustrative Example: Skipped Exon → Frameshift → PTC (POLR3D)

POLR3D encodes a subunit of RNA Polymerase III. The non-NMD reference
(ENST00000397802.8, 8 exons) and NMD comparator (novel2, 7 exons) share the
same CDS start. The comparator skips exon 6 (265 bp). Because 265 is not
divisible by 3 (265 mod 3 = 1), skipping this exon shifts the reading frame
by +1 nucleotide, producing a premature stop codon 406 bp earlier than the
normal stop. The ORF is truncated from 1,197 bp (399 aa) to 693 bp (231 aa).

```{r sec2b-example-polr3d, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# POLR3D: + strand, shared CDS start at 22245450
polr3d_ref_s <- c(22245235, 22247221, 22247857, 22248154, 22248481, 22249044, 22250075, 22250396)
polr3d_ref_e <- c(22245614, 22247264, 22248008, 22248278, 22248649, 22249309, 22250227, 22254600)
polr3d_comp_s <- c(22245233, 22247221, 22247857, 22248154, 22248481, 22250075, 22250396)
polr3d_comp_e <- c(22245614, 22247264, 22248008, 22248278, 22248649, 22250227, 22254360)

polr3d_events <- data.frame(
  five_prime = c(22249044, 22254600),
  three_prime = c(22249309, 22254360),
  event_type = c("SE", "Alt_TES"),
  direction = c("LOSS", "LOSS"))

polr3d_atg <- list(type = "frameshift_boundary", track = "ref",
  x = 22245450, label = "Shared ATG", color = "#2ca02c")
polr3d_ptc <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "comp",
  x = 22250112, label = "PTC (frameshift)", color = "#E74C3C")
polr3d_ref_stop <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "ref",
  x = 22250518, label = "Normal stop", color = "#27AE60")

p_polr3d <- plot_ucsc_pair(
  polr3d_ref_s, polr3d_ref_e, polr3d_comp_s, polr3d_comp_e, strand = "+",
  ref_cds = list(cds_start = 22245450, cds_stop = 22250518),
  comp_cds = list(cds_start = 22245450, cds_stop = 22250112),
  ref_label = "Non-NMD (ENST00000397802.8, 399 aa)",
  comp_label = "NMD (novel2, 231 aa)",
  events = polr3d_events,
  annotations = list(polr3d_atg, polr3d_ptc, polr3d_ref_stop),
  title = "POLR3D: Same ATG, Skipped Exon \u2192 Frameshift \u2192 PTC",
  subtitle = "Skipped exon 6 is 265 bp (265 mod 3 = 1 \u2192 +1 frameshift). ORF truncated from 399 to 231 aa.")
print(p_polr3d)
```

```{r sec2b-example-polr3d-zoom, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Zoomed view centered on the skipped exon and its consequences
p_polr3d_zoom <- plot_ucsc_pair(
  polr3d_ref_s, polr3d_ref_e, polr3d_comp_s, polr3d_comp_e, strand = "+",
  ref_cds = list(cds_start = 22245450, cds_stop = 22250518),
  comp_cds = list(cds_start = 22245450, cds_stop = 22250112),
  ref_label = "Non-NMD (399 aa)",
  comp_label = "NMD (231 aa)",
  events = polr3d_events[1, ],  # SE only
  annotations = list(
    polr3d_ptc, polr3d_ref_stop,
    list(type = "region_shade", track = "ref",
         xmin = 22249044, xmax = 22249309,
         color = "#E74C3C", alpha = 0.20,
         label = "Skipped exon (265 bp, not \u00f73)")),
  xlim = c(22248200, 22251000),
  title = "POLR3D: Zoom on Frameshift Region",
  subtitle = "Exon 6 (265 bp, red shade) is present in non-NMD, absent in NMD. 265 mod 3 \u2260 0 \u2192 downstream reading frame shifts, creating PTC.")
print(p_polr3d_zoom)
```

The zoomed view shows the critical region: exon 6 (red shading, 265 bp) is
present in the non-NMD reference but skipped in the NMD comparator. Because
265 is not divisible by 3, the downstream reading frame shifts by one
nucleotide. The new frame encounters a stop codon at position 22,250,112
(red triangle) — 406 bp before the normal stop at 22,250,518 (green triangle).
Four exon-exon junctions remain downstream, triggering NMD.

## Ruling Out Alternative NMD Mechanisms

The Stop Codon Analysis subsection characterized PTC-positive NMD isoforms. Here we investigate
the remaining PTC-negative isoforms through a systematic examination of
their structural properties, beginning with the 3'UTR and 5'UTR boundaries.

## 3'UTR Length Does Not Independently Predict NMD {#sec2c-3utr}

The prediction model (Section 3e) showed that adding 3'UTR length to the full
model does not improve holdout AUC (step 3:
`r round(unified$elastic_net$step3$auc_test, 3)` → step 4:
`r round(unified$elastic_net$step4$auc_test, 3)`), meaning 3'UTR length
carries no predictive information beyond downstream EJC count. Here we test
the long-3'UTR hypothesis directly and show that 3'UTR splicing operates
through PTC creation (EJC repositioning), not independently.

```{r goal3-identify-ptc-neg}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 all_samples profiles → cached PTC association
# ptc_c2_as = set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
#   Source: testPtcAssociation(ptc, gene-matched profiles), cached by script 03
#   $pair_summary: one row per gene-matched pair, with comp_has_ptc flag
# Step 1: Filter to coding pairs (both ref and comp in cds$coding_status == "coding")
# Step 2: Split into PTC+ and PTC- NMD comparators

ptc_c2_as <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
pair_summary <- ptc_c2_as$pair_summary

# Restrict to coding pairs (same filter as Table 2, using centralized coding_ids)
coding_pairs_c2 <- pair_summary[pair_summary$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids &
                                  pair_summary$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids, ]

n_ptc_pos <- sum(coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE)
n_ptc_neg <- sum(coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == FALSE)
ptc_neg_ids <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == FALSE]
```

Of `r fmt(nrow(coding_pairs_c2))` coding NMD pairs,
`r fmt(n_ptc_pos)` (`r round(100 * n_ptc_pos / nrow(coding_pairs_c2), 1)`%)
have a PTC and `r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` (`r round(100 * n_ptc_neg / nrow(coding_pairs_c2), 1)`%)
do not.

If the "long 3'UTR" hypothesis explains PTC-negative NMD, these comparators
should have longer 3'UTRs than Controls. However, measuring 3'UTR length in
PTC+ isoforms requires care: when a frameshift creates a premature stop, the
sequence between the PTC and the normal stop is counted as "3'UTR," inflating
the measurement. We address this by computing a corrected measurement using the
reference's stop position projected onto the comparator's exon structure.

## 3'UTR Length by PTC Mechanism

```{r goal3-fig6-pop}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: computed inline in this report using cached divergence + cds.rds
# Methods: METHODS.md § "3'UTR Length Analysis with PTC Correction"
# Key functions:
#   Isopair::quantifyPairDivergence() → div_c2/div_c4 (utr3_bp_comp column)
#   Isopair::.computeRegionalBp() → computes 3'UTR as exonic bp after cds_stop
#   Reference-based 3'UTR: computed inline using ref cds_stop on comp exon structure
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 and C4 profiles → cached divergence
# PTC mechanism classification: "same stop" vs "diff stop"
#   same_stop: comparator and reference share the same cds_stop position.
#     The PTC arises because a 3'UTR splicing event repositioned the last EJC
#     downstream, making the existing stop codon >50 nt upstream of the new EJC.
#     The 3'UTR length measurement (from cds_stop to tx end) is correct and
#     unaffected by the PTC classification.
#   diff_stop: comparator has a different cds_stop (= premature stop from
#     frameshift or in-frame stop in the CDS). The measured 3'UTR is inflated
#     because it includes the former CDS region between PTC and normal stop.
#     For these, we also compute a "reference-based 3'UTR": exonic bp downstream
#     of the REFERENCE's cds_stop in the COMPARATOR's exon structure. This is
#     only valid when the reference stop position falls within the comparator's
#     exons (86% of cases).

div_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
div_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence
ptc_pos_comp_ids <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE]

# Classify PTC+ by same vs different stop codon position
# Using centralized CDS lookups from load-data
ptc_pos_ps <- coding_pairs_c2[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE, ]
ptc_pos_ps$strand <- strand_lookup[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id]
ptc_pos_ps$comp_stop <- ifelse(ptc_pos_ps$strand == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id])
ptc_pos_ps$ref_stop <- ifelse(ptc_pos_ps$strand == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_pos_ps$reference_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_pos_ps$reference_isoform_id])
ptc_pos_ps$same_stop <- ptc_pos_ps$comp_stop == ptc_pos_ps$ref_stop

same_stop_ids <- ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == TRUE]
diff_stop_ids <- ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == FALSE]

# For diff-stop pairs, compute reference-based 3'UTR
diff_stop_ps <- ptc_pos_ps[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == FALSE, ]
ref_based_utr3 <- setNames(rep(NA_integer_, nrow(diff_stop_ps)), diff_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(diff_stop_ps))) {
  comp_id <- diff_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  ref_stop_pos <- diff_stop_ps$ref_stop[i]
  comp_strand <- strand_lookup[comp_id]
  if (is.na(comp_strand) || is.na(ref_stop_pos)) next

  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == comp_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) next
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]
  exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]

  # Check ref stop is in comparator exons
  in_exon <- any(ref_stop_pos >= exon_s & ref_stop_pos <= exon_e)
  if (!in_exon) next

  utr3 <- 0L
  for (k in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (comp_strand == "+") {
      if (exon_e[k] > ref_stop_pos) {
        post_start <- max(exon_s[k], ref_stop_pos + 1L)
        utr3 <- utr3 + as.integer(exon_e[k] - post_start + 1L)
      }
    } else {
      if (exon_s[k] < ref_stop_pos) {
        pre_end <- min(exon_e[k], ref_stop_pos - 1L)
        utr3 <- utr3 + as.integer(pre_end - exon_s[k] + 1L)
      }
    }
  }
  ref_based_utr3[comp_id] <- utr3
}

n_eligible <- sum(!is.na(ref_based_utr3))
n_ineligible <- sum(is.na(ref_based_utr3))

# Lookup for comparator 3'UTR from divergence
utr3_comp_lk <- setNames(div_c2$utr3_bp_comp, div_c2$comparator_isoform_id)

# Build 5-group data
utr3_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[same_stop_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[diff_stop_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)",
    utr3_bp = ref_based_utr3[!is.na(ref_based_utr3)]),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC-",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[ptc_neg_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
    utr3_bp = div_c4$utr3_bp_comp)
)
utr3_data <- utr3_data[!is.na(utr3_data$utr3_bp) & utr3_data$utr3_bp > 0, ]
utr3_data$group <- factor(utr3_data$group,
  levels = c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)",
             "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)",
             "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)",
             "NMD PTC-", "Control"))
utr3_n <- table(utr3_data$group)
```

PTC+ comparators are split by whether the stop codon is the **same** as the
reference (same-stop PTC+, n=`r fmt(utr3_n[[1]])`) or **different** (diff-stop
PTC+, n=`r fmt(utr3_n[[2]])`). For diff-stop pairs, 3'UTR is shown both at the
comparator's own stop (inflated) and corrected using the reference's stop
(`r fmt(n_eligible)` of `r fmt(n_eligible + n_ineligible)` eligible). NMD PTC-
(n=`r fmt(utr3_n[[4]])`) and Control (n=`r fmt(utr3_n[[5]])`) are measured at
their own stop codons.

```{r goal3-fig6-utr3-density, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

               "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)" = "#fc8d59",
               "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)" = "#fee08b",
               "NMD PTC-" = "#d9ef8b",
               "Control" = "#67a9cf")

fig6 <- ggplot(utr3_data, aes(x = utr3_bp, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal5_utr3) +
  labs(title = "3'UTR Length by PTC Mechanism",

       x = "3'UTR length (bp, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig6, "fig7_utr3_length_density", width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r goal3-table6-utr3-tests}
grps <- split(utr3_data$utr3_bp, utr3_data$group)

comparisons_list <- list(
  c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)", "Control"),
  c("Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)", "Control"),
  c("Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)", "Control"),
  c("NMD PTC-", "Control"),
  c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)", "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)")
)

tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(comparisons_list, function(pair) {
  g1 <- grps[[pair[1]]]
  g2 <- grps[[pair[2]]]
  wt <- wilcox.test(g1, g2)
  U <- as.numeric(wt$statistic)
  rbc <- 1 - (2 * U) / (length(g1) * length(g2))
  data.frame(
    group1 = gsub("\n", " ", pair[1]),
    n_group1 = length(g1), median_group1 = round(median(g1)),
    group2 = gsub("\n", " ", pair[2]),
    n_group2 = length(g2), median_group2 = round(median(g2)),
    median_diff_bp = round(median(g1) - median(g2)),
    rank_biserial_r = round(rbc, 3),
    p_value = signif(wt$p.value, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

write.csv(tests, file.path(table_dir, "table7_utr3_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **group1/group2** = the two groups being compared (see Figure 6 for
group definitions); **n_group1/n_group2** = number of isoforms in each group;
**median_group1/median_group2** = median 3'UTR length (bp);
**median_diff_bp** = difference in medians (group1 − group2);
**rank_biserial_r** = rank-biserial correlation (effect size; positive =
group1 longer); **p_value** = Wilcoxon rank-sum test p-value.

### 3'UTR Length of GENCODE-Annotated NMD vs Non-NMD Isoforms

The analyses above focus on isoform *pairs* from the gene-matched set and
stratify by PTC mechanism. Here we ask a simpler, broader question: among all
expressed GENCODE-annotated (ENST) isoforms, do NMD-sensitive isoforms have
longer 3'UTRs than non-NMD isoforms?

```{r goal3-gencode-utr3-nmd, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: cds.rds (CDS boundaries), structures.rds (exon coordinates),
#   nmd_classification.rds (NMD/non-NMD classification from mashr all_samples),
#   expression_data.rds (expressed isoforms)
# Population: all expressed GENCODE-annotated coding isoforms with valid CDS.
#   NMD: adj.P.Val < 0.05 AND logFC > 0 (mashr all_samples).
#   Non-NMD: adj.P.Val > 0.50 (mashr all_samples).
# 3'UTR: exonic bp downstream of cds_stop (strand-aware), computed from
#   SQANTI/TransDecoder2 CDS annotations via compute_sqanti_3utr().

# Identify GENCODE isoforms (ENST prefix, not novel)
nmd_ids_gc <- nmd_class$all_samples$nmd
non_nmd_ids_gc <- nmd_class$all_samples$non_nmd

# Restrict to GENCODE-annotated, coding, expressed
gencode_coding <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding" &
                                  !is_novel_iso(cds$isoform_id) &
                                  cds$isoform_id %in% rownames(expr_mat)]

gc_nmd     <- intersect(gencode_coding, nmd_ids_gc)
gc_non_nmd <- intersect(gencode_coding, non_nmd_ids_gc)

# Compute 3'UTR (exonic bp downstream of cds_stop, strand-aware)
compute_3utr_local <- function(iso_id) {
  cds_row <- cds[cds$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(cds_row) == 0 || cds_row$coding_status != "coding") return(NA_real_)
  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  strand <- cds_row$strand
  stop_pos <- if (strand == "+") cds_row$cds_stop else cds_row$cds_start
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]; exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]
  utr3 <- 0
  for (j in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (strand == "+") {
      if (exon_e[j] > stop_pos) utr3 <- utr3 + exon_e[j] - max(exon_s[j], stop_pos + 1) + 1
    } else {
      if (exon_s[j] < stop_pos) utr3 <- utr3 + min(exon_e[j], stop_pos - 1) - exon_s[j] + 1
    }
  }
  utr3
}

gc_nmd_utr3     <- sapply(gc_nmd, compute_3utr_local)
gc_non_nmd_utr3 <- sapply(gc_non_nmd, compute_3utr_local)

gc_utr3_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "NMD-sensitive",
             utr3_bp = gc_nmd_utr3[!is.na(gc_nmd_utr3) & gc_nmd_utr3 > 0]),
  data.frame(group = "Non-NMD",
             utr3_bp = gc_non_nmd_utr3[!is.na(gc_non_nmd_utr3) & gc_non_nmd_utr3 > 0])
)
gc_utr3_data$group <- factor(gc_utr3_data$group, levels = c("NMD-sensitive", "Non-NMD"))

# Wilcoxon test
gc_wt <- wilcox.test(gc_utr3_data$utr3_bp[gc_utr3_data$group == "NMD-sensitive"],
                     gc_utr3_data$utr3_bp[gc_utr3_data$group == "Non-NMD"])

gc_med <- tapply(gc_utr3_data$utr3_bp, gc_utr3_data$group, median, na.rm = TRUE)
gc_q25 <- tapply(gc_utr3_data$utr3_bp, gc_utr3_data$group, quantile, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
gc_q75 <- tapply(gc_utr3_data$utr3_bp, gc_utr3_data$group, quantile, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
gc_n   <- table(gc_utr3_data$group)

fig_gc_utr3 <- ggplot(gc_utr3_data, aes(x = utr3_bp, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD-sensitive" = "#d6604d", "Non-NMD" = "#67a9cf")) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
           label = sprintf("Wilcoxon p = %s", format.pval(gc_wt$p.value, digits = 2)),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
  labs(title = "3'UTR Length: GENCODE NMD-Sensitive vs Non-NMD Isoforms",
       subtitle = sprintf("NMD: %s bp (%s\u2013%s) n = %s | Non-NMD: %s bp (%s\u2013%s) n = %s  [median (IQR)]",
                          fmt(gc_med[["NMD-sensitive"]]), fmt(gc_q25[["NMD-sensitive"]]), fmt(gc_q75[["NMD-sensitive"]]),
                          fmt(gc_n[["NMD-sensitive"]]),
                          fmt(gc_med[["Non-NMD"]]), fmt(gc_q25[["Non-NMD"]]), fmt(gc_q75[["Non-NMD"]]),
                          fmt(gc_n[["Non-NMD"]])),
       x = "3'UTR length (bp, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = "") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_gc_utr3, "fig7c_gencode_utr3_nmd_vs_nonnmd", width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r goal3-gencode-utr3-table, echo=FALSE}
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Median 3'UTR (bp)` = round(median(utr3_bp, na.rm = TRUE)),
            `Mean 3'UTR (bp)` = round(mean(utr3_bp, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Q25 = round(quantile(utr3_bp, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
            Q75 = round(quantile(utr3_bp, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop")
```

Columns: **group** = NMD classification (NMD-sensitive = mashr adj.P.Val < 0.05
and logFC > 0; Non-NMD = adj.P.Val > 0.50); **n** = number of GENCODE coding
isoforms; **Median/Mean 3'UTR (bp)** = 3'UTR length from CDS stop to
transcript end (exonic bp only); **Q25/Q75** = interquartile range;
**Wilcoxon p** = two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test p-value.

</details>

This analysis uses all expressed GENCODE-annotated coding isoforms — not
restricted to the gene-matched pair set — to test whether NMD-sensitive
isoforms have systematically longer 3'UTRs. Unlike the pair-based analysis
above, this includes isoforms with curated GENCODE CDS annotations, avoiding
potential biases from TransDecoder2 CDS prediction on novel isoforms.

NMD-sensitive isoforms have significantly *shorter* 3'UTRs than non-NMD
isoforms (median `r fmt(gc_med[["NMD-sensitive"]])` vs
`r fmt(gc_med[["Non-NMD"]])` bp, p < 2e-16). This is the opposite of what
the long-3'UTR NMD model would predict and is consistent with the pair-based
analysis: the apparent 3'UTR lengthening in NMD isoforms is an artifact of
measuring from premature stop codons, not a genuine feature of these
transcripts.

## Illustrative Example: 3'UTR Measurement Correction (CMAS)

The CMAS gene illustrates why naive 3'UTR measurement is misleading for
PTC-positive isoforms. The NMD comparator (ENST00000534981.5) has a skipped exon
that causes a frameshift, creating a premature stop codon. When we measure 3'UTR
from this PTC, the sequence between the PTC and the normal stop is counted as
"3'UTR" — inflating the measurement by thousands of bases. The corrected
measurement uses the reference's stop codon position instead.

```{r goal3-utr3-example, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# CMAS: + strand, ref has 8 exons, comp has 7 (skipped exon 22061281-22061452)
# Same CDS start (22046304), different stop (ref: 22065311, comp: 22062284)

ref_s <- c(22046218, 22055149, 22055455, 22058567, 22060832, 22061281, 22062281, 22065121)
ref_e <- c(22046563, 22055291, 22055610, 22058700, 22060926, 22061452, 22062434, 22065668)
comp_s <- c(22046225, 22055149, 22055455, 22058567, 22060832, 22062281, 22065121)
comp_e <- c(22046563, 22055291, 22055610, 22058700, 22060926, 22062434, 22065674)

# Skipped exon event
se_event <- data.frame(
  five_prime = 22061281, three_prime = 22061452,
  event_type = "SE", direction = "LOSS")

# Annotations on a single panel:
# - PTC marker (red) on comparator at 22062284
# - Reference stop marker (green) on both tracks at 22065311
# - Shaded region: "inflated" 3'UTR (PTC to tx end) on comparator
# - Shaded region: "corrected" 3'UTR (ref stop to tx end) on comparator
ptc_marker <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "comp",
  x = 22062284, label = "PTC (comp stop)", color = "#E74C3C")
ref_stop_ref <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "ref",
  x = 22065311, label = "Stop", color = "#27AE60")
ref_stop_comp <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "comp",
  x = 22065311, label = "Ref stop", color = "#27AE60")

# Region shades to illustrate the two measurements
inflated_region <- list(type = "region_shade", track = "comp",
  xmin = 22062284, xmax = 22065311,
  color = "#E74C3C", alpha = 0.15,
  label = "Former CDS (inflates 3'UTR)")
corrected_region <- list(type = "region_shade", track = "comp",
  xmin = 22065311, xmax = 22065674,
  color = "#27AE60", alpha = 0.20,
  label = "True 3'UTR")

p <- plot_ucsc_pair(
  ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, strand = "+",
  ref_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22065311),
  comp_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22062284),
  ref_label = "Reference (ENST00000229329.7)",
  comp_label = "NMD Comparator (ENST00000534981.5)",
  events = se_event,
  annotations = list(ptc_marker, ref_stop_ref, ref_stop_comp,
                     inflated_region, corrected_region),
  title = "CMAS: Naive vs Corrected 3'UTR Measurement",
  subtitle = "Red shading = former CDS counted as 3'UTR when measured from PTC. Green = true 3'UTR from ref stop.")

print(p)
```

The skipped exon causes a frameshift that creates a PTC (red triangle).
Measuring 3'UTR from the PTC includes the red-shaded former coding sequence.
The corrected measurement (from the reference stop, green triangle) gives the
true 3'UTR. PTC-negative NMD comparators have 3'UTR lengths indistinguishable
from Control (p = `r format_p(tests$p_value[tests$group1 == "NMD PTC-"])`),
providing strong evidence against the long-3'UTR hypothesis.

## 3'UTR Splicing: PTC-Creating, Not PTC-Independent

If 3'UTR splicing triggers NMD independently, we would expect enrichment in
PTC-negative comparators. If instead it creates PTCs via EJC repositioning,
enrichment should appear only in PTC-positive comparators.

```{r goal3-utr3-splicing}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: computed inline using count_utr3_splicing() defined in this chunk
# Methods: METHODS.md § "3'UTR Splicing Enrichment"
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 and C4 profiles (detailed_events from
#   Isopair::buildProfiles() → compareSplicingChoices) + cds.rds (Isopair::extractCds)

# Strand-aware stop codon position for 3'UTR event detection
# + strand: stop = cds_stop; - strand: stop = cds_start
# Using centralized CDS lookups from load-data

count_utr3_splicing <- function(profiles, comp_id_subset = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(comp_id_subset)) {
    idx <- which(profiles$comparator_isoform_id %in% comp_id_subset)
  } else {
    idx <- seq_len(nrow(profiles))
  }
  n_with <- 0L
  n_total <- 0L
  for (i in idx) {
    comp_id <- profiles$comparator_isoform_id[i]
    de <- profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
    comp_strand <- strand_lookup[comp_id]
    comp_stop <- if (!is.na(comp_strand) && comp_strand == "-") {
      cds_start_lookup[comp_id]
    } else {
      cds_stop_lookup[comp_id]
    }
    if (is.na(comp_stop) || is.na(comp_strand)) next
    n_total <- n_total + 1L
    if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) next
    if (comp_strand == "+") {
      utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime >= comp_stop | de$three_prime >= comp_stop, ]
    } else {
      utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime <= comp_stop | de$three_prime <= comp_stop, ]
    }
    if (nrow(utr3_ev) > 0) n_with <- n_with + 1L
  }
  list(n_with = n_with, n_total = n_total,
       pct = round(100 * n_with / max(n_total, 1), 1))
}

prof_c4_as <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles

utr3_ptcneg <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c2, ptc_neg_ids)
utr3_ptcpos <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c2, ptc_pos_comp_ids)
utr3_ctrl   <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c4_as)

ft_utr3_neg <- fisher.test(matrix(c(
  utr3_ptcneg$n_with, utr3_ptcneg$n_total - utr3_ptcneg$n_with,
  utr3_ctrl$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_total - utr3_ctrl$n_with), nrow = 2))
ft_utr3_pos <- fisher.test(matrix(c(
  utr3_ptcpos$n_with, utr3_ptcpos$n_total - utr3_ptcpos$n_with,
  utr3_ctrl$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_total - utr3_ctrl$n_with), nrow = 2))

utr3_summary <- data.frame(
  group = c("NMD PTC-", "NMD PTC+", "Control"),
  n_with_utr3_event = c(utr3_ptcneg$n_with, utr3_ptcpos$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_with),
  n_total = c(utr3_ptcneg$n_total, utr3_ptcpos$n_total, utr3_ctrl$n_total),
  pct = c(utr3_ptcneg$pct, utr3_ptcpos$pct, utr3_ctrl$pct),
  vs_control_OR = c(round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_neg$estimate), 2),
                     round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_pos$estimate), 2), NA),
  vs_control_p = c(signif(ft_utr3_neg$p.value, 3),
                    signif(ft_utr3_pos$p.value, 3), NA))

kable(utr3_summary,
      caption = "3'UTR Splicing Prevalence by Group",
      col.names = c("Group", "With 3'UTR Event", "Total", "%",
                     "OR vs Control", "p vs Control"))
```

Columns: **Group**; **With 3'UTR Event** = pairs where ≥1 splice event has
coordinates in the 3'UTR (downstream of the strand-aware stop codon position);
**OR/p vs Control** = Fisher's exact test comparing to Control (C4).

```{r goal3-utr3-same-stop-verification}
# ── Direct verification: 3'UTR splicing creates PTCs via EJC repositioning ──
# For same-stop PTC+ pairs, the stop codon is identical to the reference.
# The PTC status arises because the comparator has more exon-exon junctions
# downstream of the stop codon (from 3'UTR splicing), repositioning the last EJC.
# We can verify by comparing n_downstream_ejcs between ref and comp.

same_stop_ps <- ptc_pos_ps[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == TRUE, ]
ptc_ejc_lookup <- setNames(ptc$n_downstream_ejcs, ptc$isoform_id)

same_stop_ps$comp_ejcs <- ptc_ejc_lookup[same_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id]
same_stop_ps$ref_ejcs <- ptc_ejc_lookup[same_stop_ps$reference_isoform_id]
same_stop_ps$ejc_diff <- same_stop_ps$comp_ejcs - same_stop_ps$ref_ejcs

n_comp_more_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_same_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_comp_fewer_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_valid <- sum(!is.na(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff))
```

### Verification: Same-Stop PTC+ Pairs Have More Downstream EJCs

Among `r fmt(nrow(same_stop_ps))` same-stop PTC+ pairs,
`r n_comp_more_ejcs` (`r round(100 * n_comp_more_ejcs / n_valid, 1)`%) have
more downstream EJCs in the comparator than the reference, confirming that
3'UTR splicing added junctions that repositioned the last EJC and created the
PTC. Only `r n_comp_fewer_ejcs` pairs show the opposite pattern.

### Summary: 3'UTR Mechanisms Operate Through PTC Creation

Three findings converge: (1) PTC-negative NMD comparators have 3'UTR lengths
indistinguishable from Control (Table 7); (2) same-stop PTC+ pairs confirm
3'UTR splicing creates PTCs via EJC repositioning; (3) 3'UTR splicing is
depleted in PTC-negative NMD vs Control (OR =
`r round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_neg$estimate), 2)`, p =
`r signif(ft_utr3_neg$p.value, 3)`), consistent with 3'UTR splicing being a
PTC-creating mechanism rather than an independent NMD trigger.


## 5'UTR Length and uORF Enrichment

We begin by examining the 5'UTR — the region upstream of the annotated CDS —
in the `r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` PTC-negative NMD comparators, their paired
references, and `r fmt(nrow(set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence))`
gene-matched Control (C4) comparators.

```{r sec2c-utr5-observations, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: set_results → divergence (quantifyPairDivergence output)
#   utr5_bp_ref/comp: exonic bp in 5'UTR for reference and comparator
# Population: PTC-negative NMD pairs (n = n_ptc_neg) vs Control (C4)

div_c2_all <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
div_c4_all <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence

# Subset to PTC-negative
ptc_neg_comp_ids_2c <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[!coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc]
ptc_pos_comp_ids_2c <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc]

div_ptcneg <- div_c2_all[div_c2_all$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_neg_comp_ids_2c, ]
div_ptcpos <- div_c2_all[div_c2_all$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_pos_comp_ids_2c, ]

utr5_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212 comp", utr5 = div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_comp),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212 ref", utr5 = div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_ref),
  data.frame(group = "Control comp", utr5 = div_c4_all$utr5_bp_comp))

fig_utr5 <- ggplot(utr5_data[utr5_data$utr5 > 0, ], aes(x = utr5, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD PTC\u2212 comp" = "#ef8a62",
                                "NMD PTC\u2212 ref" = "#fddbc7",
                                "Control comp" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "5\u2032UTR Length: PTC-Negative NMD Comparators vs References and Control",
       subtitle = sprintf("PTC\u2212 comparator median: %s bp | Reference median: %s bp | Control: %s bp",
                          fmt(median(div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_comp)),
                          fmt(median(div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_ref)),
                          fmt(median(div_c4_all$utr5_bp_comp))),
       x = "5\u2032UTR length (bp, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = NULL)
save_fig(fig_utr5, "fig_sec2c_utr5_length", width = 10, height = 5)
```

PTC-negative NMD comparators have substantially longer predicted 5'UTRs
(median `r fmt(median(div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_comp))` bp) than both their paired
references (`r fmt(median(div_ptcneg$utr5_bp_ref))` bp) and Control
comparators (`r fmt(median(div_c4_all$utr5_bp_comp))` bp). This raises the
question: why is the 5'UTR so much longer in these isoforms?



## The CDS Misprediction Problem (TD2 Occult-PTC Discovery)

The earlier subsections of Section 4 established that PTC-mediated NMD is the dominant mechanism
and that 3'UTR length is not an independent predictor. But nearly half of
NMD comparators are PTC-negative under the TransDecoder2 (TD2) CDS
annotation. Here we trace the cause: TD2 systematically selects the wrong
reading frame for NMD isoforms, choosing a longer ORF that avoids the PTC.
The gene's dominant non-NMD isoform provides the biologically correct
reading frame.

## Decomposing the 5'UTR Extension: TSS vs CDS Movement

The 5'UTR is bounded by the transcription start site (TSS) at the 5' end and
the CDS start at the 3' end. A longer 5'UTR could result from the TSS moving
upstream (extending the transcript) or the CDS start moving downstream
(shrinking the coding region), or both. We decompose the 5'UTR extension into
these two components for the same `r fmt(nrow(div_ptcneg))` PTC-negative pairs
and compare to `r fmt(nrow(div_c4_all))` Control pairs.

```{r sec2c-decompose-5utr, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: structures.rds (tx_start/tx_end for TSS), cds.rds (cds_start/cds_stop)
# Population: PTC-negative NMD pairs (n_ptc_neg) and Control pairs
# For each pair: compute strand-aware TSS shift and CDS shift

ptc_neg_pairs_2c <- coding_pairs_c2[!coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc, ]

ref_structs_2c <- structures[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, structures$isoform_id), ]
comp_structs_2c <- structures[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, structures$isoform_id), ]
strand_2c <- ref_structs_2c$strand

# TSS: strand-aware 5' end
ref_tss <- ifelse(strand_2c == "+", ref_structs_2c$tx_start, ref_structs_2c$tx_end)
comp_tss <- ifelse(strand_2c == "+", comp_structs_2c$tx_start, comp_structs_2c$tx_end)

# CDS start: strand-aware
ref_cds5_2c <- ifelse(cds$strand[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)] == "+",
                       cds$cds_start[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)],
                       cds$cds_stop[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)])
comp_cds5_2c <- ifelse(cds$strand[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)] == "+",
                        cds$cds_start[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)],
                        cds$cds_stop[match(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)])

# Compute exonic 5'UTR length for each isoform directly
compute_5utr_bp <- function(iso_id) {
  cds_row <- cds[cds$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(cds_row) == 0 || cds_row$coding_status != "coding") return(NA_real_)
  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  strand <- cds_row$strand
  cds5 <- if (strand == "+") cds_row$cds_start else cds_row$cds_stop
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]; exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]
  utr5 <- 0
  for (j in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (strand == "+") {
      if (exon_s[j] < cds5) utr5 <- utr5 + min(exon_e[j], cds5 - 1) - exon_s[j] + 1
    } else {
      if (exon_e[j] > cds5) utr5 <- utr5 + exon_e[j] - max(exon_s[j], cds5 + 1) + 1
    }
  }
  utr5
}

# Compute exonic 5'UTR for all relevant isoforms
all_utr5_ids <- unique(c(ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id,
                          ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id))
utr5_cache <- setNames(sapply(all_utr5_ids, compute_5utr_bp), all_utr5_ids)

# NMD PTC- pairs: exonic 5'UTR difference (comp - ref)
nmd_ref_5utr <- utr5_cache[ptc_neg_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id]
nmd_comp_5utr <- utr5_cache[ptc_neg_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id]
nmd_5utr_diff <- nmd_comp_5utr - nmd_ref_5utr

# Control pairs
c4_pairs_2c <- profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]]
c4_utr5_ids <- unique(c(c4_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id,
                          c4_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id))
c4_utr5_ids_new <- setdiff(c4_utr5_ids, names(utr5_cache))
if (length(c4_utr5_ids_new) > 0) {
  utr5_cache <- c(utr5_cache, setNames(sapply(c4_utr5_ids_new, compute_5utr_bp), c4_utr5_ids_new))
}
c4_ref_5utr <- utr5_cache[c4_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id]
c4_comp_5utr <- utr5_cache[c4_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id]
c4_5utr_diff <- c4_comp_5utr - c4_ref_5utr

wt_5utr <- wilcox.test(nmd_5utr_diff, c4_5utr_diff)

cat("Exonic 5'UTR difference (comp - ref):\n")
cat("  NMD PTC- median:", round(median(nmd_5utr_diff, na.rm = TRUE)), "bp\n")
cat("  Control median:", round(median(c4_5utr_diff, na.rm = TRUE)), "bp\n")
cat("  Wilcoxon p:", signif(wt_5utr$p.value, 3), "\n")

# Also compute genomic TSS and CDS shifts for decomposition context
tss_shift <- ifelse(strand_2c == "+",
  as.numeric(ref_tss) - as.numeric(comp_tss),
  as.numeric(comp_tss) - as.numeric(ref_tss))
cds_shift <- ifelse(strand_2c == "+",
  as.numeric(comp_cds5_2c) - as.numeric(ref_cds5_2c),
  as.numeric(ref_cds5_2c) - as.numeric(comp_cds5_2c))

# Figure: three-panel — exonic 5'UTR difference + genomic TSS/CDS shifts
shift_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "Exonic 5\u2032UTR\n(comp \u2212 ref)",
             shift = nmd_5utr_diff),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "Exonic 5\u2032UTR\n(comp \u2212 ref)",
             shift = c4_5utr_diff),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "Genomic TSS shift\n(upstream = extends)",
             shift = tss_shift),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "Genomic TSS shift\n(upstream = extends)",
             shift = c4_5utr_diff * NA),  # placeholder — compute below
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "Genomic CDS shift\n(downstream = extends)",
             shift = cds_shift),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "Genomic CDS shift\n(downstream = extends)",
             shift = c4_5utr_diff * NA))  # placeholder

# Properly compute control genomic shifts
c4_ref_s <- structures[match(c4_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, structures$isoform_id), ]
c4_comp_s <- structures[match(c4_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, structures$isoform_id), ]
c4_strand <- c4_ref_s$strand

c4_ref_tss <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+", c4_ref_s$tx_start, c4_ref_s$tx_end)
c4_comp_tss <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+", c4_comp_s$tx_start, c4_comp_s$tx_end)
c4_tss_shift <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+",
  as.numeric(c4_ref_tss) - as.numeric(c4_comp_tss),
  as.numeric(c4_comp_tss) - as.numeric(c4_ref_tss))

c4_ref_cds5 <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+",
  cds$cds_start[match(c4_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)],
  cds$cds_stop[match(c4_pairs_2c$reference_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)])
c4_comp_cds5 <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+",
  cds$cds_start[match(c4_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)],
  cds$cds_stop[match(c4_pairs_2c$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id)])
c4_cds_shift <- ifelse(c4_strand == "+",
  as.numeric(c4_comp_cds5) - as.numeric(c4_ref_cds5),
  as.numeric(c4_ref_cds5) - as.numeric(c4_comp_cds5))

# --- Figure 1: Exonic distances ---
# Compute exonic TSS and CDS contributions to the 5'UTR difference
# TSS contribution = exonic bp upstream of ref CDS5 in comp but not ref
# CDS contribution = exonic bp between ref CDS5 and comp CDS5
# These are not easily decomposed additively, so show all three exonic
# measures separately: total 5'UTR diff, ref 5'UTR, comp 5'UTR

exonic_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "5\u2032UTR diff\n(comp \u2212 ref)",
             shift = nmd_5utr_diff),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "5\u2032UTR diff\n(comp \u2212 ref)",
             shift = c4_5utr_diff),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "Ref 5\u2032UTR",
             shift = nmd_ref_5utr),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "Ref 5\u2032UTR",
             shift = c4_ref_5utr),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC\u2212",
             panel = "Comp 5\u2032UTR",
             shift = nmd_comp_5utr),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             panel = "Comp 5\u2032UTR",
             shift = c4_comp_5utr))

exonic_data$panel <- factor(exonic_data$panel,
  levels = c("Ref 5\u2032UTR", "Comp 5\u2032UTR", "5\u2032UTR diff\n(comp \u2212 ref)"))

exonic_data$shift_trunc <- pmin(pmax(exonic_data$shift, -5000), 5000)
n_trunc_exonic <- sum(abs(exonic_data$shift) > 5000, na.rm = TRUE)

fig_exonic <- ggplot(exonic_data, aes(x = group, y = shift_trunc, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD PTC\u2212" = "#ef8a62", "Control" = "#67a9cf")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Exonic 5\u2032UTR: PTC-Negative NMD vs Control",
       subtitle = sprintf("PTC\u2212 (n=%s) vs Control (n=%s) | Exonic bp only | Truncated at \u00b15 kb (%d clipped)",
                          fmt(nrow(ptc_neg_pairs_2c)), fmt(nrow(c4_pairs_2c)), n_trunc_exonic),
       x = NULL, y = "Exonic bp", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
save_fig(fig_exonic, "fig_sec2c_exonic_5utr", width = 10, height = 5)
```

PTC-negative NMD comparators have a median exonic 5'UTR
`r round(median(nmd_5utr_diff, na.rm = TRUE))` bp longer than their paired
references (p = `r format_p(wt_5utr$p.value)` vs Control). The genomic
decomposition (second figure) shows where this extension comes from: the TSS
moves modestly upstream (median `r round(median(tss_shift, na.rm = TRUE))` bp
genomic), while the CDS start moves substantially downstream (median
`r fmt(round(median(cds_shift, na.rm = TRUE)))` bp genomic). **The longer
5'UTR is driven primarily by a downstream shift in the predicted CDS start,
not by an upstream shift in transcription start.**

This raises the next question: why did the CDS prediction move downstream?

## The Reference ATG Is Still Present

Of the `r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` PTC-negative pairs,
`r fmt(sum(ref_cds5_2c != comp_cds5_2c, na.rm = TRUE))`
(`r round(100 * mean(ref_cds5_2c != comp_cds5_2c, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`%) have a
different predicted CDS start than their reference. We ask: has the reference's
CDS start ATG been lost from the comparator, or is it still present in shared
exonic sequence?

```{r sec2c-ref-atg-load}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Reference-ATG Tracing (PTC-Negative Reclassification)"
# Source: 05r_ref_atg_analysis.R → ref_atg_analysis.rds
# Population: All PTC-negative coding pairs (n = n_ptc_neg)
# For each pair: checks whether the reference CDS start ATG position is
# exonic in the comparator, then traces the reading frame to find the
# first in-frame stop and counts downstream EJCs.

ref_atg <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "ref_atg_analysis.rds"))
c2_ref <- ref_atg$c2
c4_ref <- ref_atg$c4

ptc_neg_ref <- c2_ref[!c2_ref$original_ptc, ]

n_atg_avail <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
n_atg_lost_2c <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Canonical subgroup assignment ──
# Two-pass reclassification:
#   Pass 1 (ref-ATG tracing): effectively_ptc → PTC+
#   Pass 2 (TD2 fallback): ref_atg_lost with ptc$n_downstream_ejcs > 0 → PTC+
# Remaining groups:
#   no_downstream_ejc + truncated_no_ejc → NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained
#   ref_atg_lost (TD2 EJC == 0) + rare categories → NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost

# TD2 second-pass: check downstream EJCs from TD2 CDS for ref_atg_lost pairs
td2_ejc_lookup <- setNames(ptc$n_downstream_ejcs, ptc$isoform_id)
ref_lost_cats <- c("ref_atg_lost", "not_atg_in_ref", "no_stop_in_comp")
is_ref_lost <- ptc_neg_ref$category %in% ref_lost_cats
td2_ejc_vals <- td2_ejc_lookup[ptc_neg_ref$comparator_isoform_id[is_ref_lost]]
stopifnot("All ref_atg_lost comparators found in ptc.rds" =
            all(ptc_neg_ref$comparator_isoform_id[is_ref_lost] %in% ptc$isoform_id))
td2_reclass_mask <- is_ref_lost & td2_ejc_lookup[ptc_neg_ref$comparator_isoform_id] > 0
n_td2_reclass <- sum(td2_reclass_mask, na.rm = TRUE)

ptc_neg_ref$subgroup <- case_when(
  ptc_neg_ref$category == "effectively_ptc" ~ "NMD PTC+",
  td2_reclass_mask ~ "NMD PTC+",
  ptc_neg_ref$category %in% c("no_downstream_ejc", "truncated_no_ejc") ~
    "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
  ptc_neg_ref$category %in% ref_lost_cats ~ "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost",
  TRUE ~ "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"
)

# subgroup_detail preserves the original split within ref ATG retained
ptc_neg_ref$subgroup_detail <- case_when(
  ptc_neg_ref$subgroup == "NMD PTC+" ~ "NMD PTC+",
  ptc_neg_ref$category == "no_downstream_ejc" ~ "No downstream EJC",
  ptc_neg_ref$category == "truncated_no_ejc" ~ "Truncated, no EJC",
  ptc_neg_ref$subgroup == "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost" ~ "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost",
  TRUE ~ ptc_neg_ref$category
)

# Canonical palette (matching Report 2)
subgroup_pal <- c("NMD PTC+" = "#ef8a62",
                  "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained" = "#fdd49e",
                  "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost" = "#fdbb84",
                  "Control" = "#67a9cf")

# Convenience counts
n_subgroup_ptcplus <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$subgroup == "NMD PTC+")
n_subgroup_retained <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$subgroup == "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained")
n_subgroup_lost <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$subgroup == "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost")

n_refatg_reclass <- sum(ptc_neg_ref$category == "effectively_ptc")

cat(sprintf("Canonical subgroup assignment (PTC-negative pairs, n = %d):\n", nrow(ptc_neg_ref)))
cat(sprintf("  NMD PTC+ (ref-ATG + TD2 reclass): %d (%d ref-ATG + %d TD2)\n",
            n_subgroup_ptcplus, n_refatg_reclass, n_td2_reclass))
cat(sprintf("  NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained: %d\n", n_subgroup_retained))
cat(sprintf("  NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost: %d\n", n_subgroup_lost))
```

Of the `r fmt(sum(ref_cds5_2c != comp_cds5_2c, na.rm = TRUE))` pairs with a
different CDS start, `r fmt(n_atg_avail - sum(ref_cds5_2c == comp_cds5_2c, na.rm = TRUE))`
retain the reference ATG in shared exonic sequence. Together with the
`r fmt(sum(ref_cds5_2c == comp_cds5_2c, na.rm = TRUE))` pairs that share the
same CDS start (where the reference ATG is present by definition), a total of
`r fmt(n_atg_avail)` of `r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` PTC-negative pairs
(`r round(100 * n_atg_avail / n_ptc_neg, 1)`%) have the reference ATG
available in the comparator. The ATG was not lost in these cases — the CDS
prediction algorithm simply selected a different start codon.

CDS annotations come from SQANTI3's TransDecoder2 (TD2) pipeline, which
selects ORFs using PSAURON (a neural network coding potential scorer) and a
length-based false discovery rate filter. When a frameshift creates a premature
stop codon, the truncated ORF scores lower, and TD2 selects a longer
alternative in a different reading frame.

## Reference-ATG Tracing Reveals Hidden PTCs

For the `r fmt(n_atg_avail)` PTC-negative pairs where the reference ATG is
available (see above), we trace the reference reading frame through the
comparator's transcript — finding the first in-frame stop codon and counting
downstream EJCs.

```{r sec2c-ref-atg-density, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}

atg_avail <- ptc_neg_ref[ptc_neg_ref$category == "effectively_ptc", ]

fig_ratio <- ggplot(atg_avail, aes(x = orf_ratio)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#ef8a62", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(atg_avail$orf_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
             color = "#d62728", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = median(atg_avail$orf_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), y = Inf,
           label = sprintf("median = %.2f", median(atg_avail$orf_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)),
           vjust = 2, hjust = -0.1, color = "#d62728", size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2), breaks = seq(0, 2, 0.25)) +
  labs(title = "ORF Truncation: Reference ATG Traced Through PTC\u2212 Comparators",
       subtitle = sprintf("Effectively-PTC cases (n = %s of %s with ref ATG available) | Ratio < 1 = truncated",
                          fmt(nrow(atg_avail)), fmt(n_atg_avail)),
       x = "ORF length ratio (comparator / reference)", y = "Density")
save_fig(fig_ratio, "fig_sec2c_ref_atg_orf_ratio", width = 10, height = 5)
```

## Reference ATG Provenance and Kozak Context

The reclassification depends on the reference isoform's CDS start ATG. For
GENCODE-annotated (ENST) reference isoforms, this ATG derives from curated
CDS annotation; for novel isoforms, it comes from TD2 prediction.

```{r sec2c-kozak-context}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Reference-ATG Tracing (PTC-Negative Reclassification)"
# Source: eff_ptc reference isoform IDs, corrected FASTA, structures.rds, cds.rds
# Population: reference isoforms of reclassified effectively-PTC pairs

# ENST vs novel composition
eff_ptc$ref_is_novel <- grepl("\\.novel\\d+$", eff_ptc$reference_isoform_id)
n_ref_enst <- sum(!eff_ptc$ref_is_novel)
n_ref_novel <- sum(eff_ptc$ref_is_novel)

cat(sprintf("Reference isoform provenance (n=%d reclassified pairs):\n", nrow(eff_ptc)))
cat(sprintf("  ENST (GENCODE): %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_ref_enst, 100 * n_ref_enst / nrow(eff_ptc)))
cat(sprintf("  Novel (TD2 CDS): %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_ref_novel, 100 * n_ref_novel / nrow(eff_ptc)))

# Kozak context: extract 7-nt window around ATG from FASTA
# Kozak: position -3 (A/G = strong), position +4 (G = strong)
# Strong = both; Adequate = one; Weak = neither
FASTA_PATH <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/sqanti/nmd_lungcells/results/nmd_lungcells_corrected.fasta"

# Map ref ATG genomic → transcript position, extract sequence context
genomic_to_transcript_local <- function(genomic_pos, exon_starts, exon_ends, strand) {
  if (strand == "-") { exon_starts <- rev(exon_starts); exon_ends <- rev(exon_ends) }
  cum <- 0L
  for (j in seq_along(exon_starts)) {
    es <- exon_starts[j]; ee <- exon_ends[j]
    if (strand == "+") {
      if (genomic_pos >= es && genomic_pos <= ee) return(cum + (genomic_pos - es) + 1L)
    } else {
      if (genomic_pos >= es && genomic_pos <= ee) return(cum + (ee - genomic_pos) + 1L)
    }
    cum <- cum + (ee - es + 1L)
  }
  NA_integer_
}

# Load sequences for reference isoforms
ref_ids <- unique(eff_ptc$reference_isoform_id)
id_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines(ref_ids, id_file)
awk_cmd <- sprintf(
  "awk 'BEGIN{while((getline id < \"%s\") > 0) want[id]=1} /^>/{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq; hdr=substr($1,2); found=(hdr in want); seq=\"\"; next} found{seq=seq$0} END{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq}' '%s'",
  id_file, FASTA_PATH)
raw <- system(awk_cmd, intern = TRUE)
unlink(id_file)
split_lines <- strsplit(raw, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
seq_vec <- setNames(toupper(vapply(split_lines, `[`, character(1), 2)),
                     vapply(split_lines, `[`, character(1), 1))

# For each reference, extract Kozak context at its CDS start
kozak_results <- data.frame(
  ref_id = eff_ptc$reference_isoform_id,
  is_novel = eff_ptc$ref_is_novel,
  kozak_class = NA_character_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(eff_ptc))) {
  ref_id <- eff_ptc$reference_isoform_id[i]
  ref_atg_g <- eff_ptc$ref_atg_genomic[i]
  strand <- eff_ptc$strand[i]
  if (is.na(ref_atg_g) || !ref_id %in% names(seq_vec)) next

  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == ref_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) next

  tx_pos <- genomic_to_transcript_local(ref_atg_g, str_row$exon_starts[[1]],
                                         str_row$exon_ends[[1]], strand)
  if (is.na(tx_pos)) next

  seq_i <- seq_vec[ref_id]
  # Extract positions: -3 is at tx_pos - 3, +4 is at tx_pos + 3 (0-indexed: A=0, T=1, G=2)
  if (tx_pos < 4 || tx_pos + 3 > nchar(seq_i)) next

  pos_minus3 <- substr(seq_i, tx_pos - 3, tx_pos - 3)
  pos_plus4 <- substr(seq_i, tx_pos + 3, tx_pos + 3)

  strong_m3 <- pos_minus3 %in% c("A", "G")
  strong_p4 <- pos_plus4 == "G"

  if (strong_m3 && strong_p4) {
    kozak_results$kozak_class[i] <- "Strong"
  } else if (strong_m3 || strong_p4) {
    kozak_results$kozak_class[i] <- "Adequate"
  } else {
    kozak_results$kozak_class[i] <- "Weak"
  }
}

kozak_results$kozak_class <- factor(kozak_results$kozak_class,
                                     levels = c("Strong", "Adequate", "Weak"))

# Summary by ENST vs novel
kozak_tab <- kozak_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(kozak_class)) %>%
  mutate(source = ifelse(is_novel, "Novel (TD2)", "ENST (GENCODE)")) %>%
  count(source, kozak_class) %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

render_dt(kozak_tab, caption = "Kozak Context at Reference ATG by CDS Source")
```

Columns: **source** = ENST (GENCODE-annotated) or Novel (TD2-predicted CDS);
**kozak_class** = Strong (A/G at -3 AND G at +4), Adequate (one match), or
Weak (neither); **n** = count; **pct** = percentage within source group.

`r n_ref_enst` (`r round(100 * n_ref_enst / nrow(eff_ptc), 1)`%) of the
reference isoforms are GENCODE-annotated, whose CDS start is curated. The
remaining `r n_ref_novel` (`r round(100 * n_ref_novel / nrow(eff_ptc), 1)`%)
are novel isoforms with TD2-predicted CDS. Both groups show predominantly
strong or adequate Kozak context at the reference ATG, consistent with
biologically active translation initiation sites. ENST references have
slightly stronger Kozak context than novel references, as expected from
curated annotation.

### Reference ATG vs TD2 ATG: Kozak Comparison in NMD Comparators

Of the `r fmt(nrow(ptc_neg_ref[ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE &
!is.na(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp), ]))` PTC-negative NMD
comparators where the reference ATG is exonic, `r { comp_cds_sec2c <- cds[match(ptc_neg_ref$comparator_isoform_id[ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE & !is.na(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp)], cds$isoform_id), ]; td2_5p <- ifelse(comp_cds_sec2c$strand == "+", comp_cds_sec2c$cds_start, comp_cds_sec2c$cds_stop); ref_5p <- ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_genomic[ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE & !is.na(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp)]; fmt(sum(ref_5p != td2_5p, na.rm = TRUE)) }`
use a different CDS start than their reference. For these pairs, the
ribosome faces two candidate ATGs: the reference ATG (used by the gene's
dominant non-NMD isoform) and the TD2-predicted ATG (selected by the CDS
prediction algorithm for ORF length). We compare their Kozak initiation
context to assess which is more likely to be used by scanning ribosomes.

```{r sec2c-kozak-comparison, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: corrected FASTA (transcript sequences), cds.rds (TD2 CDS),
#   ref_atg_analysis.rds (reference ATG positions), structures.rds
# Population: PTC-negative NMD comparators with ref ATG available AND
#   different TD2 CDS start (n pairs where ref ATG != TD2 ATG)

# Structure lookup (for coordinate conversion)
structs_lookup <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(structures)), function(i)
    list(starts = structures$exon_starts[[i]], ends = structures$exon_ends[[i]])),
  structures$isoform_id)

# Identify pairs with different ATGs
ptc_neg_avail <- ptc_neg_ref[ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE &
                               !is.na(ptc_neg_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp), ]
comp_cds_koz <- cds[match(ptc_neg_avail$comparator_isoform_id, cds$isoform_id), ]
td2_atg_koz <- ifelse(comp_cds_koz$strand == "+", comp_cds_koz$cds_start, comp_cds_koz$cds_stop)
diff_atg_mask <- ptc_neg_avail$ref_atg_genomic != td2_atg_koz & !is.na(td2_atg_koz)
diff_pairs_koz <- ptc_neg_avail[diff_atg_mask, ]
diff_td2_atg <- td2_atg_koz[diff_atg_mask]

# Load comparator sequences
comp_ids_koz <- unique(diff_pairs_koz$comparator_isoform_id)
id_file_koz <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines(comp_ids_koz, id_file_koz)
awk_koz <- sprintf(
  "awk 'BEGIN{while((getline id < \"%s\") > 0) want[id]=1} /^>/{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq; hdr=substr($1,2); found=(hdr in want); seq=\"\"; next} found{seq=seq$0} END{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq}' '%s'",
  id_file_koz, FASTA_PATH)
raw_koz <- system(awk_koz, intern = TRUE)
unlink(id_file_koz)
split_koz <- strsplit(raw_koz, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
seq_koz <- setNames(toupper(vapply(split_koz, `[`, character(1), 2)),
                      vapply(split_koz, `[`, character(1), 1))

# Score Kozak for both ATGs in each pair
kozak_score_fn <- function(seq_str, tx_pos) {
  if (is.na(tx_pos) || tx_pos < 4 || tx_pos + 3 > nchar(seq_str)) return(NA_character_)
  if (substr(seq_str, tx_pos, tx_pos + 2) != "ATG") return(NA_character_)
  m3 <- substr(seq_str, tx_pos - 3, tx_pos - 3)
  p4 <- substr(seq_str, tx_pos + 3, tx_pos + 3)
  if (m3 %in% c("A","G") && p4 == "G") "Strong"
  else if (m3 %in% c("A","G") || p4 == "G") "Adequate"
  else "Weak"
}

ref_kozak_vec <- character(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))
td2_kozak_vec <- character(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))

for (k in seq_len(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))) {
  cid <- diff_pairs_koz$comparator_isoform_id[k]
  strand_k <- diff_pairs_koz$strand[k]
  if (!cid %in% names(seq_koz)) { ref_kozak_vec[k] <- NA; td2_kozak_vec[k] <- NA; next }
  cs <- structs_lookup[[cid]]
  if (is.null(cs)) { ref_kozak_vec[k] <- NA; td2_kozak_vec[k] <- NA; next }

  ref_tx <- genomic_to_transcript_local(diff_pairs_koz$ref_atg_genomic[k],
                                          cs$starts, cs$ends, strand_k)
  td2_tx <- genomic_to_transcript_local(diff_td2_atg[k], cs$starts, cs$ends, strand_k)

  ref_kozak_vec[k] <- kozak_score_fn(seq_koz[cid], ref_tx)
  td2_kozak_vec[k] <- kozak_score_fn(seq_koz[cid], td2_tx)
}

# Kozak PWM score using Isopair::scoreKozakPWM (log-odds across 8 positions)
# Matches the scoring used in orf_model_report_v5 Section 6.4
ref_tx_pos <- integer(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))
td2_tx_pos <- integer(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))
pwm_seqs <- character(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))

for (k in seq_len(nrow(diff_pairs_koz))) {
  cid <- diff_pairs_koz$comparator_isoform_id[k]
  strand_k <- diff_pairs_koz$strand[k]
  if (!cid %in% names(seq_koz)) { ref_tx_pos[k] <- NA; td2_tx_pos[k] <- NA; next }
  cs <- structs_lookup[[cid]]
  if (is.null(cs)) { ref_tx_pos[k] <- NA; td2_tx_pos[k] <- NA; next }
  ref_tx_pos[k] <- genomic_to_transcript_local(diff_pairs_koz$ref_atg_genomic[k],
                                                 cs$starts, cs$ends, strand_k)
  td2_tx_pos[k] <- genomic_to_transcript_local(diff_td2_atg[k], cs$starts, cs$ends, strand_k)
  pwm_seqs[k] <- seq_koz[cid]
}

# Score both ATGs using Isopair's log-odds PWM
valid_ref <- !is.na(ref_tx_pos) & pwm_seqs != ""
valid_td2 <- !is.na(td2_tx_pos) & pwm_seqs != ""

ref_pwm <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(diff_pairs_koz))
td2_pwm <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(diff_pairs_koz))

if (sum(valid_ref) > 0) {
  ref_result <- Isopair::scoreKozakPWM(pwm_seqs[valid_ref], ref_tx_pos[valid_ref])
  ref_pwm[valid_ref] <- ref_result$score
}
if (sum(valid_td2) > 0) {
  td2_result <- Isopair::scoreKozakPWM(pwm_seqs[valid_td2], td2_tx_pos[valid_td2])
  td2_pwm[valid_td2] <- td2_result$score
}

koz_valid <- !is.na(ref_pwm) & !is.na(td2_pwm)
n_koz_valid <- sum(koz_valid)

# Boxplot of numeric Kozak PWM scores
koz_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(ATG_source = "Reference ATG", score = ref_pwm[koz_valid]),
  data.frame(ATG_source = "TD2-predicted ATG", score = td2_pwm[koz_valid]))
koz_df$ATG_source <- factor(koz_df$ATG_source,
  levels = c("Reference ATG", "TD2-predicted ATG"))

wt_koz <- wilcox.test(ref_pwm[koz_valid], td2_pwm[koz_valid], paired = TRUE)

fig_kozak <- ggplot(koz_df, aes(x = ATG_source, y = score, fill = ATG_source)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7, width = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Reference ATG" = "#4393c3",
                                "TD2-predicted ATG" = "#ef8a62")) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = max(koz_df$score, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.3,
           label = sprintf("paired Wilcoxon p = %s", signif(wt_koz$p.value, 3)),
           size = 4.5) +
  labs(title = "Kozak Initiation Context Score: Reference vs TD2-Predicted ATG",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s NMD comparators with different ref and TD2 start codons | Isopair scoreKozakPWM (log-odds)",
                          fmt(n_koz_valid)),
       x = NULL, y = "Kozak PWM score (log-odds)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", text = element_text(size = 14))
save_fig(fig_kozak, "fig_sec2c_kozak_ref_vs_td2", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec2c-kozak-comparison-stats}
ref_median <- round(median(ref_pwm[koz_valid]), 1)
td2_median <- round(median(td2_pwm[koz_valid]), 1)
pct_ref_higher <- round(100 * mean(ref_pwm[koz_valid] > td2_pwm[koz_valid]), 1)
```

Among `r fmt(n_koz_valid)` pairs where the reference and TD2 ATGs differ,
the reference ATG has a median Kozak score of `r ref_median` versus
`r td2_median` for the TD2 ATG (paired Wilcoxon p =
`r signif(wt_koz$p.value, 3)`). The reference ATG scores higher in
`r pct_ref_higher`% of pairs. The Kozak PWM score (`Isopair::scoreKozakPWM`)
computes log-odds across 8 positions (-6 to +5) relative to a background
nucleotide frequency model; positive values indicate stronger-than-average
initiation context, and the same scoring function is used in the external CNN
model report (`orf_model_report_v5`, §6.4). TD2
selects ATGs that maximize ORF length, not initiation context --- the
reference ATG, used by the gene's dominant isoform, has substantially
stronger Kozak context and is more likely to be the biologically active
start codon.



## Updated PTC Accounting

With the reference-ATG reclassification complete, we can now provide a
comprehensive accounting of PTC-mediated NMD. The reclassified pairs
show the same splice event patterns and NMD response magnitudes as the
originally PTC-positive pairs, confirming they are genuine PTCs that TD2
failed to identify.

## PTC-Causing Mechanisms in Reclassified Pairs

The `r fmt(nrow(eff_ptc))` reclassified pairs share the reference ATG — any
PTC must arise from splice events between the ATG and the premature stop.
We attribute PTC-causing events using the same three-mechanism framework as
the PTC-Causing Splice Events subsection of Section 4 (see METHODS.md § "PTC-Causing Event Attribution"):

1. **Frameshift**: `analyzeFrameWalk()` identifies splice events between the
   shared ATG and the premature stop that shift the reading frame
   (`Isopair::analyzeFrameWalk`, cached as `fw_c2_allsamples.rds`)
2. **In-frame stop**: a splice event introduces exonic sequence containing a
   stop codon in the original reading frame (event coordinates contain the
   premature stop position)

```{r sec2c-ptc-attribution, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds → attr_mechanism + attr_event columns
# Population: reclassified effectively-PTC pairs (originally PTC-)
# Methods: METHODS.md § "PTC-Causing Event Attribution"
# Three-mechanism attribution using same analyzeFrameWalk() + coordinate
# containment approach as Section 4 mechanism analysis. All three mechanisms (frameshift,
# in-frame stop, 3'UTR splice) apply to the reclassified population.

reclass_attr <- c2_ref[c2_ref$category == "effectively_ptc" & !c2_ref$original_ptc, ]
reclass_attr <- reclass_attr[!is.na(reclass_attr$attr_mechanism), ]

# Build attribution table matching Section 4 mechanism-attribution format
attr_df <- reclass_attr %>%
  filter(attr_mechanism != "unresolved") %>%
  group_by(attr_mechanism, attr_event) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(attr_mechanism, desc(n))

n_attr_total <- sum(attr_df$n)
n_attr_fs <- sum(attr_df$n[attr_df$attr_mechanism == "Frameshift"])
n_attr_ifs <- sum(attr_df$n[attr_df$attr_mechanism == "In-frame stop"])
n_attr_3utr <- sum(attr_df$n[attr_df$attr_mechanism == "3'UTR splice"])
n_attr_unres <- sum(reclass_attr$attr_mechanism == "unresolved")

# Shorten event type labels and collapse rare types (shared function)
attr_df$event_short <- shorten_event_labels(attr_df$attr_event)
# Collapse rare types within the aggregated counts
evt_counts <- tapply(attr_df$n, attr_df$event_short, sum)
rare <- names(evt_counts[evt_counts < 3])
attr_df$event_short[attr_df$event_short %in% rare] <- "Other"

# Re-aggregate after collapsing
sankey_agg <- attr_df %>%
  group_by(event_short, attr_mechanism) %>%
  summarise(freq = sum(n), .groups = "drop")

mech_colors_reclass <- c("Frameshift" = "#d6604d",
                          "In-frame stop" = "#4393c3",
                          "3'UTR splice" = "#66c2a5")

# Interactive Sankey (HTML only)
nodes_vec_r <- unique(c(sankey_agg$event_short, sankey_agg$attr_mechanism))
nodes_r <- data.frame(name = nodes_vec_r, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
links_r <- data.frame(
  source = match(sankey_agg$event_short, nodes_vec_r) - 1L,
  target = match(sankey_agg$attr_mechanism, nodes_vec_r) - 1L,
  value  = sankey_agg$freq)
node_colors_r <- ifelse(nodes_r$name %in% names(mech_colors_reclass),
                         mech_colors_reclass[nodes_r$name], "#bdbdbd")
color_scale_r <- paste0(
  'd3.scaleOrdinal().domain([',
  paste0('"', nodes_r$name, '"', collapse = ','), ']).range([',
  paste0('"', node_colors_r, '"', collapse = ','), '])')
networkD3::sankeyNetwork(
  Links = links_r, Nodes = nodes_r,
  Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value",
  NodeID = "name", fontSize = 14, nodeWidth = 30, nodePadding = 15,
  colourScale = color_scale_r, sinksRight = TRUE)

# Static stacked bar chart (saves as PNG/PDF for paper)
evt_totals_r <- sankey_agg %>%
  group_by(event_short) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(total)
sankey_agg$event_short <- factor(sankey_agg$event_short, levels = evt_totals_r$event_short)
sankey_agg$attr_mechanism <- factor(sankey_agg$attr_mechanism,
  levels = c("Frameshift", "In-frame stop", "3'UTR splice"))

fig_sankey_reclass <- ggplot(sankey_agg,
    aes(x = freq, y = event_short, fill = attr_mechanism)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(freq >= 10, fmt(freq), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.8, color = "white",
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mech_colors_reclass) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "PTC-Causing Splice Events (Reclassified Pairs)",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s attributed pairs | Stacked by mechanism",
                          fmt(sum(sankey_agg$freq))),
       x = "Number of pairs", y = NULL, fill = "Mechanism") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 14))
save_fig(fig_sankey_reclass, "fig_sankey_reclass", width = 10, height = 7)
```

**Frameshift** (red; `r fmt(n_attr_fs)` pairs,
`r round(100 * n_attr_fs / n_attr_total, 1)`%), **In-frame stop** (blue;
`r fmt(n_attr_ifs)`, `r round(100 * n_attr_ifs / n_attr_total, 1)`%),
and **3'UTR splice** (`r fmt(n_attr_3utr)` pairs,
`r round(100 * n_attr_3utr / n_attr_total, 1)`% — reclassified pairs with
same or longer ORFs whose PTC arises from a splice event in the 3'UTR
introducing a downstream EJC).
`r fmt(n_attr_total)` of `r fmt(nrow(eff_ptc))` reclassified pairs are
directly attributed; `r fmt(n_attr_unres)` remain unresolved
(`r round(100 * n_attr_unres / nrow(eff_ptc), 1)`%). Most reclassified pairs
have truncated ORFs (frameshift or in-frame stop), but a subset use the same
3'UTR splice mechanism seen in the original PTC+ group.

The event type distribution mirrors the Section 4 PTC-Causing Splice Events subsection: SE dominates both
mechanisms, followed by A3SS and A5SS for frameshifts. This confirms that
the reclassified pairs arise from the same biological processes as the
original PTC+ pairs — the difference is purely which CDS the prediction
algorithm selected.

## Reclassified Pairs Have the Same Splicing Patterns as PTC+

If the `r fmt(nrow(eff_ptc))` reclassified pairs are truly PTC-positive
isoforms misclassified by CDS prediction, their splicing patterns should
resemble the original `r fmt(n_ptc_pos)` PTC+ pairs. We compare splice event
proportions between these two groups.

```{r sec2c-reclass-events, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: profiles_list C2 (reclassified pairs vs original PTC+ pairs)
# Population: reclassified effectively-PTC vs original PTC+
# Analysis: splice event type proportions, paired dodged bars

eff_ptc_profiles <- profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]] %>%
  filter(comparator_isoform_id %in% eff_ptc$comparator_isoform_id)

nmd_reclass_events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(eff_ptc_profiles)), function(i) {
  de <- eff_ptc_profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
  de[, c("event_type", "direction", "bp_diff")]
}))

# Original PTC+ events for comparison
ptc_pos_profiles <- profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]] %>%
  filter(comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc])

ptcpos_events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ptc_pos_profiles)), function(i) {
  de <- ptc_pos_profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
  de[, c("event_type", "direction", "bp_diff")]
}))

# Also get Control for three-way comparison
ctrl_profiles_sec2c <- profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]] %>%
  filter(reference_isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"],
         comparator_isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"])

ctrl_events_sec2c <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ctrl_profiles_sec2c)), function(i) {
  de <- ctrl_profiles_sec2c$detailed_events[[i]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
  de[, c("event_type", "direction", "bp_diff")]
}))

n_nmd_events <- nrow(nmd_reclass_events)
n_ptcpos_events <- nrow(ptcpos_events)
n_ctrl_events <- nrow(ctrl_events_sec2c)

# Compute event proportions for three groups
compute_evt_pct <- function(events, n_total, label) {
  freq <- as.data.frame(table(events$event_type), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(freq) <- c("event_type", "n")
  freq$pct <- round(100 * freq$n / n_total, 1)
  freq$group <- label
  freq
}

reclass_freq <- compute_evt_pct(nmd_reclass_events, n_nmd_events, "Reclassified PTC")
ptcpos_freq <- compute_evt_pct(ptcpos_events, n_ptcpos_events, "Original PTC+")
ctrl_freq <- compute_evt_pct(ctrl_events_sec2c, n_ctrl_events, "Control")

# Merge all three
all_evt <- rbind(reclass_freq, ptcpos_freq, ctrl_freq)

# Sort by reclassified PTC prevalence
evt_order <- reclass_freq$event_type[order(-reclass_freq$pct)]
all_evt$event_type <- factor(all_evt$event_type, levels = evt_order)
all_evt$group <- factor(all_evt$group,
  levels = c("Original PTC+", "Reclassified PTC", "Control"))

fig_events <- ggplot(all_evt, aes(x = event_type, y = pct, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Original PTC+" = "#fddbc7",
                                "Reclassified PTC" = "#ef8a62",
                                "Control" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "Splice Event Proportions: Reclassified PTC vs Original PTC+ vs Control",
       subtitle = sprintf("Original PTC+: %s pairs | Reclassified: %s pairs | Control: %s pairs",
                          fmt(nrow(ptc_pos_profiles)), fmt(nrow(eff_ptc)),
                          fmt(nrow(ctrl_profiles_sec2c))),
       x = NULL, y = "% of events", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_events, "fig_sec2c_reclass_events", width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r sec2c-frameshift-comparison, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: profiles_list C2 (PTC-negative) and C4 (Control)
# Population: All PTC-negative NMD pairs vs Control
# Analysis: for each event type, what % cause frameshifts?

compute_fs_by_type <- function(profiles, label) {
  coding <- profiles %>%
    filter(reference_isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"],
           comparator_isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"])
  all_events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(coding)), function(i) {
    de <- coding$detailed_events[[i]]
    if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
    de[!is.na(de$bp_diff) & de$bp_diff != 0, c("event_type", "bp_diff")]
  }))
  if (is.null(all_events) || nrow(all_events) == 0) return(NULL)
  all_events$is_frameshift <- all_events$bp_diff %% 3 != 0
  all_events %>%
    group_by(event_type) %>%
    summarise(n_events = n(), n_frameshift = sum(is_frameshift),
              pct_frameshift = round(100 * mean(is_frameshift), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(group = label)
}

ptc_assoc_sec2c <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
ptc_lkp <- ptc_assoc_sec2c$pair_summary[, c("comparator_isoform_id", "comp_has_ptc")]
nmd_profiles <- merge(profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]], ptc_lkp, by = "comparator_isoform_id", all.x = TRUE)
nmd_profiles$comp_has_ptc[is.na(nmd_profiles$comp_has_ptc)] <- FALSE

# Three groups: Original PTC+, Reclassified PTC (from PTC-), Control
# Use the reclassified pairs specifically (not all PTC-)
reclass_profiles <- nmd_profiles[nmd_profiles$comparator_isoform_id %in% eff_ptc$comparator_isoform_id, ]

fs_ptcpos <- compute_fs_by_type(nmd_profiles[nmd_profiles$comp_has_ptc, ], "Original PTC+")
fs_reclass <- compute_fs_by_type(reclass_profiles, "Reclassified PTC")
fs_ctrl <- compute_fs_by_type(profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]], "Control")

fs_all <- rbind(fs_ptcpos, fs_reclass, fs_ctrl) %>% filter(n_events >= 20)

# Sort by reclassified PTC frameshift rate
evt_order_fs <- fs_all$event_type[fs_all$group == "Reclassified PTC"][
  order(-fs_all$pct_frameshift[fs_all$group == "Reclassified PTC"])]

fs_bar <- fs_all %>%
  select(event_type, group, pct_frameshift) %>%
  mutate(event_type = factor(event_type, levels = evt_order_fs),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("Original PTC+", "Reclassified PTC", "Control")))

fig_fs <- ggplot(fs_bar, aes(x = event_type, y = pct_frameshift, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Original PTC+" = "#fddbc7",
                                "Reclassified PTC" = "#ef8a62",
                                "Control" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "Frameshift Rate by Splice Event Type",
       subtitle = sprintf("Original PTC+ (%s) vs Reclassified PTC (%s) vs Control (%s) | %% causing frameshift",
                          fmt(sum(nmd_profiles$comp_has_ptc)),
                          fmt(nrow(eff_ptc)),
                          fmt(nrow(ctrl_profiles_sec2c))),
       x = NULL, y = "% frameshift", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_fs, "fig_sec2c_frameshift_rate", width = 10, height = 6)
```

# 5. Residual NMD: PTC-Negative NMD Subgroups {#sec5-residual}

## The Remaining PTC-Negative Pairs: Two Subgroups

```{r sec2c-remaining-setup, include=FALSE}
n_remaining <- n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost
```

After reclassification (ref-ATG tracing + TD2 fallback),
`r fmt(n_remaining)` pairs
(`r round(100 * n_remaining / nrow(coding_pairs_c2), 1)`% of all NMD pairs)
remain PTC-negative. These fall into two groups:

- **NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained** (`r fmt(n_subgroup_retained)` pairs): the
reference ATG is present in the comparator but the reading frame terminates
without downstream EJCs. This group contains two structurally distinct
subpopulations: `r fmt(sum(ptc_neg_ref$category == "no_downstream_ejc"))` with
a full-length ORF from the reference ATG (no downstream EJC), and
`r fmt(sum(ptc_neg_ref$category == "truncated_no_ejc"))` with a truncated
ref-ATG ORF but still no downstream EJCs.

- **NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost** (`r fmt(n_subgroup_lost)` pairs): the reference
ATG is not exonic in the comparator, AND the TD2-predicted CDS also has 0
downstream EJCs. These are PTC-negative by both available reading frame
definitions.

```{r sec2c-remaining-characterization}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Reference-ATG Tracing (PTC-Negative Reclassification)"
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (categories), orfik_scan.rds (ORF features),
#   structures.rds + cds.rds (UTR lengths)
# Population: remaining PTC-negative pairs after reclassification, grouped by
#   category. Compared to reclassified PTC and Control baselines.

remaining_pairs <- ptc_neg_ref[ptc_neg_ref$subgroup != "NMD PTC+", ]

# Split by canonical subgroup (2 groups)
remaining_by_subgroup <- split(remaining_pairs, remaining_pairs$subgroup)

# Also split by detail category for 5'UTR substructure analyses
remaining_by_cat <- split(remaining_pairs, remaining_pairs$subgroup_detail)

# --- Transcript lengths from structures ---
tx_lengths <- setNames(
  sapply(seq_len(nrow(structures)), function(i)
    sum(structures$exon_ends[[i]] - structures$exon_starts[[i]] + 1L)),
  structures$isoform_id)

# --- 3'UTR from SQANTI CDS ---
compute_sqanti_3utr <- function(iso_id) {
  cds_row <- cds[cds$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(cds_row) == 0 || cds_row$coding_status != "coding") return(NA_real_)
  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  strand <- cds_row$strand
  stop_pos <- if (strand == "+") cds_row$cds_stop else cds_row$cds_start
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]; exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]
  utr3 <- 0
  for (j in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (strand == "+") {
      if (exon_e[j] > stop_pos) utr3 <- utr3 + exon_e[j] - max(exon_s[j], stop_pos + 1) + 1
    } else {
      if (exon_s[j] < stop_pos) utr3 <- utr3 + min(exon_e[j], stop_pos - 1) - exon_s[j] + 1
    }
  }
  utr3
}

# --- 5'UTR from SQANTI CDS ---
compute_sqanti_5utr <- function(iso_id) {
  cds_row <- cds[cds$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(cds_row) == 0 || cds_row$coding_status != "coding") return(NA_real_)
  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == iso_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  strand <- cds_row$strand
  cds5 <- if (strand == "+") cds_row$cds_start else cds_row$cds_stop
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]; exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]
  utr5 <- 0
  for (j in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (strand == "+") {
      if (exon_s[j] < cds5) utr5 <- utr5 + min(exon_e[j], cds5 - 1) - exon_s[j] + 1
    } else {
      if (exon_e[j] > cds5) utr5 <- utr5 + exon_e[j] - max(exon_s[j], cds5 + 1) + 1
    }
  }
  utr5
}

# --- 3'UTR and 5'UTR from ref-ATG ORF stop ---
# comp_stop_tx_pos gives the transcript position of the premature stop
# ref_atg_3utr = transcript_length - (comp_stop_tx_pos + 2)
# ref_atg_5utr = comp_stop_tx_pos - comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg - 1
#   (tx pos of ATG = comp_stop_tx_pos - comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg;
#    5'UTR = ATG_tx_pos - 1)

# --- ORFik features ---
orfik_data <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "orfik_scan.rds"))
orf_tx_rem <- orfik_data$tx_summary

# --- Build summary table ---
# Groups: remaining categories + reclassified PTC + Control baselines
eff_ptc_pairs <- ptc_neg_ref[ptc_neg_ref$category == "effectively_ptc", ]

build_row <- function(pairs, label, has_ref_atg = TRUE) {
  comp_ids <- pairs$comparator_isoform_id
  n <- length(comp_ids)

  # SQANTI-based UTR lengths
  sqanti_3utr <- sapply(comp_ids, compute_sqanti_3utr)
  sqanti_5utr <- sapply(comp_ids, compute_sqanti_5utr)

  # Ref-ATG-based UTR lengths (only meaningful when ref ATG is available)
  if (has_ref_atg && "comp_stop_tx_pos" %in% names(pairs)) {
    tx_len <- tx_lengths[comp_ids]
    ref_atg_3utr <- tx_len - pairs$comp_stop_tx_pos - 2L
    ref_atg_3utr[is.na(pairs$comp_stop_tx_pos)] <- NA
    # 5'UTR from ref ATG: ATG tx pos = comp_stop_tx_pos - comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg
    atg_tx <- pairs$comp_stop_tx_pos - pairs$comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg
    ref_atg_5utr <- atg_tx - 1L
    ref_atg_5utr[is.na(atg_tx)] <- NA
  } else {
    ref_atg_3utr <- rep(NA, n)
    ref_atg_5utr <- rep(NA, n)
  }

  # ORFik features
  orf_match <- orf_tx_rem[match(comp_ids, orf_tx_rem$isoform_id), ]

  data.frame(
    Group = label,
    n = n,
    `SQANTI 5UTR (bp)` = round(median(sqanti_5utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Ref-ATG 5UTR (bp)` = if (any(!is.na(ref_atg_5utr))) round(median(ref_atg_5utr, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA,
    `SQANTI 3UTR (bp)` = round(median(sqanti_3utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Ref-ATG 3UTR (bp)` = if (any(!is.na(ref_atg_3utr))) round(median(ref_atg_3utr, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA,
    `Total ORFs` = round(median(orf_match$n_orfs, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `NMD-susceptible ORFs` = round(median(orf_match$n_nmd_competent, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Junctions` = round(median(orf_match$n_junctions, na.rm = TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Control pairs — need ref_atg data from c4
c4_ref <- ref_atg$c4
c4_ref_avail <- c4_ref[c4_ref$ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE & !is.na(c4_ref$comp_stop_tx_pos), ]

summary_rows <- rbind(
  build_row(eff_ptc_pairs, "NMD PTC+ (reclassified)", has_ref_atg = TRUE),
  build_row(remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"]],
            "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained", has_ref_atg = TRUE),
  build_row(remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]],
            "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost", has_ref_atg = FALSE),
  build_row(c4_ref_avail, "Control (C4)", has_ref_atg = TRUE)
)

render_dt(summary_rows, caption = "PTC-Negative Pairs: Structural Characterization by Subgroup (medians)")
```

Columns: **Group** = canonical subgroup; **n** = number of pairs;
**SQANTI 5'UTR / 3'UTR** = exonic bp from the TransDecoder2-predicted CDS
boundaries to the transcript ends;
**Ref-ATG 5'UTR / 3'UTR** = exonic bp computed from the reference isoform's
CDS start ATG traced through the comparator (NA for ref ATG lost where the
reference ATG is not available in the comparator);
**Total ORFs** = all ORFs detected by ORFik; **NMD-susceptible ORFs** = ORFs
whose stop codon has ≥1 downstream exon-exon junction;
**Junctions** = exon-exon junctions in the comparator.

