```{r sec2c-remaining-isoform-table}
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (remaining PTC-negative pairs),
#   gene_symbol_lookup (from mashr DE files)
# Population: PTC-negative NMD pairs that could not be reclassified as PTC+

remaining_display <- data.frame(
  gene_id = remaining_pairs$gene_id,
  gene_symbol = sapply(remaining_pairs$gene_id, get_gene_sym),
  reference_isoform = remaining_pairs$reference_isoform_id,

write.csv(remaining_display, file.path(table_dir, "remaining_ptc_negative_pairs.csv"),
```

Columns: **gene_id/gene_symbol** = gene identifier; **reference/comparator_isoform** =

### DIE logFC Across All Subgroups

We now compare NMD response magnitude across all four canonical subgroups.

```{r sec2c-logfc-all-subgroups, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: meta_logfc (STAGE 5, mashr posterior means averaged across cell types)
#   NMD PTC+: all_ptcplus_ids (original + ref-ATG + TD2 reclassified)
#   NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained: remaining_by_subgroup
#   NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost: remaining_by_subgroup
#   Control: profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]] (C4 gene-matched pairs)
# Population: comparator isoforms with mashr logFC available

retained_ids <- remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"]]$comparator_isoform_id
lost_ids     <- remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]]$comparator_isoform_id

logfc_all <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC+",
             mean_logFC = meta_logfc$mean_logFC[meta_logfc$txid %in% all_ptcplus_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
             mean_logFC = meta_logfc$mean_logFC[meta_logfc$txid %in% retained_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost",
             mean_logFC = meta_logfc$mean_logFC[meta_logfc$txid %in% lost_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
             mean_logFC = meta_logfc$mean_logFC[meta_logfc$txid %in% ctrl_ids])
)

logfc_all$group <- factor(logfc_all$group,
  levels = c("NMD PTC+", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
             "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost", "Control"))

# Group medians for subtitle

# Pairwise Wilcoxon tests
pw_test <- pairwise.wilcox.test(logfc_all$mean_logFC, logfc_all$group,
                                 p.adjust.method = "BH")

fig_logfc_all <- ggplot(logfc_all, aes(x = group, y = mean_logFC, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, outlier.size = 0.5, width = 0.6) +

                          med_all[["NMD PTC+"]], med_all[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"]],
                          med_all[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]], med_all[["Control"]]),
       x = NULL, y = "Mean logFC (mashr, SMG1i vs DMSO)") +

save_fig(fig_logfc_all, "fig_sec2c_logfc_all_subgroups", width = 10, height = 6)
```

NMD PTC+ isoforms show the strongest NMD response (median logFC
`r round(med_all[["NMD PTC+"]], 2)`). Both PTC-negative subgroups show
intermediate responses that are significantly above Control: ref ATG retained
(median `r round(med_all[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"]], 2)`) and ref ATG
lost (median `r round(med_all[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]], 2)`). The weaker
but still substantial logFC in these groups indicates NMD engagement through
non-canonical mechanisms — consistent with the 5'UTR and uORF features
characterized below.

### Splicing and Stop Codon Landscape

Before characterizing each group individually, we compare structural features
across all five groups (original PTC+, reclassified PTC, and the three
residual categories) to establish what distinguishes them.

```{r sec2c-crossgroup-stop-codon, include=FALSE}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (all categories), cds.rds (TD2 stop codons)
# Population: PTC+, no_downstream_ejc — stop codon concordance for inline text

cds_stop_lookup <- cds %>%
  filter(coding_status == "coding") %>%
  transmute(isoform_id,
            stop_3prime = ifelse(strand == "+", cds_stop, cds_start))

compute_same_stop <- function(ref_ids, comp_ids) {
  ref_stops <- cds_stop_lookup$stop_3prime[match(ref_ids, cds_stop_lookup$isoform_id)]
  comp_stops <- cds_stop_lookup$stop_3prime[match(comp_ids, cds_stop_lookup$isoform_id)]
  valid <- !is.na(ref_stops) & !is.na(comp_stops)
  c(n_valid = sum(valid), n_same = sum(ref_stops[valid] == comp_stops[valid]),
    pct_same = round(100 * mean(ref_stops[valid] == comp_stops[valid]), 1))
}

ptc_pos_pairs_local <- c2_ref[c2_ref$original_ptc, ]
no_ejc_local <- remaining_by_cat[["No downstream EJC"]]
ref_lost_local <- remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]]
trunc_local <- remaining_by_cat[["Truncated, no EJC"]]

pct_same_ptcpos <- compute_same_stop(ptc_pos_pairs_local$reference_isoform_id,
                                      ptc_pos_pairs_local$comparator_isoform_id)[["pct_same"]]
pct_same_no_ejc <- compute_same_stop(no_ejc_local$reference_isoform_id,
                                      no_ejc_local$comparator_isoform_id)[["pct_same"]]
```

```{r sec2c-crossgroup-splicing, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: profiles_list (C2 and C4 splicing profiles)
# Population: 5 NMD groups + Control, splice event type proportions

# Extract events for each group
extract_events <- function(profile_df, pair_ids, label) {
  sub <- profile_df[profile_df$comparator_isoform_id %in% pair_ids, ]
  events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i) {
    de <- sub$detailed_events[[i]]
    if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
    de[, "event_type", drop = FALSE]
  }))
  if (is.null(events) || nrow(events) == 0) return(data.frame(event_type = character(0), group = character(0)))
  data.frame(event_type = events$event_type, group = label, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

c2_profiles <- profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]]
c4_profiles <- profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]]

# Get PTC+ comparator IDs
ptc_assoc_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
ptc_pos_comp_ids <- ptc_assoc_c2$pair_summary$comparator_isoform_id[
  ptc_assoc_c2$pair_summary$comp_has_ptc == TRUE]

retained_comp_ids <- c(no_ejc_local$comparator_isoform_id,
                       trunc_local$comparator_isoform_id)

all_events <- rbind(
  extract_events(c2_profiles, all_ptcplus_ids, "NMD PTC+"),
  extract_events(c2_profiles, retained_comp_ids, "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"),
  extract_events(c2_profiles, ref_lost_local$comparator_isoform_id, "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"),
  extract_events(c4_profiles, c4_profiles$comparator_isoform_id, "Control")
)

# Compute within-group proportions
event_pct <- all_events %>%
  group_by(group, event_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Focus on key event types
key_events <- c("SE", "Missing_Internal", "Alt_TSS", "Alt_TES", "A3SS", "A5SS",
                "IR", "Partial_IR_5", "Partial_IR_3")
event_pct_key <- event_pct %>%
  filter(event_type %in% key_events) %>%
  mutate(event_type = factor(event_type, levels = key_events),
         group = factor(group,
           levels = c("NMD PTC+", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
                      "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost", "Control")))

fig_splice <- ggplot(event_pct_key, aes(x = event_type, y = pct, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = subgroup_pal) +
  labs(title = "Splicing Event Proportions Across All Subgroups",
       subtitle = "SE dominates NMD PTC+; Alt_TSS elevated in ref ATG lost",
       x = NULL, y = "% of events within group", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_splice, "fig_sec2c_crossgroup_splicing", width = 12, height = 6)
```

```{r sec2c-crossgroup-splicing-table, echo=FALSE}
  select(group, event_type, pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
render_dt(splice_wide, caption = "Splicing Event Proportions (%) by Group")
```

Columns: **event_type** = splice event; remaining columns = percentage of
events within each group.

</details>

The splicing landscape reveals a quantitative shift between PTC-mediated and
PTC-negative subgroups. SE events dominate NMD PTC+ (the primary
frameshift-causing mechanism). The PTC-negative subgroups still carry SE
events but show a relative enrichment for Missing_Internal events and TSS/TES
changes. This is consistent with their defining feature: they lack a
main-ORF PTC despite undergoing alternative splicing, suggesting that the
splicing events present in these isoforms alter the ORF landscape without
necessarily creating a classical frameshift-to-stop path.

Stop codon concordance reinforces this distinction: only
`r pct_same_ptcpos`% of NMD PTC+ pairs share the same stop codon as their
reference (consistent with a premature stop), while `r pct_same_no_ejc`% of
the ref ATG retained subpopulation with no downstream EJCs use the *same*
stop codon --- their main reading frame is intact, ruling out a classical
main-ORF PTC as the NMD trigger.

### NMD PTC-, Ref ATG Retained (n = `r fmt(n_subgroup_retained)`)

These isoforms retain the reference ATG but the reading frame terminates
without downstream EJCs — no classical PTC is present. Yet they show robust
NMD response (median logFC `r round(med_all[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained"]], 2)`).
This group contains two structurally distinct subpopulations:
`r nrow(no_ejc_local)` with a full-length ORF from the reference ATG
("no downstream EJC"), and `r nrow(trunc_local)` with a truncated ref-ATG
ORF but still no downstream EJCs ("truncated, no EJC"). We characterize
the dominant subpopulation (no downstream EJC) first, then note how the
truncated subpopulation differs.

```{r sec2c-uorf-populations}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (categories, ref-ATG tracing results),
#   utr5_features_all.rds (5'UTR features), orfik_scan.rds (per-ORF features)
# Population: no_downstream_ejc (n=187), ref_atg_lost (n=240),
#   reclassified PTC (eff_ptc_pairs), Control (c4_ref_avail)

# Load 5'UTR features and per-ORF data (not yet in scope)
utr5_feat_all <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "utr5_features_all.rds"))
utr5_feat <- utr5_feat_all$isoform_features %>% filter(!excluded)
orf_feat_local <- orfik_data$orf_features

# Define populations (using subgroup_detail keys from remaining_by_cat)
no_ejc <- remaining_by_cat[["No downstream EJC"]]
ref_lost <- remaining_by_subgroup[["NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"]]
trunc_noejc <- remaining_by_cat[["Truncated, no EJC"]]

# Compute ref-ATG 5'UTR for no_downstream_ejc
# ATG tx position = comp_stop_tx_pos - comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg; 5'UTR = ATG - 1
no_ejc$ref_5utr <- (no_ejc$comp_stop_tx_pos - no_ejc$comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg) - 1L
no_ejc$sqanti_5utr <- sapply(no_ejc$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr)

# Same for Control
c4_ref_avail$ref_5utr <- (c4_ref_avail$comp_stop_tx_pos -
  c4_ref_avail$comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg) - 1L
c4_ref_avail$sqanti_5utr <- sapply(c4_ref_avail$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr)

# Ref-ATG 3'UTR: transcript_length - (stop_tx_pos + 2)
no_ejc$ref_3utr <- tx_lengths[no_ejc$comparator_isoform_id] -
  (no_ejc$comp_stop_tx_pos + 2L)
c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr <- tx_lengths[c4_ref_avail$comparator_isoform_id] -
  (c4_ref_avail$comp_stop_tx_pos + 2L)

# Ref-ATG 5'UTR and 3'UTR for reclassified PTC+ group
# These pairs have the ref ATG — the 5'UTR from the ref ATG reveals the
# true distance, which should be much shorter than the TD2 5'UTR (artifact)
eff_ptc_pairs$ref_5utr <- (eff_ptc_pairs$comp_stop_tx_pos -
  eff_ptc_pairs$comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg) - 1L
eff_ptc_pairs$ref_3utr <- tx_lengths[eff_ptc_pairs$comparator_isoform_id] -
  (eff_ptc_pairs$comp_stop_tx_pos + 2L)

# Validation table
val_table <- data.frame(
  Group = c("No downstream EJC", "Ref ATG lost", "Reclassified PTC+", "Control (C4)"),
  n = c(nrow(no_ejc), nrow(ref_lost), nrow(eff_ptc_pairs), nrow(c4_ref_avail)),
  `SQANTI 5'UTR (bp)` = c(
    round(median(no_ejc$sqanti_5utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(sapply(ref_lost$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr), na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(sapply(eff_ptc_pairs$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr), na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(c4_ref_avail$sqanti_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))),
  `Ref-ATG 5'UTR (bp)` = c(
    round(median(no_ejc$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    NA,  # ref ATG not available
    round(median(eff_ptc_pairs$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))),
  `Ref-ATG 3'UTR (bp)` = c(
    round(median(no_ejc$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    NA,
    round(median(eff_ptc_pairs$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

render_dt(val_table, caption = "5'UTR and 3'UTR Validation: Genuine vs Artifact")
```

Column definitions: **Group** = pair category; **n** = pairs;
**SQANTI 5'UTR** = median exonic bp from TD2-predicted CDS start to
transcript 5' end; **Ref-ATG 5'UTR** = median exonic bp from reference
ATG to transcript 5' end (NA for ref_atg_lost where the reference ATG is
absent from the comparator);
**Ref-ATG 3'UTR** = median exonic bp from ref-ATG ORF stop to 3' end.

The two 5'UTR measurements tell different stories depending on the group.
For the `Reclassified PTC+` group, the TD2-predicted 5'UTR
(`r round(median(sapply(eff_ptc_pairs$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr), na.rm = TRUE))` bp)
is dramatically longer than the ref-ATG 5'UTR
(`r round(median(eff_ptc_pairs$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp), confirming
that the apparent long 5'UTR in this group is an artifact of incorrect CDS
annotation --- TD2 selected a downstream alternative CDS, inflating the
apparent 5'UTR. The ref-ATG 5'UTR is similar to Control
(`r round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp).

For the `No downstream EJC` group, by contrast, the two measurements agree
(both ~`r round(median(no_ejc$sqanti_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))` --
`r round(median(no_ejc$ref_5utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp), roughly 3x the
Control median. This is a genuinely long 5'UTR, not a TD2 artifact.
Meanwhile, the ref-ATG 3'UTR
(`r round(median(no_ejc$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp) is significantly
shorter than Control
(`r round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp; Wilcoxon
p = `r format_p(wilcox.test(no_ejc$ref_3utr, c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr)$p.value)`),
ruling out the long-3'UTR NMD pathway.

#### 5'UTR Feature Landscape

The figure below compares eight features of the 5'UTR (the region from the
transcript 5' end to the TD2-predicted CDS start) across the residual groups
and Control. All features are computed per isoform from the transcript
sequence using `scan5UtrFeatures()`:

- **5'UTR length (bp)**: Total exonic length from transcript start to CDS start
- **ATG count**: Number of AUG trinucleotides in the 5'UTR
- **ATG density (per 100 bp)**: ATG count normalized by 5'UTR length
- **Strong Kozak ATG count**: ATGs with favorable initiation context at
  positions -3 (purine) and +4 (G), scored 2 on a 0--2 scale
- **Overlapping uORF count**: uORFs whose reading frame extends past the
  CDS start (overlapping the main ORF)
- **Out-of-frame uORF count**: uORFs in a different reading frame than the
  main CDS
- **Longest uORF (nt)**: Length of the longest open reading frame within the
  5'UTR
- **ORF coverage (%)**: Fraction of the 5'UTR covered by any ORF

```{r sec2c-uorf-5utr-features, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: utr5_features_all.rds (per-isoform features from scan5UtrFeatures)
# Population: 4 groups defined in sec2c-uorf-populations

key_feats <- c("utr5_length", "n_atg", "atg_density", "n_strong_kozak_atg",
               "n_orfs_overlapping", "n_orfs_outframe", "longest_orf_nt",
               "pct_utr5_in_orfs")
uorf_feat_labels <- c(
  utr5_length = "5\u2032UTR length (bp)", n_atg = "ATG count",
  atg_density = "ATG density\n(per 100 bp)", n_strong_kozak_atg = "Strong Kozak\nATG count",
  n_orfs_overlapping = "Overlapping\nuORF count", n_orfs_outframe = "Out-of-frame\nuORF count",
  longest_orf_nt = "Longest uORF (nt)", pct_utr5_in_orfs = "ORF coverage (%)")

# --- Primary figure: 3 canonical groups ---
uorf_groups_3 <- list(
  "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained" = c(no_ejc$comparator_isoform_id,
                                    trunc_noejc$comparator_isoform_id),
  "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost" = ref_lost$comparator_isoform_id,
  "Control" = c4_ref_avail$comparator_isoform_id)

uorf_plot_3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(uorf_groups_3), function(grp) {
  sub <- utr5_feat[utr5_feat$isoform_id %in% uorf_groups_3[[grp]], ]
  sub$group <- grp
  sub[, c("group", key_feats)]
}))
uorf_plot_3$group <- factor(uorf_plot_3$group,
  levels = c("Control", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"))

uorf_long_3 <- uorf_plot_3 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(key_feats), names_to = "feature", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(feature = uorf_feat_labels[feature],
         feature = factor(feature, levels = uorf_feat_labels))

fig_uorf_3 <- ggplot(uorf_long_3, aes(x = group, y = value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~feature, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = subgroup_pal[c("Control", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
                                             "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost")]) +
  labs(title = "5\u2032UTR Features: PTC-Negative Subgroups vs Control",
       subtitle = "NMD PTC+ excluded (TD2-predicted 5\u2032UTR is artifactually inflated)",
       x = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10))
save_fig(fig_uorf_3, "fig_sec2c_uorf_5utr_features", width = 14, height = 8)
```

Both PTC-negative subgroups have substantially longer 5'UTRs and increased
uORF features relative to Control. The ref ATG retained group shows the most
extreme enrichment, but the ref ATG lost group follows a similar pattern ---
consistent with the shared structural feature of long 5'UTRs that provide
space for multiple upstream ORFs.

The ref ATG retained group merges two structurally distinct subpopulations
(`r nrow(no_ejc)` "no downstream EJC" pairs with a full-length ref-ATG ORF,
and `r nrow(trunc_noejc)` "truncated, no EJC" pairs with a shortened ORF).
The supplementary figure below splits this group to show whether the 5'UTR
signal comes from both subpopulations or is driven by one.

```{r sec2c-uorf-logfc-setup, include=FALSE}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: orfik_scan.rds (per-ORF features), utr5_features_all.rds
# Population: no_downstream_ejc comparators — compute per-isoform NMD-susceptible
#   ORF counts needed for logFC correlation below

no_ejc_ids <- no_ejc$comparator_isoform_id
no_ejc_orfs <- orf_feat_local[orf_feat_local$isoform_id %in% no_ejc_ids, ]

utr5_lookup <- utr5_feat %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% no_ejc_ids) %>%
  select(isoform_id, utr5_length)

no_ejc_orfs <- no_ejc_orfs %>%
  left_join(utr5_lookup, by = "isoform_id") %>%
  mutate(position_class = case_when(
    orf_start < utr5_length ~ "Upstream (true uORF)",
    TRUE ~ "At/past CDS start"))

nmd_orfs <- no_ejc_orfs %>% filter(has_downstream_ejc)

per_iso <- nmd_orfs %>%
  group_by(isoform_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_nmd_orfs = n(),
    n_upstream = sum(position_class == "Upstream (true uORF)"),
    n_strong_kozak = sum(kozak_score == 2),
    .groups = "drop")
```

#### NMD Response Magnitude and uORF Density

```{r sec2c-uorf-logfc-correlation, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: meta_logfc (mashr posterior mean logFC, loaded in Section 0),
#   per_iso (NMD-susceptible ORF counts from sec2c-uorf-logfc-setup),
#   orf_tx_rem (per-isoform ORF summary from orfik_scan.rds)
# Population: no_downstream_ejc comparators with mashr logFC

no_ejc_logfc <- meta_logfc %>%
  filter(txid %in% no_ejc_ids) %>%
  left_join(per_iso, by = c("txid" = "isoform_id")) %>%
  left_join(orf_tx_rem %>% select(isoform_id, n_orfs),
            by = c("txid" = "isoform_id"))

rho_nmd <- cor.test(no_ejc_logfc$mean_logFC, no_ejc_logfc$n_nmd_orfs,
                     method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
rho_orfs <- cor.test(no_ejc_logfc$mean_logFC, no_ejc_logfc$n_orfs,
                      method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

fig_corr <- ggplot(no_ejc_logfc, aes(x = n_nmd_orfs, y = mean_logFC)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5, color = "#d95f02") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#1a1a1a", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "NMD Response vs NMD-Susceptible ORF Count",
       subtitle = sprintf("No downstream EJC group (n = %s) | Spearman \u03C1 = %.3f, p = %s",
                          fmt(sum(!is.na(no_ejc_logfc$n_nmd_orfs))),
                          rho_nmd$estimate, signif(rho_nmd$p.value, 3)),
       x = "NMD-susceptible ORFs per isoform",
       y = "Mean logFC (mashr)")
save_fig(fig_corr, "fig_sec2c_uorf_logfc_correlation", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec2c-uorf-logfc-table, echo=FALSE}
  Feature = c("NMD-susceptible ORFs", "Total ORFs (all frames)"),
  `Spearman rho` = round(c(rho_nmd$estimate, rho_orfs$estimate), 3),
  `p-value` = c(signif(rho_nmd$p.value, 3), signif(rho_orfs$p.value, 3)),
  n = c(sum(!is.na(no_ejc_logfc$n_nmd_orfs)), sum(!is.na(no_ejc_logfc$n_orfs))),
```

with mashr posterior mean logFC; **p-value** = significance; **n** = isoforms
with both logFC and ORF data.

</details>

Within this group, the number of NMD-susceptible ORFs does not predict NMD
response magnitude (Spearman rho = `r round(rho_nmd$estimate, 3)`,
p = `r format_p(rho_nmd$p.value)`). Whatever drives the quantitative
strength of the NMD response in these isoforms, it is not simply the count
of ORFs with downstream EJCs.

### NMD PTC-, Ref ATG Lost (n = `r fmt(n_subgroup_lost)`)

These isoforms lost the reference start codon entirely --- the comparator's
transcript does not contain the reference ATG in its exonic sequence, AND the
TD2-predicted CDS also has 0 downstream EJCs. (An additional
`r fmt(n_td2_reclass)` pairs that lost the reference ATG were reclassified
as NMD PTC+ because their TD2 CDS had ≥1 downstream EJC.) What removed the
ATG, and what reading frame does the comparator actually use?

```{r sec2c-group2-characterization}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (ref_atg_lost pairs), profiles_list (splicing),
#   orfik_scan.rds (per-ORF features), cds.rds (TD2 CDS)
# Population: ref_atg_lost NMD comparators (n=240)

# --- TSS direction: did the comparator TSS move upstream or downstream? ---
ref_lost_profiles <- profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]] %>%
  filter(comparator_isoform_id %in% ref_lost$comparator_isoform_id)

# TSS direction from detailed_events
ref_lost_tss <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ref_lost_profiles)), function(i) {
  de <- ref_lost_profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
  tss <- de[de$event_type == "Alt_TSS", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(tss) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    comparator_isoform_id = ref_lost_profiles$comparator_isoform_id[i],
    direction = tss$direction[1],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

n_tss_changed <- sum(ref_lost_profiles$tss_changed)
n_tss_downstream <- sum(ref_lost_tss$direction == "LOSS", na.rm = TRUE)
n_tss_upstream <- sum(ref_lost_tss$direction == "GAIN", na.rm = TRUE)
pct_tss_downstream <- round(100 * n_tss_downstream / nrow(ref_lost_tss), 1)

# --- logFC for this group ---
ref_lost_logfc <- meta_logfc$mean_logFC[match(ref_lost$comparator_isoform_id, meta_logfc$txid)]

# --- TD2 5'UTR for this group ---
td2_5utr_ref_lost <- sapply(ref_lost$comparator_isoform_id, compute_sqanti_5utr)
median_td2_5utr_rl <- round(median(td2_5utr_ref_lost, na.rm = TRUE))

ref_lost_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Total pairs", "TSS changed", "TSS moved downstream (5' truncated)",
             "TSS moved upstream (5' extended)",
             "TD2 5'UTR (bp)", "Median logFC"),
  Value = c(nrow(ref_lost), n_tss_changed, n_tss_downstream,
            n_tss_upstream, median_td2_5utr_rl,
            round(median(ref_lost_logfc, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
  Percentage = c("", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_tss_changed / nrow(ref_lost)),
                 sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_tss_downstream),
                 sprintf("%.1f%%", round(100 * n_tss_upstream / nrow(ref_lost_tss), 1)),
                 "", ""),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

render_dt(ref_lost_summary, caption = "NMD PTC-, Ref ATG Lost — Structural Characterization")
```

Columns: **Metric** = structural feature; **Value** = count or measurement;
**Percentage** = proportion of the group.

The majority of ref ATG lost pairs (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_tss_changed / nrow(ref_lost))`)
have a changed TSS, with `r pct_tss_downstream`% moving *downstream*
(5'-truncated). This truncation removes the reference ATG from the exonic
sequence. These isoforms are PTC-negative by both available reading frame
definitions (ref-ATG tracing and TD2 CDS), yet they show a median logFC of
`r round(median(ref_lost_logfc, na.rm = TRUE), 2)` — weaker than the PTC+
group but substantially above Control.

The long 5'UTR in this group (TD2 median `r median_td2_5utr_rl` bp, ~3x
longer than Control) suggests uORF-mediated NMD as a candidate mechanism,
similar to the ref ATG retained group. Their NMD mechanism remains open ---
candidates include uORF-mediated NMD, near-cognate initiation from non-AUG
codons, or EJC-independent NMD pathways.

#### Subpopulation: Truncated, No EJC (n = `r nrow(trunc_noejc)`)

Within the ref ATG retained group, `r nrow(trunc_noejc)` pairs have a
truncated ref-ATG ORF (shorter than the reference) but still no downstream
EJCs. These differ structurally from the no_downstream_ejc subpopulation
above — their ORF is shortened rather than full-length, and they tend to
have 3'-truncated isoforms rather than 5'-extended ones.

```{r sec2c-group3-characterization}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: ref_atg_analysis.rds (truncated_no_ejc pairs), profiles_list,
#   mashr_isoform_model (lfsr), meta_logfc
# Population: truncated_no_ejc NMD comparators (n=71)

# --- TES direction ---
trunc_profiles <- profiles_list[["c2_allsamples"]] %>%
  filter(comparator_isoform_id %in% trunc_noejc$comparator_isoform_id)

trunc_tes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(trunc_profiles)), function(i) {
  de <- trunc_profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) return(NULL)
  tes <- de[de$event_type == "Alt_TES", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(tes) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    comparator_isoform_id = trunc_profiles$comparator_isoform_id[i],
    direction = tes$direction[1],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

n_tes_tot <- if (is.null(trunc_tes)) 0L else nrow(trunc_tes)
n_tes_upstream <- if (n_tes_tot > 0) sum(trunc_tes$direction == "LOSS", na.rm = TRUE) else 0L
pct_tes_upstream <- if (n_tes_tot > 0) round(100 * n_tes_upstream / n_tes_tot, 1) else NA_real_

# --- 3'UTR length ---
trunc_noejc$ref_3utr <- tx_lengths[trunc_noejc$comparator_isoform_id] -
  (trunc_noejc$comp_stop_tx_pos + 2L)

# --- lfsr classification confidence ---
# mashr_model already loaded in STAGE 5 (line ~539)
lfsr_mat <- ashr::get_lfsr(mashr_model)
main_cols <- c("Smg1i_in_DD", "Smg1i_in_AT", "Smg1i_in_FB", "Smg1i_in_MV")
min_lfsr_vec <- apply(lfsr_mat[, main_cols], 1, min)

trunc_lfsr <- min_lfsr_vec[match(trunc_noejc$comparator_isoform_id, names(min_lfsr_vec))]
trunc_lfsr <- trunc_lfsr[!is.na(trunc_lfsr)]
pct_near_boundary <- round(100 * mean(trunc_lfsr > 0.01), 1)

# For comparison: PTC+ lfsr
ptc_pos_lfsr <- min_lfsr_vec[match(ptc_pos_comp_ids, names(min_lfsr_vec))]
ptc_pos_lfsr <- ptc_pos_lfsr[!is.na(ptc_pos_lfsr)]
pct_ptc_boundary <- round(100 * mean(ptc_pos_lfsr > 0.01), 1)

# --- logFC ---
trunc_logfc <- meta_logfc$mean_logFC[match(trunc_noejc$comparator_isoform_id, meta_logfc$txid)]

# Defensive: each cell collapsed to a length-1 character so empty subgroups
# don't drop columns to length 6 in the data.frame() call below.
fmt1 <- function(x) {
  s <- format(x, nsmall = 0)
  if (length(s) == 0) "NA" else as.character(s[1])
}
fmt_pct <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x) || is.nan(x)) "NA" else sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
}

trunc_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Total pairs", "TES moved upstream (3' truncated)",
             "Median 3'UTR (bp)", "Control median 3'UTR (bp)",
             "lfsr > 0.01 (near boundary)", "PTC+ lfsr > 0.01 (comparison)",
             "Median logFC"),
  Value = c(fmt1(nrow(trunc_noejc)), fmt1(n_tes_upstream),
            fmt1(round(median(trunc_noejc$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))),
            fmt1(round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))),
            sprintf("%d/%d", sum(trunc_lfsr > 0.01), length(trunc_lfsr)),
            sprintf("%d/%d", sum(ptc_pos_lfsr > 0.01), length(ptc_pos_lfsr)),
            fmt1(round(median(trunc_logfc, na.rm = TRUE), 3))),
  Percentage = c("", fmt_pct(pct_tes_upstream),
                 "", "", fmt_pct(pct_near_boundary),
                 fmt_pct(pct_ptc_boundary), ""),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

render_dt(trunc_summary, caption = "Group 3: Truncated, No EJC — Structural Characterization")
```

Columns: **Metric** = structural feature; **Value** = count or measurement;
**Percentage** = proportion of the group.

The truncated_no_ejc group is the smallest (`r nrow(trunc_noejc)` pairs) and
has the weakest structural evidence for NMD. The dominant structural change
is 3'-end truncation: `r pct_tes_upstream`% have the TES moved upstream.
Despite the truncated ORF, their 3'UTR length
(`r round(median(trunc_noejc$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp) is similar to
Control (`r round(median(c4_ref_avail$ref_3utr, na.rm = TRUE))` bp),
suggesting that the truncation does not dramatically extend the 3'UTR.

Classification confidence is notably lower: `r pct_near_boundary`% of these
isoforms have lfsr > 0.01 (near the NMD classification boundary), compared
to only `r pct_ptc_boundary`% of PTC+ pairs. Some fraction of this group
may represent false positives in the NMD classification rather than genuine
NMD targets.

### Updated Accounting and Population Flow

With the three residual groups now characterized, we can update the NMD
mechanism accounting. PTC-mediated NMD (original PTC+ and reclassified pairs)
remains the dominant mechanism. The `no_downstream_ejc` group is
structurally consistent with uORF-mediated NMD (long 5'UTRs, elevated
NMD-susceptible ORFs, intact main reading frame), though this remains an
association rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism. The remaining
groups --- ref_atg_lost and truncated_no_ejc --- represent a substantial
PTC-negative population whose NMD mechanism is unresolved.

```{r sec2c-accounting}
# Canonical subgroup accounting
n_total_coding <- nrow(coding_pairs_c2)
n_ptcplus_total <- n_ptc_pos + n_subgroup_ptcplus  # original + reclassified (ref-ATG + TD2)

cat("NMD accounting (canonical subgroups):\n")
cat("  NMD PTC+ total:", fmt(n_ptcplus_total),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_ptcplus_total / n_total_coding))
cat("    Original PTC+:", fmt(n_ptc_pos),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_ptc_pos / n_total_coding))
cat("    Reclassified (ref-ATG):", fmt(n_refatg_reclass),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_refatg_reclass / n_total_coding))
cat("    Reclassified (TD2):", fmt(n_td2_reclass),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_td2_reclass / n_total_coding))
cat("  NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained:", fmt(n_subgroup_retained),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_subgroup_retained / n_total_coding))
cat("  NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost:", fmt(n_subgroup_lost),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * n_subgroup_lost / n_total_coding))
cat("  Total:", fmt(n_ptcplus_total + n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost), "\n")
stopifnot(n_ptcplus_total + n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost == n_total_coding)
```


NMD PTC+ --- combining original PTC+ (annotated CDS), ref-ATG reclassified,
and TD2-reclassified pairs --- accounts for
`r round(100 * n_ptcplus_total / n_total_coding, 1)`% of all coding NMD pairs.

The remaining `r fmt(n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost)` pairs
(`r round(100 * (n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost) / n_total_coding, 1)`%)
are PTC-negative by all available reading frame definitions:
`r fmt(n_subgroup_retained)` retain the reference ATG but lack downstream EJCs
(NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained), and `r fmt(n_subgroup_lost)` lost the reference
ATG and also have 0 downstream EJCs from the TD2 CDS (NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost).
Both groups have long 5'UTRs enriched for uORFs, consistent with
non-classical NMD mechanisms.

### Gene Architecture and NMD Susceptibility

Beyond characterizing individual residual groups, we examine whether
NMD-harboring genes differ from non-NMD genes at the structural level. We
compare the dominant non-NMD isoform (highest DMSO expression) between
these two gene classes using ORFik comprehensive ORF detection.

```{r sec2d-junction-basis}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: orfik_scan.rds (per-isoform ORF summaries), expression_data.rds
# Population: dominant non-NMD isoform per gene, NMD-harboring vs non-NMD genes

orf_feat <- orfik_data$orf_features
orf_tx_sum <- orfik_data$tx_summary

nmd_ids_all <- nmd_class$all_samples$nmd
non_nmd_ids_all <- nmd_class$all_samples$non_nmd
gene_map <- structures[, c("isoform_id", "gene_id")]
nmd_genes_all <- unique(gene_map$gene_id[gene_map$isoform_id %in% nmd_ids_all])

expr_mat_local <- readRDS("data_mashr/expression_data.rds")
sample_meta_local <- readRDS("data_mashr/sample_metadata.rds")
dmso_cols <- sample_meta_local$sample_id[sample_meta_local$treatment == "DMSO"]
dmso_cpm <- sweep(expr_mat_local[, dmso_cols], 2, colSums(expr_mat_local[, dmso_cols]), "/") * 1e6
mean_cpm <- rowMeans(dmso_cpm)

dom_iso <- data.frame(isoform_id = names(mean_cpm), mean_cpm = as.numeric(mean_cpm),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% non_nmd_ids_all,
         isoform_id %in% cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]) %>%
  inner_join(gene_map, by = "isoform_id") %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  slice_max(mean_cpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

dom_features <- inner_join(dom_iso, orf_tx_sum, by = "isoform_id")
dom_features$gene_type <- ifelse(dom_features$gene_id %in% nmd_genes_all, "NMD-harboring", "Non-NMD")

# Add transcript length (exonic bp) from structures
dom_tx_lengths <- sapply(match(dom_features$isoform_id, structures$isoform_id), function(i) {
  if (is.na(i)) return(NA_integer_)
  sum(structures$exon_ends[[i]] - structures$exon_starts[[i]] + 1L)
})
dom_features$tx_length <- dom_tx_lengths

dom_summary <- dom_features %>%
  group_by(gene_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            median_length = median(tx_length, na.rm = TRUE),
            iqr_length = sprintf("%s\u2013%s",
              format(quantile(tx_length, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ","),
              format(quantile(tx_length, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")),
            median_orfs = median(n_orfs),
            median_nmd_comp = median(n_nmd_competent),
            median_junctions = median(n_junctions),
            frac_nmd_comp = round(100 * median(n_nmd_competent / pmax(n_orfs, 1)), 1),
            .groups = "drop")

render_dt(dom_summary,
  caption = "Dominant Isoform ORF Landscape by Gene NMD Status")
```

Column definitions: **median_length** = median transcript length (exonic bp);
**iqr_length** = interquartile range (Q25--Q75) of transcript length;
**median_orfs** = median ORFs per transcript;
**median_nmd_comp** = median ORFs with >=1 downstream EJC;
**median_junctions** = median exon-exon junctions;
**frac_nmd_comp** = median fraction of ORFs that are NMD-susceptible.

NMD-harboring genes have substantially more exon-exon junctions in their
dominant isoform (median `r dom_summary$median_junctions[dom_summary$gene_type == "NMD-harboring"]`
vs `r dom_summary$median_junctions[dom_summary$gene_type == "Non-NMD"]`)
without being longer (median transcript length
`r format(dom_summary$median_length[dom_summary$gene_type == "NMD-harboring"], big.mark = ",")`
vs `r format(dom_summary$median_length[dom_summary$gene_type == "Non-NMD"], big.mark = ",")` bp).
This higher junction density results in a larger fraction of their ORFs being
NMD-susceptible
(`r dom_summary$frac_nmd_comp[dom_summary$gene_type == "NMD-harboring"]`% vs
`r dom_summary$frac_nmd_comp[dom_summary$gene_type == "Non-NMD"]`%),
while total ORF count is similar.

### NMD-Susceptible ORFs at the Isoform Level

The gene-level analysis above used one representative isoform per gene. We now
shift to the isoform level to ask: do NMD comparators themselves have more
NMD-susceptible ORFs than Control comparators? We compare all
`r fmt(nrow(coding_pairs_c2))` NMD comparators from gene-matched C2 pairs
versus gene-matched Control (C4) comparators, stratified by Kozak start codon
context strength.

```{r sec2d-orf-landscape, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: orfik_scan.rds
# Population: ALL NMD comparators vs Control

all_nmd_comp_ids <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id
ctrl_comp_ids <- unique(profiles_list[["c4_allsamples"]]$comparator_isoform_id)
ctrl_comp_ids <- ctrl_comp_ids[ctrl_comp_ids %in% orf_tx_sum$isoform_id]

count_by_kozak <- function(iso_ids) {
  sub <- orf_feat[orf_feat$isoform_id %in% iso_ids, ]
  sub %>%
    group_by(isoform_id) %>%
    summarise(n_k2_ejc = sum(kozak_score == 2 & has_downstream_ejc),
              n_k1plus_ejc = sum(kozak_score >= 1 & has_downstream_ejc),
              n_any_ejc = sum(has_downstream_ejc), .groups = "drop")
}

nmd_kozak <- count_by_kozak(all_nmd_comp_ids) %>% mutate(group = "NMD (all)")
ctrl_kozak <- count_by_kozak(ctrl_comp_ids) %>% mutate(group = "Control")

kozak_all <- rbind(nmd_kozak, ctrl_kozak) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(n_k2_ejc, n_k1plus_ejc, n_any_ejc),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric,
    levels = c("n_k2_ejc", "n_k1plus_ejc", "n_any_ejc"),
    labels = c("Strong Kozak\n(score = 2)", "Moderate+ Kozak\n(score \u2265 1)", "Any ORF")))

fig_kozak <- ggplot(kozak_all, aes(x = group, y = count, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD (all)" = "#ef8a62", "Control" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "NMD-Susceptible ORFs by Kozak Strength: All NMD vs Control",
       subtitle = sprintf("NMD comparators (n=%s) vs Control (n=%s) | ORFs with \u22651 downstream EJC",
                          fmt(nrow(nmd_kozak)), fmt(nrow(ctrl_kozak))),
       x = NULL, y = "Count per transcript") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
save_fig(fig_kozak, "fig_sec2d_orf_landscape", width = 10, height = 6)
```

<summary>Click to view tabular data for ORF landscape</summary>

```{r sec2d-orf-landscape-table, echo=FALSE}
orf_summary <- kozak_all %>%
  group_by(metric, group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            Median = round(median(count, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            Q25 = round(quantile(count, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            Q75 = round(quantile(count, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
render_dt(orf_summary, caption = "ORF Landscape: NMD-Susceptible ORFs by Kozak Strength")
```

Columns: **metric** = ORF selection criterion (Kozak strength + downstream
EJC); **group** = NMD or Control comparators; **n** = isoforms;
**Median/Q25/Q75** = count of qualifying ORFs per transcript.

</details>

```{r sec2d-orf-landscape-tests}
for (var in c("n_k2_ejc", "n_k1plus_ejc", "n_any_ejc")) {
  wt <- wilcox.test(nmd_kozak[[var]], ctrl_kozak[[var]])
  cat(sprintf("  %s: NMD median %g vs Control %g (p = %g)\n",
      var, median(nmd_kozak[[var]]), median(ctrl_kozak[[var]]), wt$p.value))
}
```

NMD comparators have more NMD-susceptible ORFs at every Kozak strength level.

### Non-NMD Isoform Response in NMD-Harboring Genes

If the gene architecture differences above are functionally relevant, they
might also affect isoforms not classified as NMD targets. We compare the
logFC (SMG1i vs DMSO) of non-NMD isoforms from NMD-harboring genes versus
non-NMD genes, using the same
`r fmt(nrow(dom_summary %>% summarise(n = sum(n))))` genes from the junction
architecture analysis.

```{r sec2d-gene-continuum, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mashr DE files (logFC per isoform per cell type)
# Population: non-NMD isoforms, grouped by gene NMD status

de_dir <- "/Users/petecastaldi/claude_projects/nmd/isocall_dge/mashr"
# Match only per-CT DIE files; the directory also has mashr meta CSVs
# (lfsr, posterior_means, sharing, null_correlation) with different schemas.
de_files <- list.files(de_dir, pattern = "^nmd_mashr_die_.*\\.csv$",
                       full.names = TRUE)

logfc_per_ct <- lapply(de_files, function(f) {
  d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  data.frame(isoform_id = d$txid, logFC = d$logFC, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})
logfc_combined <- do.call(rbind, logfc_per_ct)
mean_logfc <- logfc_combined %>%
  group_by(isoform_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_logFC = mean(logFC, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Restrict to the same gene set as Step 1 (genes with dominant isoform in ORFik)
step1_genes <- unique(dom_features$gene_id[!is.na(dom_features$gene_type)])

non_nmd_logfc <- mean_logfc %>%
  filter(isoform_id %in% non_nmd_ids_all) %>%
  inner_join(gene_map, by = "isoform_id") %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% step1_genes) %>%
  mutate(gene_type = ifelse(gene_id %in% nmd_genes_all, "NMD-harboring gene", "Non-NMD gene"))

gene_logfc <- non_nmd_logfc %>%
  group_by(gene_id, gene_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_nonnmd_logfc = mean(mean_logFC, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

wt_gene <- wilcox.test(gene_logfc$mean_nonnmd_logfc[gene_logfc$gene_type == "NMD-harboring gene"],
                        gene_logfc$mean_nonnmd_logfc[gene_logfc$gene_type == "Non-NMD gene"])

fig_continuum <- ggplot(gene_logfc, aes(x = gene_type, y = mean_nonnmd_logfc, fill = gene_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD-harboring gene" = "#ef8a62", "Non-NMD gene" = "#67a9cf")) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = max(gene_logfc$mean_nonnmd_logfc, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.8,
           label = sprintf("p = %s", signif(wt_gene$p.value, 3)), size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Non-NMD Isoform logFC by Gene NMD Status",
       subtitle = sprintf("NMD-harboring: %s genes | Non-NMD: %s genes",
                          fmt(sum(gene_logfc$gene_type == "NMD-harboring gene")),
                          fmt(sum(gene_logfc$gene_type == "Non-NMD gene"))),
       x = NULL, y = "Mean logFC (SMG1i vs DMSO)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
save_fig(fig_continuum, "fig_sec2d_gene_continuum", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec2d-gene-continuum-table, echo=FALSE}
            `Median logFC` = round(median(mean_nonnmd_logfc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `Mean logFC` = round(mean(mean_nonnmd_logfc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
```

Non-NMD isoforms from NMD-harboring genes show a significantly higher logFC
than those from non-NMD genes (p = `r format_p(wt_gene$p.value)`). The
effect is small --- both groups are centered near zero --- but the direction
is consistent with low-level NMD sensitivity in genes that also harbor
NMD-classified isoforms. However, this observation alone does not
distinguish between direct NMD effects on these isoforms and indirect
transcriptional or post-transcriptional consequences of SMG1 inhibition.


# 6. Predictive Model: ORF Assumption Drives Attribution {#sec6-model}

Can we predict which isoforms trigger NMD from structural features alone?
We built a gradient-boosted tree model (XGBoost) using structural features
derived from two CDS annotation strategies, achieving holdout AUC =
`r round(mc$combined_model$auc_test, 3)`. Below we present the combined model,
then decompose it to understand the dependency structure of its features.

The two CDS strategies differ in how they define the reading frame for each
isoform:

- **TD2 CDS**: Each isoform's own TransDecoder2-predicted CDS boundaries.
  Features (downstream EJCs, 5'UTR, uORFs) computed from these boundaries.
- **Reference CDS**: The dominant non-NMD isoform's CDS used as the reading
  frame anchor for every isoform in the gene. The reference ATG is traced
  through each target isoform's transcript, and features are computed from
  the resulting CDS boundaries.

NMD status is defined empirically from the observed SMG1i response (mashr
posterior logFC and lfsr), not from structural features --- the model predicts
an experimental outcome from sequence-derived predictors.

**Statistical approach:** XGBoost gradient-boosted trees with 10-fold
cross-validation for early stopping on the training set. Holdout chromosomes
1, 3, 5, 7 are never used for feature selection or model tuning. TD2 and
combined models use the full population; reference-CDS models use the subset
with available reference ATG. XGBoost handles missing values natively, so
ref-CDS features are NA (not imputed) for isoforms lacking a reference ATG. AUC
comparisons are not confounded by population differences.

```{r sec3a-load-models}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Combined Prediction Model"
# Source: 05v_model_comparison.R → model_comparison.rds
#   Built from: 05l_unified_model.R (TD2 features),
#               05t_ref_cds_features.R (ref-CDS features),
#               05u_paralog_annotation.R (paralog leakage filtering)
# Model: XGBoost gradient-boosted trees with TreeSHAP
# Population: all classified coding isoforms with TD2 features (~60K);
#   ref-CDS features NA for ref_atg_lost isoforms (XGBoost handles natively)
# Train: non-holdout chromosomes
# Test: holdout chr 1,3,5,7 with high-similarity cross-split paralogs removed

# mc loaded in Section 0 data loading chunk

cat("Full population:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_complete), "isoforms\n")
cat("  NMD:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_nmd_train + mc$metadata$n_nmd_test), "\n")
cat("  Non-NMD:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_complete -
    mc$metadata$n_nmd_train - mc$metadata$n_nmd_test), "\n")
cat("  Ref-CDS available subset:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_ref_complete), "\n")
cat("Train:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_train), "| Test:", fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_final), "\n")
cat("Paralog genes removed from test:", mc$metadata$n_paralog_removed_genes,
    "(", fmt(mc$metadata$n_paralog_removed_isoforms), "isoforms)\n")

# unified and feat_labels loaded in Section 0 data loading chunk
```

## Model Features

Each feature is computed twice --- once from the TD2-predicted CDS and once
from the reference isoform's CDS traced through the target transcript. The
table below describes each feature and its CDS source.

```{r sec3a-feature-table}
feature_desc <- data.frame(
  Feature = c(
    "Downstream EJC count",
    "5\u2032UTR ATG density",
    "5\u2032UTR ATG count",
    "Strong Kozak ATG count",
    "Orphan ATG count",
    "Overlapping uORF count",
    "Longest uORF (nt)",
    "In-frame uORF count",
    "Out-of-frame uORF count",
    "5\u2032UTR ORF coverage",
    "5\u2032UTR stop density",
    "3\u2032UTR length (log bp)"
  ),
  Category = c(
    "Stop codon position",
    "Start codon context",
    "Start codon context",
    "Start codon context",
    "Start codon context",
    "Upstream ORF",
    "Upstream ORF",
    "Upstream ORF",
    "Upstream ORF",
    "Start codon context",
    "Start codon context",
    "3\u2032UTR"
  ),
  CDS_source = c(rep("Both", 12)),
  Description = c(
    "Number of exon-exon junctions downstream of the stop codon (truncated at 5).",
    "ATG codons per 100 bp of 5\u2032UTR.",
    "Total ATG codons in the 5\u2032UTR.",
    "5\u2032UTR ATGs matching strong Kozak consensus (-3 and +4).",
    "5\u2032UTR ATGs not associated with any predicted ORF.",
    "uORFs extending past the CDS start codon.",
    "Length of the longest 5\u2032UTR ORF (nt).",
    "uORFs in the same reading frame as the main CDS.",
    "uORFs in a different reading frame from the main CDS.",
    "Percentage of 5\u2032UTR spanned by predicted ORFs.",
    "Stop codons (all frames) per 100 bp of 5\u2032UTR.",
    "Log-transformed exonic bp from stop codon to 3\u2032 transcript end."
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

render_dt(feature_desc, caption = "Table: Model Feature Definitions")
```

Column definitions: **Feature** = display name; **Category** = biological
domain; **CDS_source** = both TD2 and reference CDS versions are computed
for each feature; **Description** = what the feature measures.

## Dataset Construction

```{r sec3a-dataset-table}
dataset_desc <- data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Training (full)", "Test (full)",
              "Training (ref-CDS)", "Test (ref-CDS)"),
  Chromosomes = c("2, 4, 6, 8\u201322, X", "1, 3, 5, 7",
                  "2, 4, 6, 8\u201322, X", "1, 3, 5, 7"),
  Population = c(
    "All classified coding isoforms",
    "All classified coding, paralog genes removed",
    "Ref-CDS available, complete features",
    "Ref-CDS available, complete features, paralog genes removed"
  ),
  N_isoforms = c(fmt(mc$metadata$n_train), fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_final),
                 fmt(mc$metadata$n_train_ref), fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_ref_final)),
  N_NMD = c(fmt(mc$metadata$n_nmd_train), fmt(mc$metadata$n_nmd_test),
            fmt(sum(mc$train$is_nmd[mc$train$ref_atg_available %in% TRUE &
              !is.na(mc$train$ref_downstream_ejc)])),
            fmt(sum(mc$test$is_nmd[mc$test$ref_atg_available %in% TRUE &
              !is.na(mc$test$ref_downstream_ejc)]))),
  Used_by = c("TD2 and combined models", "TD2 and combined models",
              "Ref-CDS models", "Ref-CDS models"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

render_dt(dataset_desc, caption = "Table: Train/Test Dataset Construction")
```

Column definitions: **Dataset** = partition name; **Chromosomes** = which
chromosomes contribute; **Population** = inclusion criteria; **N_isoforms**
= total isoforms; **N_NMD** = NMD-classified isoforms; **Used_by** = which
model sets use this population.

**Paralog removal:** Genes with a high-similarity expressed paralog
(protein identity \u2265 80%) on the opposite side of the train/test split are
removed from the test set only. This prevents data leakage from
structurally similar gene family members.
`r mc$metadata$n_paralog_removed_genes` genes
(`r fmt(mc$metadata$n_paralog_removed_isoforms)` isoforms) were removed,
representing
`r round(100 * mc$metadata$n_paralog_removed_isoforms / mc$metadata$n_test_before_paralog, 1)`%
of the holdout set.

**Population design:** TD2 and combined models use the **full population**
(`r fmt(mc$metadata$n_complete)` isoforms). Reference-CDS models use the
subset with available reference ATG (`r fmt(mc$metadata$n_ref_complete)`
isoforms). XGBoost handles missing ref-CDS features natively, so the
combined model includes all isoforms without imputation.


## The Combined Model

The XGBoost model receives all 24 features (12 TD2 + 12 reference CDS).
Feature importance is assessed via SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)
values, which decompose each prediction into per-feature contributions.

```{r sec3a-combined-coefficients}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$combined_model (XGBoost with all 24 features)
# mc$combined_shap_importance (mean |SHAP| per feature with CDS source tag)

cat(sprintf("Combined model test AUC: %.4f\n", mc$combined_model$auc_test))
cat(sprintf("  TD2 features: %d\n",
            sum(mc$combined_shap_importance$source == "TD2")))
cat(sprintf("  Ref-CDS features: %d\n",
            sum(mc$combined_shap_importance$source == "Ref-CDS")))

# Build display table from pre-computed SHAP importance
coef_display <- mc$combined_shap_importance %>%
  mutate(
    Feature = ifelse(feature %in% names(mc$feature_labels),
                     mc$feature_labels[feature], feature),
    `Mean |SHAP|` = round(mean_abs_shap, 4),
    Source = source
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(`Mean |SHAP|`)) %>%
  select(Feature, `Mean |SHAP|`, Source)

invisible(NULL)  # table rendered in collapsible block below
```

<details>
<summary>Click to view tabular data for combined model feature importance</summary>

```{r sec3a-combined-coef-table, echo=FALSE}
render_dt(coef_display,
          caption = "Table: Combined Model Feature Importance (TD2 + Ref-CDS)")
```

Column definitions: **Feature** = model variable (display name);
**Mean |SHAP|** = mean absolute SHAP value across the holdout test set
(higher = more important); **Source** = which CDS annotation produced this
feature (TD2 or Ref-CDS).

</details>

```{r sec3a-combined-barplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
coef_plot <- coef_display %>%
  mutate(
    Feature = factor(Feature, levels = rev(Feature))
  )

fig_combined_coefs <- ggplot(coef_plot,
    aes(x = `Mean |SHAP|`, y = Feature, fill = Source)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TD2" = "#67a9cf", "Ref-CDS" = "#ef8a62")) +
  labs(title = "Combined Model Feature Importance",
       subtitle = sprintf("XGBoost \u2014 mean |SHAP| across %s holdout isoforms",
                          fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_final)),
       x = "Mean |SHAP| (log-odds)", y = NULL, fill = "CDS source") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_combined_coefs, "fig_combined_feature_importance", width = 9, height = 7)
```

Both CDS sources contribute to the combined model. The two strongest
features are the downstream EJC counts from each CDS source, indicating
they capture partially non-overlapping PTC information. This makes
biological sense: reference CDS correctly identifies PTCs in isoforms where
TD2 chose the wrong reading frame, while TD2 provides PTC information for
isoforms where the reference ATG is lost.


## Decomposing the Combined Model

To understand the dependency structure of these 24 features, we decompose
the combined model into subsets stratified by CDS source and feature
category. All decomposition models use the same train/test split and
population as the combined model.

### By CDS Source

Restricting to the 11 TD2-only features yields holdout AUC =
`r round(mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test, 3)`. Restricting to the 11
reference-CDS-only features yields AUC =
`r round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test, 3)`. **Note that these AUCs are
computed on different populations:** TD2 features can be evaluated on
every coding isoform in the holdout test set
(N = `r fmt(length(mc$td2_models$step3$pred_test))`), but the reference-CDS
model is restricted to the `ref_atg_available` subset where the reference
ATG is exonic in the comparator (N = `r fmt(length(mc$ref_models$step3$pred_test))`).
Population selection alone changes apparent performance — the
reference-restricted subset is intrinsically easier to classify regardless
of feature source.

```{r sec3d-matched-population-auc}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$td2_models$step3$pred_test (TD2 predictions on full test set)
#   mc$ref_test (ref-CDS test set; subset of mc$test where ref ATG available)
#   mc$test (full TD2 test set)
# Method: re-evaluate TD2 model AUC on the subset of test isoforms that also
#   appear in the ref-CDS test set, so the comparison is apples-to-apples.

# Identify the ref-CDS test population: rows of mc$test where ref-CDS
# features are complete (ref_utr5_excluded == FALSE). This is the same
# population mc$ref_models$step3 was evaluated on (n=7,373).
matched_idx <- which(!is.na(mc$test$ref_utr5_excluded) &
                       mc$test$ref_utr5_excluded == FALSE)

td2_pred_matched <- mc$td2_models$step3$pred_test[matched_idx]
y_matched        <- mc$test$is_nmd[matched_idx]

td2_auc_matched <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(y_matched, td2_pred_matched,
                                                  quiet = TRUE)))

matched_pop_auc <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("Headline (different populations)",
                 "Matched population (ref-CDS subset)"),
  `TD2 AUC`     = c(round(mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test, 3),
                    round(td2_auc_matched, 3)),
  `Ref-CDS AUC` = c(round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test, 3),
                    round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test, 3)),
  Difference    = c(round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test -
                            mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test, 3),
                    round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test - td2_auc_matched, 3)),
  N             = c(sprintf("TD2: %s / Ref: %s",
                            fmt(length(mc$td2_models$step3$pred_test)),
                            fmt(length(mc$ref_models$step3$pred_test))),
                    sprintf("Both: %s", fmt(length(matched_idx)))),
  check.names = FALSE
)

render_dt(matched_pop_auc, caption = "TD2 vs Ref-CDS AUC on matched populations")
```

Column definitions: **Comparison** = headline (different populations) vs
matched (ref-CDS subset only); **TD2 AUC** = AUC of the 11-feature TD2
model on each population; **Ref-CDS AUC** = AUC of the 11-feature
reference-CDS model on the `ref_atg_available` subset; **Difference** =
Ref-CDS AUC − TD2 AUC; **N** = test isoforms.

On the **matched population** (the `ref_atg_available` subset where both
models can be evaluated), the AUC difference shrinks from
`r round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test - mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test, 3)`
to **`r round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test - td2_auc_matched, 3)`** — i.e., most
of the headline difference reflects population selection, not features.
This means the *discrimination* benefit of reference-CDS features is small.
The substantive benefit, demonstrated in the next subsection, is in
*attribution*: which features the model leans on for occult-PTC isoforms.

### By Feature Category: EJC Counts Alone

```{r sec3d-ejc-only-model}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$td2_models$step1 (TD2 EJC-only), mc$ref_models$step1 (Ref EJC-only)
# Pre-computed in 05v_model_comparison.R — no inline model fitting needed
# Purpose: demonstrate that EJC counts alone capture most of the signal

ejc_td2_auc <- mc$td2_models$step1$auc_test
ejc_ref_auc <- mc$ref_models$step1$auc_test

cat(sprintf("TD2 EJC-only (1 feature): Test AUC = %.4f\n", ejc_td2_auc))
cat(sprintf("Ref EJC-only (1 feature): Test AUC = %.4f\n", ejc_ref_auc))
```

The downstream EJC count alone achieves AUC =
`r round(ejc_ref_auc, 3)` (reference CDS) and
`r round(ejc_td2_auc, 3)` (TD2). The remaining 5'UTR, uORF, and 3'UTR
features contribute
+`r round(mc$combined_model$auc_test - ejc_ref_auc, 3)` additional AUC
beyond the reference EJC count. PTC identification is the dominant signal.

### The Compensatory Role of 5'UTR Features

The progressive models (not shown as separate figures) reveal a striking
asymmetry in how the two CDS sources use 5'UTR features. Starting from EJC
count alone, TD2-only achieves AUC =
`r round(mc$td2_models$step1$auc_test, 3)` and gains
+`r round(mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test - mc$td2_models$step1$auc_test, 3)`
when 5'UTR features are added (reaching
`r round(mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test, 3)`). Reference-CDS starts higher
(AUC = `r round(mc$ref_models$step1$auc_test, 3)`) and gains only
+`r round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test - mc$ref_models$step1$auc_test, 3)`
from the same feature categories (reaching
`r round(mc$ref_models$step3$auc_test, 3)`).

The interpretation: TD2's 5'UTR features compensate for incorrect PTC
identification. When TD2 selects the wrong reading frame, the resulting
5'UTR is structurally abnormal in ways that correlate with NMD status ---
the model learns these correlates as a proxy for the missed PTC. When
PTC identification is correct (reference CDS), the 5'UTR features are
largely redundant.

## ROC Comparison

The overlapping ROC compares the combined model against its three
decompositions: TD2-only features, reference-CDS-only features, and
EJC counts alone.

```{r sec3d-roc-comparison, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$td2_models, mc$ref_models, mc$combined_model (from
#   model_comparison.rds)
# All evaluated on paralog-free holdout test sets

roc_specs <- list(
  list(roc = mc$td2_models$step3$roc_test,
       name = "TD2 CDS model (11 features)", color = "#91bfdb"),
  list(roc = mc$ref_models$step3$roc_test,
       name = "Reference CDS model (11 features)", color = "#b2182b"),
  list(roc = mc$ref_models$step1$roc_test,
       name = "Ref EJC-only model (1 feature)", color = "#4393c3"),
  list(roc = mc$combined_model$roc_test,
       name = "Combined model (24 features)", color = "#1a1a1a")
)

roc_comp <- lapply(roc_specs, function(spec) {
  auc_val <- as.numeric(auc(spec$roc))
  data.frame(
    fpr = 1 - spec$roc$specificities,
    tpr = spec$roc$sensitivities,
    model = sprintf("%s (AUC = %.3f)", spec$name, auc_val),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
roc_comp_df <- do.call(rbind, roc_comp)
roc_comp_df$model <- factor(roc_comp_df$model, levels = unique(roc_comp_df$model))

roc_colors <- setNames(
  sapply(roc_specs, `[[`, "color"),
  levels(roc_comp_df$model)
)

fig_roc_comp <- ggplot(roc_comp_df, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, color = model)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = roc_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0.02, 0)) +
  labs(title = "NMD Prediction: Combined Model and Decompositions",
       subtitle = sprintf("Holdout test set (N = %s, paralog-free)",
                          fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_final)),
       x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate", color = "") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.62, 0.22),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "grey80"),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))
save_fig(fig_roc_comp, "fig_roc_td2_vs_ref", width = 8, height = 8)
```

```{r sec3d-auc-summary, echo=FALSE}
            "TD2 CDS model (11 features)",

            "Ref EJC-only model (1 feature)"),
  `Test AUC` = round(c(mc$combined_model$auc_test,
                        mc$td2_models$step3$auc_test,

  `Train AUC` = round(c(mc$combined_model$auc_train,
```

The combined model (AUC = `r round(mc$combined_model$auc_test, 3)`)
achieves the best holdout performance. The reference EJC-only model (AUC =
`r round(mc$ref_models$step1$auc_test, 3)`) demonstrates that PTC
identification from a single feature captures the majority of the signal.
The TD2 CDS model and reference CDS model perform comparably when given
all 11 features, but the reference CDS achieves near-equivalent performance
with its EJC count alone.

## NMD Response Magnitude

```{r sec3a-dose-response, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: meta_logfc (loaded in STAGE 5) — mashr posterior mean logFC averaged
# across the 4 paper-scope cell types (AT, DD, FB, MV). Dose-response evaluates
# whether the combined model's predicted NMD probability tracks the magnitude
# of SMG1i rescue measured by mashr.

# Score NMD isoforms with the combined model
nmd_test <- mc$test[mc$test$is_nmd == 1, ]
nmd_test$pred_combined <- mc$combined_model$pred_test[
  match(nmd_test$isoform_id,
        mc$test$isoform_id)]

nmd_dose <- nmd_test %>%
  inner_join(meta_logfc, by = c("isoform_id" = "txid"))

rho_combined <- cor(nmd_dose$pred_combined, nmd_dose$mean_logFC,
                     method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
p_combined <- cor.test(nmd_dose$pred_combined, nmd_dose$mean_logFC,
                        method = "spearman")$p.value

fig_dose <- ggplot(nmd_dose,
                   aes(x = pred_combined, y = mean_logFC)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8, color = "#1a1a1a") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1, color = "#1a1a1a") +
  labs(title = "Combined Model Score vs NMD Response Magnitude",
       subtitle = sprintf("Holdout NMD isoforms (n = %s) | Spearman rho = %.3f, p = %s",
                          fmt(nrow(nmd_dose)), rho_combined,
                          signif(p_combined, 3)),
       x = "Predicted NMD probability (combined model)",
       y = "Mean mashr posterior logFC (across 4 cell types)")
save_fig(fig_dose, "fig_dose_response_combined", width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r sec3d-dose-response-table, echo=FALSE}
  mutate(score_bin = cut(pred_combined, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                          include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(score_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Median logFC` = round(median(mean_logFC, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `Mean logFC` = round(mean(mean_logFC, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop")
render_dt(dose_summary, caption = "NMD Response by Combined Model Score Bin")
```

isoforms; **Median/Mean logFC** = SMG1i response within that score bin.

</details>

The combined model's predicted probability correlates with actual NMD
response magnitude (Spearman rho = `r round(rho_combined, 3)`,
p = `r format_p(p_combined)`), confirming that the structural features
capture the continuous nature of NMD --- isoforms with stronger structural
signals show greater SMG1i rescue.

## SHAP-Based Isoform Clustering

The combined model uses 24 features, but different isoforms may be classified
as NMD through different structural mechanisms. SHAP (SHapley Additive
exPlanations) values decompose each isoform's predicted log-odds into
per-feature contributions, revealing which features drive each prediction.
SHAP values are computed directly from the XGBoost model via TreeSHAP,
which provides exact Shapley values for tree-based models.

All SHAP analyses use the **holdout test set** (N =
`r fmt(mc$metadata$n_test_final)` isoforms on chromosomes 1, 3, 5, 7,
paralog-free) --- the same population used for model evaluation.

```{r sec3d-shap-compute}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$combined_model$shap_test (pre-computed TreeSHAP from 05v_model_comparison.R)
# mc$combined_model$shap_feature_values (raw feature matrix for beeswarm colors)
# Population: holdout test set (mc$test) — same as ROC evaluation

shap_nz <- mc$combined_model$shap_test
shap_feature_raw <- mc$combined_model$shap_feature_values

cat("SHAP matrix:", nrow(shap_nz), "isoforms x", ncol(shap_nz), "features\n")
```

```{r sec3d-shap-beeswarm, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: shap_nz (pre-computed SHAP values from sec3d-shap-compute)
# shap_feature_raw (raw feature values for beeswarm color scale)

feat_labels_shap <- mc$feature_labels
n_plot <- nrow(mc$test)

shap_long <- as.data.frame(shap_nz) %>%
  mutate(row_id = seq_len(n())) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-row_id, names_to = "feature", values_to = "shap_value")

# Rank-transform feature values for color scale (avoids scale domination)
rank_vals <- as.data.frame(shap_feature_raw)
for (col in names(rank_vals)) {
  non_na <- !is.na(rank_vals[[col]])
  rank_vals[[col]][non_na] <- rank(rank_vals[[col]][non_na]) /
    sum(non_na)
  rank_vals[[col]][!non_na] <- 0.5  # neutral color for NA
}
rank_long <- rank_vals %>%
  mutate(row_id = seq_len(n())) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-row_id, names_to = "feature", values_to = "feature_value")

shap_plot_df <- shap_long %>%
  left_join(rank_long, by = c("row_id", "feature")) %>%
  mutate(
    Feature = ifelse(feature %in% names(feat_labels_shap),
                      feat_labels_shap[feature], feature)
  )

feat_order <- shap_plot_df %>%
  group_by(Feature) %>%
  summarise(mean_abs_shap = mean(abs(shap_value)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mean_abs_shap) %>%
  pull(Feature)
shap_plot_df$Feature <- factor(shap_plot_df$Feature, levels = feat_order)

fig_shap_bee <- ggplot(shap_plot_df,
    aes(x = shap_value, y = Feature, color = feature_value)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.25, width = 0, alpha = 0.15, size = 0.25) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#b2182b",
                         midpoint = 0.5, name = "Feature value\n(rank-normalized)") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "SHAP Summary — Combined Model",
       subtitle = sprintf("Holdout test set (N = %s)", fmt(n_plot)),
       x = "SHAP value (log-odds)", y = NULL)
save_fig(fig_shap_bee, "fig_shap_beeswarm", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r sec3d-shap-importance-table, echo=FALSE}
  group_by(Feature) %>%
  summarise(`Mean |SHAP|` = round(mean(abs(shap_value)), 4),
            `Median SHAP` = round(median(shap_value), 4),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(`Mean |SHAP|`))
render_dt(shap_importance, caption = "SHAP Feature Importance (Holdout Test Set)")
```

Columns: **Feature** = model variable; **Mean |SHAP|** = mean absolute SHAP

</details>

Column definitions for the SHAP beeswarm: each dot is one holdout test set
isoform. The x-axis shows the SHAP contribution (positive = pushes
prediction toward NMD); color indicates the rank-normalized feature value
(red = high, blue = low). Features are ordered by mean absolute SHAP (most
important at top). Missing values (ref-CDS features for NMD PTC-, ref ATG
lost isoforms) are shown at the midpoint color.

## NMD-Only SHAP Clustering

To identify **structural subgroups within NMD isoforms**, we cluster the
SHAP profiles of holdout NMD isoforms only. This asks: among isoforms that
*are* NMD-sensitive, which features drive the prediction, and are there
mechanistically distinct subpopulations?

```{r sec3d-shap-nmd-only}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: shap_nz (SHAP values from sec3d-shap-compute, holdout test set)
# Population: NMD isoforms only (is_nmd == 1) from the holdout test set
# Clustering: k-means on non-zero SHAP features, optimal k by silhouette

library(cluster)

nmd_mask <- mc$test$is_nmd == 1
shap_nmd <- shap_nz[nmd_mask, , drop = FALSE]
cat("Holdout NMD isoforms for clustering:", nrow(shap_nmd), "\n")

set.seed(42)
sil_nmd <- sapply(2:8, function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(shap_nmd, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)
  mean(silhouette(km$cluster, dist(shap_nmd))[, 3])
})
best_k_nmd <- which.max(sil_nmd) + 1
cat("Silhouette scores (k=2..8):", round(sil_nmd, 3), "\n")
cat("Best k:", best_k_nmd, "\n")

km_nmd <- kmeans(shap_nmd, centers = best_k_nmd, nstart = 50, iter.max = 100)

nmd_subset <- mc$test[nmd_mask, ]
nmd_subset$nmd_cluster <- km_nmd$cluster
```

```{r sec3d-shap-nmd-cluster-summary}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: nmd_subset (holdout NMD isoforms with cluster assignments)
# Features: shap_nmd (SHAP matrix restricted to holdout NMD isoforms)

nmd_cluster_summary <- nmd_subset %>%
  mutate(pred_prob = mc$combined_model$pred_test[
    match(isoform_id, mc$test$isoform_id)]) %>%
  group_by(nmd_cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `Mean pred. prob.` = round(mean(pred_prob, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `TD2 dEJC > 0 (%)` = round(100 * mean(downstream_ejc > 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Ref dEJC > 0 (%)` = round(100 * mean(ref_downstream_ejc > 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Mean TD2 dEJC` = round(mean(downstream_ejc, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Mean Ref dEJC` = round(mean(ref_downstream_ejc, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(nmd_cluster)

shap_nmd_df <- as.data.frame(shap_nmd)
shap_nmd_df$nmd_cluster <- km_nmd$cluster

nmd_dominant <- shap_nmd_df %>%
  group_by(nmd_cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-nmd_cluster, names_to = "feature", values_to = "mean_shap") %>%
  group_by(nmd_cluster) %>%
  slice_max(abs(mean_shap), n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    `Dominant feature` = ifelse(feature %in% names(mc$feature_labels),
                                 mc$feature_labels[feature], feature),
    `Mean SHAP` = round(mean_shap, 3)
  ) %>%
  select(nmd_cluster, `Dominant feature`, `Mean SHAP`)

nmd_cluster_summary <- nmd_cluster_summary %>%
  left_join(nmd_dominant, by = "nmd_cluster")

invisible(NULL)  # table rendered in collapsible block below
```
