<summary>Click to view tabular data for NMD SHAP clusters</summary>

```{r sec3d-shap-nmd-cluster-table, echo=FALSE}
render_dt(nmd_cluster_summary, caption = "Table: SHAP Clusters — Holdout NMD Isoforms")
```

Column definitions: **nmd_cluster** = cluster ID; **N** = holdout NMD
isoforms in cluster; **Mean pred. prob.** = mean combined model predicted
probability; **TD2 dEJC > 0 (%)** = percentage with non-zero TD2 downstream
EJC count; **Ref dEJC > 0 (%)** = percentage with non-zero reference
downstream EJC count; **Mean TD2/Ref dEJC** = mean downstream EJC count from
each CDS source; **Dominant feature** = feature with largest absolute mean
SHAP; **Mean SHAP** = that feature's mean SHAP value.

</details>

```{r sec3d-shap-nmd-heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: shap_nmd_df (holdout NMD-only SHAP values with cluster assignments)

nmd_cluster_means <- shap_nmd_df %>%
  group_by(nmd_cluster) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop")

nmd_cm_long <- nmd_cluster_means %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-nmd_cluster, names_to = "feature", values_to = "mean_shap") %>%
  mutate(
    Feature = ifelse(feature %in% names(mc$feature_labels),
                      mc$feature_labels[feature], feature),
    Feature = factor(Feature, levels = rev(unique(Feature)))
  )

fig_nmd_heat <- ggplot(nmd_cm_long,
    aes(x = factor(nmd_cluster), y = Feature, fill = mean_shap)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                        midpoint = 0, name = "Mean SHAP\n(log-odds)") +
  labs(title = "SHAP Cluster Profiles — Holdout NMD Isoforms",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d clusters, %s holdout NMD isoforms",
                          best_k_nmd, fmt(nrow(shap_nmd))),
       x = "Cluster", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))
save_fig(fig_nmd_heat, "fig_shap_nmd_cluster_heatmap", width = 12, height = 7)
```

Each column is an NMD subgroup; each row a surviving model feature. The
clusters can be interpreted as mechanistically distinct NMD subpopulations:

- **Dual-PTC clusters** (high TD2 + Ref downstream EJC): Both CDS sources
  identify the PTC. These are structurally unambiguous NMD targets.
- **Ref-CDS-driven clusters** (high Ref EJC, low TD2 EJC): The reference
  reading frame reveals a PTC that TD2 missed by selecting the wrong ORF.
  These correspond to the reclassified PTC-negative isoforms from Section 4 (CDS Misprediction Problem).
- **5'UTR-driven clusters** (low EJC from both sources, elevated uORF/ATG
  features): Neither CDS source identifies a clear PTC. The model relies on
  translational regulation features --- these may represent uORF-mediated
  NMD or isoforms where the PTC mechanism is not captured by either CDS
  annotation.

## Attribution Dissociation in Occult-PTC Isoforms

A central methodological finding of this work is that **TD2 and Ref-CDS XGBoost
models achieve similar discrimination on occult-PTC isoforms but rely on
systematically different features**. The TD2 model classifies most occult-PTC
isoforms as NMD, but its predictions are driven by spurious 5'UTR/uORF features
that are mechanistic shadows of the reference CDS that TD2 demoted to a
"5'UTR" by jumping to a downstream ATG. The Ref-CDS model attributes the same
isoforms to the actual PTC. We refer to this as the *attribution dissociation*:
both models can call NMD correctly, but only one identifies the correct cause.

### Per-Family SHAP Decomposition

```{r sec3d-attribution-discordance}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$combined_model$shap_test (TreeSHAP from XGBoost on holdout test)
#   mc$test (holdout test isoforms, 1:1 with shap_test rows)
#   ref_atg_analysis.rds c2 table — categorizes NMD pairs by ref-ATG fate
# Population: holdout test NMD isoforms, split into occult-PTC vs non-occult NMD
# Methods: identify occult-PTC = NMD pair where comparator was originally PTC-
#   per TD2 but reclassified as effectively_ptc by ref-ATG analysis. Compare
#   per-isoform |SHAP| fraction from Ref-CDS feature family vs TD2 family.

ra <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "ref_atg_analysis.rds"))
occult_ids <- ra$c2$comparator_isoform_id[
  ra$c2$category == "effectively_ptc" & !ra$c2$original_ptc]

shap_combined <- mc$combined_model$shap_test
test_df <- mc$test
nmd_test_idx <- which(test_df$is_nmd == 1)
occult_test_idx <- nmd_test_idx[test_df$isoform_id[nmd_test_idx] %in% occult_ids]
nonoccult_test_idx <- setdiff(nmd_test_idx, occult_test_idx)

# Partition combined-model features by family (Ref-CDS columns prefixed "ref_")
all_feat <- colnames(shap_combined)
ref_feat <- grep("^ref_", all_feat, value = TRUE)
td2_feat <- setdiff(all_feat, ref_feat)

# Per-isoform fraction of |SHAP| from Ref-CDS family
abs_shap <- abs(shap_combined)
row_sum   <- rowSums(abs_shap)
ref_frac  <- rowSums(abs_shap[, ref_feat, drop = FALSE]) / pmax(row_sum, 1e-12)

attribution_summary <- data.frame(
  Subset = c("Occult-PTC NMD", "Non-occult NMD"),
  N      = c(length(occult_test_idx), length(nonoccult_test_idx)),
  `Mean Ref-CDS |SHAP| fraction` = c(
    round(mean(ref_frac[occult_test_idx]), 3),
    round(mean(ref_frac[nonoccult_test_idx]), 3)
  ),
  `Median Ref-CDS |SHAP| fraction` = c(
    round(median(ref_frac[occult_test_idx]), 3),
    round(median(ref_frac[nonoccult_test_idx]), 3)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
wt_attr <- wilcox.test(ref_frac[occult_test_idx], ref_frac[nonoccult_test_idx])

render_dt(attribution_summary,
  caption = "Per-isoform |SHAP| family fractions, combined model")
```

Column definitions: **Subset** = NMD subgroup; **N** = isoforms in holdout test set;
**Mean / Median Ref-CDS |SHAP| fraction** = per-isoform sum of |SHAP| from
Ref-CDS-prefixed features divided by total |SHAP|, averaged across isoforms.

Occult-PTC isoforms attribute **`r round(100 * attribution_summary[1, 3], 1)`%** of
combined-model |SHAP| to Ref-CDS features, vs only
**`r round(100 * attribution_summary[2, 3], 1)`%** for non-occult NMD
(Wilcoxon p = `r format_p(wt_attr$p.value)`). The Ref-CDS family carries
~`r round((attribution_summary[1, 3] / attribution_summary[2, 3] - 1) * 100, 0)`%
more relative attribution in occult-PTC than in standard NMD, even though
both subpopulations are correctly classified as NMD.

### Top Feature Attributions per Subset

```{r sec3d-top-features-by-subset}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: mc$td2_models$step4$shap_test, mc$ref_models$step4$shap_test,
#   mc$combined_model$shap_test — TreeSHAP from each XGBoost variant
# Population: occult-PTC isoforms in each model's test set
# Method: mean |SHAP| per feature within occult-PTC subset, ranked

# TD2 model SHAP — same test set as combined
td2_shap <- mc$td2_models$step4$shap_test
td2_test_df <- mc$test
td2_occult_idx <- which(td2_test_df$is_nmd == 1 &
                          td2_test_df$isoform_id %in% occult_ids)
td2_nonoccult_idx <- setdiff(which(td2_test_df$is_nmd == 1), td2_occult_idx)

# Ref-CDS model SHAP — restricted test set (ref-CDS features complete:
# ref_utr5_excluded == FALSE in mc$test). Row order is preserved between
# mc$ref_models$step4$shap_test and mc$test[ref_utr5_excluded == FALSE, ].
ref_shap <- mc$ref_models$step4$shap_test
ref_filter_idx <- which(!is.na(mc$test$ref_utr5_excluded) &
                          mc$test$ref_utr5_excluded == FALSE)
ref_test_df <- mc$test[ref_filter_idx, ]
ref_occult_idx <- which(ref_test_df$is_nmd == 1 &
                          ref_test_df$isoform_id %in% occult_ids)
ref_nonoccult_idx <- setdiff(which(ref_test_df$is_nmd == 1), ref_occult_idx)

mean_abs <- function(mat, idx) colMeans(abs(mat[idx, , drop = FALSE]))

td2_occult_top <- sort(mean_abs(td2_shap, td2_occult_idx), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6]
ref_occult_top <- sort(mean_abs(ref_shap, ref_occult_idx), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6]
td2_nonoccult_top <- mean_abs(td2_shap, td2_nonoccult_idx)[names(td2_occult_top)]
ref_nonoccult_top <- mean_abs(ref_shap, ref_nonoccult_idx)[names(ref_occult_top)]

td2_table <- data.frame(
  Feature = names(td2_occult_top),
  `Mean |SHAP| occult` = round(td2_occult_top, 3),
  `Mean |SHAP| non-occult` = round(td2_nonoccult_top, 3),
  Ratio = round(td2_occult_top / pmax(td2_nonoccult_top, 1e-6), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
ref_table <- data.frame(
  Feature = names(ref_occult_top),
  `Mean |SHAP| occult` = round(ref_occult_top, 3),
  `Mean |SHAP| non-occult` = round(ref_nonoccult_top, 3),
  Ratio = round(ref_occult_top / pmax(ref_nonoccult_top, 1e-6), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)

render_dt(td2_table,
  caption = "TD2-only model: top features for occult-PTC isoforms")
render_dt(ref_table,
  caption = "Ref-CDS-only model: top features for occult-PTC isoforms")
```

Column definitions (both tables): **Feature** = XGBoost feature name; **Mean
|SHAP| occult** / **non-occult** = average absolute SHAP value across occult-PTC
or non-occult NMD isoforms; **Ratio** = mean |SHAP| (occult) / mean |SHAP|
(non-occult). A ratio above 1 means the feature carries more attribution weight
for occult-PTC than for standard NMD.

The TD2 model's top occult-PTC feature is `uorf_longest_nt` — the median
length is ~432 nt in occult-PTC vs ~183 nt in non-occult NMD. A 432-nt
"uORF" is biologically implausible; this signal is the **reference CDS that
TD2 demoted** when it skipped the early PTC and chose a downstream ATG.
Meanwhile the TD2 model's `downstream_ejc` feature (TD2's notion of PTC
status) carries near-zero |SHAP| for occult-PTC because TD2's chosen ORF
contains no downstream EJC — the early PTC has been absorbed into TD2's
"5'UTR".

The Ref-CDS model attributes the same isoforms primarily to
`ref_downstream_ejc` (the genuine PTC signal in the reference reading
frame), with mean |SHAP| ~2× higher than for non-occult NMD.

### Independent Corroboration: Three-Way ORF Caller Agreement

If TD2's downstream-ATG choice is genuinely incorrect for occult-PTC isoforms,
a second, independently-motivated ORF caller should also disagree with TD2
and converge on the reference-ATG. We test this using **ORFik**, which scores
all ATGs by their Kozak context and selects the highest-scoring ORF without
any splicing-context information. ORFik's choices come from a different
prior (translation initiation strength) than reference-ATG tracing (splicing
preserves the start), so agreement between the two would be strong evidence
that *both* are recovering the biologically correct ORF.

```{r sec3d-orfik-agreement}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: orfik_scan.rds$orf_features (Isopair-derived per-ORF table)
#   ref_atg_analysis.rds c2 (ref-ATG categorization)
#   cds.rds (TD2 CDS coordinates)
#   structures.rds (exon coordinates for genomic-to-transcript mapping)
# Method: for each comparator isoform, compute three candidate ATG
#   tx-positions (TD2 CDS, ref-ATG, ORFik top-Kozak) and tabulate agreement
#   within ±2 nt tolerance. Restrict to NMD pairs by category.

orfik <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "orfik_scan.rds"))
orfik_features <- orfik$orf_features

# ORFik top-Kozak ATG per isoform (tiebreak by smallest tx position)
orfik_top <- orfik_features %>%
  group_by(isoform_id) %>%
  arrange(desc(kozak_score), orf_start) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(isoform_id,
         orfik_atg_tx     = orf_start,
         orfik_kozak      = kozak_score,
         orfik_n_dejc     = n_downstream_ejc,
         orfik_has_dejc   = has_downstream_ejc)

# TD2 ATG genomic → tx position per comparator
struct_lookup <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(structures)), function(i) {
    list(starts = structures$exon_starts[[i]],
         ends   = structures$exon_ends[[i]],
         strand = structures$strand[i])
  }), structures$isoform_id)

td2_atg_genomic_for <- function(iso_id) {
  cd <- cds[match(iso_id, cds$isoform_id), ]
  if (is.na(cd$strand)) return(NA_integer_)
  ifelse(cd$strand == "+", cd$cds_start, cd$cds_stop)
}

g2t_safe <- function(genomic, iso_id) {
  s <- struct_lookup[[iso_id]]
  if (is.null(s) || is.na(genomic)) return(NA_integer_)
  Isopair::genomicToTranscript(genomic, s$starts, s$ends, s$strand)
}

# Build per-pair table of three ATG tx positions (NMD pairs only)
ra_c2 <- ra$c2
ra_c2$td2_atg_tx <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ra_c2)), function(i) {
  cid <- ra_c2$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  g2t_safe(td2_atg_genomic_for(cid), cid)
}, numeric(1))
ra_c2$ref_atg_tx <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ra_c2)), function(i) {
  cid <- ra_c2$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  g2t_safe(ra_c2$ref_atg_genomic[i], cid)
}, numeric(1))
ra_c2 <- merge(ra_c2, orfik_top,
               by.x = "comparator_isoform_id", by.y = "isoform_id",
               all.x = TRUE)

# Subset definitions for the agreement table
ra_c2$subset <- dplyr::case_when(
  ra_c2$category == "effectively_ptc" & !ra_c2$original_ptc ~ "Occult-PTC",
  ra_c2$original_ptc ~ "Genuinely PTC+",
  ra_c2$category == "no_downstream_ejc" ~ "PTC-, no_downstream_ejc",
  ra_c2$category == "truncated_no_ejc"  ~ "PTC-, truncated_no_ejc",
  ra_c2$category == "ref_atg_lost"      ~ "Ref-ATG lost",
  TRUE ~ "Other"
)

resolvable <- !is.na(ra_c2$td2_atg_tx) & !is.na(ra_c2$ref_atg_tx) &
               !is.na(ra_c2$orfik_atg_tx)
TOL <- 2L
ra_c2$agree_orfik_td2 <- resolvable &
  abs(ra_c2$orfik_atg_tx - ra_c2$td2_atg_tx) <= TOL
ra_c2$agree_orfik_ref <- resolvable &
  abs(ra_c2$orfik_atg_tx - ra_c2$ref_atg_tx) <= TOL
ra_c2$agree_td2_ref   <- resolvable &
  abs(ra_c2$td2_atg_tx - ra_c2$ref_atg_tx) <= TOL

ra_c2$bucket <- dplyr::case_when(
  !resolvable                                   ~ "Unresolvable",
  ra_c2$agree_orfik_td2 & ra_c2$agree_orfik_ref ~ "All three agree",
  ra_c2$agree_orfik_td2                         ~ "ORFik = TD2 only",
  ra_c2$agree_orfik_ref                         ~ "ORFik = ref-ATG only",
  TRUE                                          ~ "ORFik picks third ATG"
)

agreement_table <- ra_c2 %>%
  filter(subset != "Other", subset != "Ref-ATG lost") %>%
  group_by(subset) %>%
  summarise(
    N_resolvable = sum(bucket != "Unresolvable"),
    `ORFik = TD2 only`     = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
        sum(bucket == "ORFik = TD2 only"),
        100 * sum(bucket == "ORFik = TD2 only") / pmax(sum(bucket != "Unresolvable"), 1)),
    `ORFik = ref-ATG only` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
        sum(bucket == "ORFik = ref-ATG only"),
        100 * sum(bucket == "ORFik = ref-ATG only") / pmax(sum(bucket != "Unresolvable"), 1)),
    `All three agree`      = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
        sum(bucket == "All three agree"),
        100 * sum(bucket == "All three agree") / pmax(sum(bucket != "Unresolvable"), 1)),
    `ORFik picks third ATG` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)",
        sum(bucket == "ORFik picks third ATG"),
        100 * sum(bucket == "ORFik picks third ATG") / pmax(sum(bucket != "Unresolvable"), 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

render_dt(agreement_table,
  caption = "Three-way ORF caller agreement (ORFik vs TD2 vs ref-ATG, ±2 nt tolerance)")

# Headline numbers for prose
occult_row <- ra_c2[ra_c2$subset == "Occult-PTC", ]
n_occult_resolvable <- sum(!is.na(occult_row$td2_atg_tx) &
                            !is.na(occult_row$ref_atg_tx) &
                            !is.na(occult_row$orfik_atg_tx))
n_occult_orfik_ref <- sum(occult_row$bucket == "ORFik = ref-ATG only")
n_occult_orfik_td2 <- sum(occult_row$bucket == "ORFik = TD2 only")
pct_orfik_ref_occult <- round(100 * n_occult_orfik_ref / n_occult_resolvable, 1)
pct_orfik_td2_occult <- round(100 * n_occult_orfik_td2 / n_occult_resolvable, 1)

# Of occult-PTC pairs where ORFik agrees with ref-ATG, what fraction are PTC-bearing per ORFik?
n_orfik_ref_with_dejc <- sum(occult_row$bucket == "ORFik = ref-ATG only" &
                              occult_row$orfik_has_dejc, na.rm = TRUE)
pct_orfik_ref_ptc <- round(100 * n_orfik_ref_with_dejc /
                            pmax(n_occult_orfik_ref, 1), 1)
```

Column definitions: **Subset** = NMD pair category (occult-PTC, genuinely
PTC+, etc.); **N_resolvable** = pairs where all three ATG positions could be
resolved on the comparator transcript; **ORFik = TD2/ref-ATG only** =
pairs where ORFik's top-Kozak ATG matches one caller exclusively (within
±2 nt); **All three agree** = TD2, ref-ATG, and ORFik converge on the
same position; **ORFik picks third ATG** = ORFik selects an ATG that
matches neither.

For occult-PTC isoforms (where TD2 and ref-ATG disagree by construction),
ORFik agrees with ref-ATG **`r pct_orfik_ref_occult`%** of the time and
with TD2 only **`r pct_orfik_td2_occult`%** —
ORFik corroborates ref-ATG ~`r round(pct_orfik_ref_occult / pmax(pct_orfik_td2_occult, 0.1), 0)`×
more often than TD2. In genuinely-PTC+ pairs where TD2 and ref-ATG agree
by construction, ORFik aligns with both at similar rates (no preference),
confirming that ORFik's bias toward ref-ATG is specific to occult-PTC.

Importantly, of the `r n_occult_orfik_ref` occult-PTC pairs where ORFik
agrees with ref-ATG, **`r pct_orfik_ref_ptc`% of those ORFik-derived ORFs
have a downstream exon-exon junction** — i.e., they are PTC-bearing per
ORFik's own classification. Two independent ORF callers, motivated by
unrelated priors (translation initiation strength vs splicing context),
converge on the same answer where TD2 fails: an early PTC.

(Caveat: the ORFik scan in this run uses an integer-binned Kozak score
0–2; ~57% of occult-PTC pairs have ORFik picking a third ATG due to
tied-strong-Kozak alternatives broken by smallest-position tiebreaker.
Switching to the continuous PWM Kozak score (`scoreKozakPWM()`) should
recover most of those cases. The exclusive `ORFik = ref-ATG` count is
therefore a lower bound on agreement.)

## Structural Features vs Sequence: The Remaining Gap

The combined structural model achieves holdout AUC =
`r round(mc$combined_model$auc_test, 3)`, demonstrating that isoform
architecture --- primarily PTC identification from two CDS sources ---
captures the majority of NMD sensitivity variation. However, a preliminary
CNN model trained on raw transcript sequences alone achieves AUC ~0.73,
and the structural model itself plateaus at ~0.93. The
`r round(1 - mc$combined_model$auc_test, 2)` residual may reflect:

- **Sequence-level NMD determinants** not captured by structural features
  (e.g., specific cis-regulatory elements, RNA secondary structure)
- **Long 3'UTR NMD** where distance between the stop codon and the poly(A)
  tail, rather than EJC position, triggers degradation
- **Stochastic ORF selection** where ribosome scanning dynamics depend on
  sequence context beyond Kozak consensus

Whether sequence-based models can close or exceed the structural model's
performance --- particularly for the PTC-absent NMD subpopulation --- is an
active question for the next phase of this analysis.

# 7. NMD Mechanism Summary {#sec7-accounting}

```{r sec3-summary-figure, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Methods: METHODS.md § "Cumulative NMD Mechanism Attribution"
# Source: coding_pairs_c2 (Section 4), ref_atg_analysis.rds (Section 4 occult-PTC subsection),
#   frame walk (fw_c2_allsamples.rds), attribute_ptc_events (analysis_functions.R)
# Every coding gene-matched NMD pair is classified into one mutually exclusive
# category. PTC+ pairs use the annotated CDS; PTC- pairs use reference-ATG tracing.

# --- PTC+ breakdown ---
ptc_pos_pairs <- coding_pairs_c2[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc, ]
cds_pos_acct <- cds %>%
  filter(coding_status == "coding") %>%
  transmute(isoform_id, stop_3prime = ifelse(strand == "+", cds_stop, cds_start))

ptc_pos_pairs$ref_stop <- cds_pos_acct$stop_3prime[
  match(ptc_pos_pairs$reference_isoform_id, cds_pos_acct$isoform_id)]
ptc_pos_pairs$comp_stop <- cds_pos_acct$stop_3prime[
  match(ptc_pos_pairs$comparator_isoform_id, cds_pos_acct$isoform_id)]
ptc_pos_pairs$same_stop <- ptc_pos_pairs$ref_stop == ptc_pos_pairs$comp_stop

fw_data <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "fw_c2_allsamples.rds"))
diff_stop_pairs <- ptc_pos_pairs[!ptc_pos_pairs$same_stop, ]
diff_keys <- paste(diff_stop_pairs$reference_isoform_id,
                   diff_stop_pairs$comparator_isoform_id)
fw_keys <- paste(fw_data$events$reference_isoform_id,
                 fw_data$events$comparator_isoform_id)

diff_stop_pairs$has_frameshift <- sapply(diff_keys, function(k) {
  evts <- fw_data$events[fw_keys == k, ]
  any(evts$is_frameshift, na.rm = TRUE)
})

n_ptcplus_fs <- sum(diff_stop_pairs$has_frameshift)
n_ptcplus_ifs <- sum(!diff_stop_pairs$has_frameshift)
n_ptcplus_3utr <- sum(ptc_pos_pairs$same_stop)

# --- Reclassified PTC- breakdown ---
reclass <- c2_ref[c2_ref$category == "effectively_ptc" & !c2_ref$original_ptc, ]
n_reclass_fs <- sum(reclass$attr_mechanism == "Frameshift", na.rm = TRUE)
n_reclass_ifs <- sum(reclass$attr_mechanism == "In-frame stop", na.rm = TRUE)
n_reclass_3utr <- sum(reclass$attr_mechanism == "3'UTR splice", na.rm = TRUE)

# --- TD2 reclassified PTC breakdown ---
td2_reclass_pairs <- ptc_neg_ref[td2_reclass_mask, ]

n_total <- nrow(coding_pairs_c2)

# --- Build waterfall data using canonical subgroups ---
acct <- data.frame(
  category = c("PTC+: Frameshift", "PTC+: In-frame stop", "PTC+: 3'UTR splice",
                "Reclassified (ref-ATG): Frameshift", "Reclassified (ref-ATG): In-frame stop",
                "Reclassified (ref-ATG): 3'UTR splice",
                "Reclassified (TD2 fallback)",
                "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
                "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"),
  n = c(n_ptcplus_fs, n_ptcplus_ifs, n_ptcplus_3utr,
        n_reclass_fs, n_reclass_ifs, n_reclass_3utr,
        n_td2_reclass,
        n_subgroup_retained,
        n_subgroup_lost),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
acct$pct <- round(100 * acct$n / n_total, 1)
acct$group <- c(rep("NMD PTC+ (annotated CDS)", 3),
                rep("NMD PTC+ (ref-ATG reclassified)", 3),
                "NMD PTC+ (TD2 reclassified)",
                "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained",
                "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost")

acct$group <- factor(acct$group,
  levels = c("NMD PTC+ (annotated CDS)", "NMD PTC+ (ref-ATG reclassified)",
             "NMD PTC+ (TD2 reclassified)",
             "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained", "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost"))
acct <- acct[order(acct$group, -acct$n), ]
acct$category <- factor(acct$category, levels = rev(acct$category))

group_colors <- c("NMD PTC+ (annotated CDS)" = "#c7e9c0",
                   "NMD PTC+ (ref-ATG reclassified)" = "#fdd0a2",
                   "NMD PTC+ (TD2 reclassified)" = "#b2df8a",
                   "NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained" = "#fdd49e",
                   "NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost" = "#fdbb84")

fig_acct <- ggplot(acct, aes(x = category, y = n, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s (%s%%)", fmt(n), pct)),
            hjust = -0.05, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(title = "NMD Mechanism Accounting: All Coding Pairs",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s coding gene-matched NMD pairs | NMD PTC+: %s (%.1f%%) | PTC-negative: %s (%.1f%%)",
                          fmt(n_total), fmt(n_ptcplus_total),
                          100 * n_ptcplus_total / n_total,
                          fmt(n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost),
                          100 * (n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost) / n_total),
       x = NULL, y = "Number of pairs", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
save_fig(fig_acct, "fig_sec3_mechanism_accounting", width = 10, height = 6)

# Verify sum
stopifnot(sum(acct$n) == n_total)  # accounting must be exhaustive
```

<details>
<summary>Click to view tabular data for mechanism accounting</summary>

```{r sec3-mechanism-table, echo=FALSE}
acct_display <- acct %>%
  select(Category = category, Group = group, n, `%` = pct)
render_dt(acct_display, caption = "NMD Mechanism Accounting")
```

Columns: **Category** = NMD mechanism category; **Group** = attribution
source; **n** = coding NMD pairs; **%** = percentage of all coding NMD pairs.

</details>

Every coding NMD pair is accounted for. **NMD PTC+** --- detected from the
annotated CDS, ref-ATG tracing, or TD2 CDS fallback --- accounts for
`r round(100 * n_ptcplus_total / n_total, 1)`% of pairs. The dominant
mechanism is **frameshift-causing splice events (primarily exon skipping)
that create premature stop codons with downstream EJCs.** The original
PTC+/PTC- distinction largely reflects which ORF the CDS prediction algorithm
selects, not distinct biological mechanisms.

The remaining `r round(100 * (n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost) / n_total, 1)`%
(`r fmt(n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost)` pairs) are PTC-negative by all
available reading frame definitions. They divide into two canonical subgroups:
**NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained** (`r fmt(n_subgroup_retained)` pairs) and
**NMD PTC-, ref ATG lost** (`r fmt(n_subgroup_lost)` pairs). Both show
intermediate NMD response and long 5'UTRs enriched for uORFs, consistent
with non-classical NMD mechanisms. This PTC-negative population represents
an important target for future mechanistic investigation.

# 8. Cross-Cell-Type Summary {#sec8-cross-ct}

```{r sec6-summary-table}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles and cached analyses across all cell types
# Each row computed via helper functions that access set_results[[key]]:
#   - Pair counts: nrow(gene-matched profiles)
#   - PTC rates: compute_ptc_rates_row() — coding pairs from gene-matched profiles + ptc.rds
#   - Divergence: compute_divergence_row() — from cached quantifyPairDivergence()
#   - Productive frameshifts: from pf_data precompute (all_samples only)
# All helpers operate on gene-matched data (profiles_list was matched in STAGE 2)

summary_rows <- lapply(c("all_samples", main_cts), function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)

  # NMD and Control pair counts
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  n_nmd  <- if (c2_key %in% names(set_results)) nrow(set_results[[c2_key]]$profiles) else NA
  n_ctrl <- if (c4_key %in% names(set_results)) nrow(set_results[[c4_key]]$profiles) else NA

  # PTC rates
  ptc_row <- compute_ptc_rates_row(ct)
  ptc_rate_nmd  <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$NMD_comp_ptc_pct else NA
  ptc_rate_ctrl <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct else NA
  ptc_or        <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$fisher_OR else NA

  # PTC-neg %
  ptc_neg_pct <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) round(100 - ptc_row$NMD_comp_ptc_pct, 1) else NA

  # Median pct_shared for C4
  div_row <- compute_divergence_row(ct)
  med_shared <- if (!is.null(div_row)) div_row$Ctrl_median_pct_shared else NA

  # Productive frameshifts (only available for all_samples; pf_data may be NULL)
  n_pf <- if (ct == "all_samples" && !is.null(pf_data))
            nrow(pf_data$characterization) else NA

  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    N_NMD_pairs = n_nmd,
    N_Ctrl_pairs = n_ctrl,
    PTC_rate_NMD_pct = ptc_rate_nmd,
    PTC_rate_Ctrl_pct = ptc_rate_ctrl,
    PTC_OR = ptc_or,
    PTC_neg_pct = ptc_neg_pct,
    Median_pct_shared_C4 = med_shared,
    N_productive_FS = n_pf)
})

summary_table <- do.call(rbind, summary_rows)
render_dt(summary_table, caption = "Table 11: Cross-Cell-Type Summary")
write.csv(summary_table, file.path(table_dir, "table11_cross_ct_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **cell_type** = sample set; **N_NMD/N_Ctrl_pairs** = gene-matched pair
counts; **PTC_rate_NMD/Ctrl_pct** = PTC rate among coding comparators;
**PTC_OR** = Fisher OR for PTC enrichment; **PTC_neg_pct** = percentage of
coding NMD comparators without PTC; **Median_pct_shared_C4** = median exonic
sequence shared in Control pairs (from `quantifyPairDivergence()`);
**N_productive_FS** = productive frameshifts (all_samples only).

The PTC enrichment OR is consistently high across all cell types
(`r paste(sprintf("%.1f", summary_table$PTC_OR[!is.na(summary_table$PTC_OR)]), collapse = ", ")`),
confirming that the PTC → NMD association is not driven by a single cell type.
PTC rates among NMD comparators range from
`r round(min(summary_table$PTC_rate_NMD_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`% to
`r round(max(summary_table$PTC_rate_NMD_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`% — the
variation reflects cell-type differences in which genes express NMD isoforms,
not in the underlying NMD mechanism. Control PTC rates are uniformly low
(`r round(min(summary_table$PTC_rate_Ctrl_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`–`r round(max(summary_table$PTC_rate_Ctrl_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`%),
as expected for non-NMD isoform pairs.

# Summary

This report characterized the structural mechanisms underlying NMD
sensitivity across `r fmt(nrow(coding_pairs_c2))` coding gene-matched
isoform pairs from long-read RNA-seq of lung cell lines treated with the
SMG1 inhibitor.

**PTC-mediated NMD dominates.** Premature termination codons with downstream
exon-exon junctions account for
`r round(100 * n_ptcplus_total / n_total_coding, 1)`% of NMD pairs —
`r round(100 * n_ptc_pos / n_total_coding, 1)`% from the annotated CDS,
`r round(100 * n_refatg_reclass / n_total_coding, 1)`% revealed by tracing
the reference isoform's ATG through the NMD comparator, and
`r round(100 * n_td2_reclass / n_total_coding, 1)`% reclassified via the
TD2 CDS fallback. The dominant mechanism is frameshift-causing exon skipping.

**CDS prediction obscures the true PTC rate.** TransDecoder2 selects the
longest high-scoring ORF. When a frameshift truncates the reference reading
frame, TD2 selects a longer alternative whose stop falls in the last exon,
making the isoform appear PTC-negative. Reference-ATG tracing recovers these
hidden PTCs. The reference ATGs have strong Kozak context
(`r round(100 * mean(kozak_results$kozak_class == "Strong", na.rm = TRUE), 1)`%
strong), and `r round(100 * n_ref_enst / nrow(eff_ptc), 1)`% come from GENCODE-annotated isoforms.

**NMD susceptibility has a gene-level component.** Genes that produce NMD
isoforms have more exon-exon junctions and a higher fraction of
NMD-susceptible ORFs than non-NMD genes. This structural property creates a
baseline NMD susceptibility that affects all isoforms of the gene.

**`r round(100 * (n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost) / n_total_coding, 1)`%
of NMD pairs are PTC-negative.** These `r fmt(n_subgroup_retained + n_subgroup_lost)`
pairs fall into two canonical subgroups: `r fmt(n_subgroup_retained)` retain
the reference ATG but lack downstream EJCs (NMD PTC-, ref ATG retained), and
`r fmt(n_subgroup_lost)` lost the reference ATG entirely (NMD PTC-, ref ATG
lost). Both groups show intermediate NMD response and long 5'UTRs enriched
for uORFs, consistent with non-classical NMD mechanisms. Their precise NMD
trigger remains an open question.
